summary_zh: 密西西比州民主党人指出特朗普做出的承诺：降低价格，停止无休止的战争，并在最近成为第一个密西西比州民主党人后释放爱泼斯坦的文件
body_en: Mississippi Democrat points to commitments Trump made: lower prices, halt endless wars and release Epstein files

After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Donald Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024.

Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.

But prices for fuel and other goods soared as Trump and Israel started war in Iran in February, a conflict which has dragged on for months – and critics have said many of the so-called Epstein files have been excluded from allegedly incomplete disclosures by the president’s administration.
Voters “elected me to make sure he follows through on the commitments he made in 2024,” Colom said. “Well, I want to work … to actually accomplish that.”

Colom also said that he intended to support efforts to pass legislation restricting stock trading by members of Congress, saying it was important for Americans to know lawmakers at the US Capitol in Washington DC “aren’t making money instead of looking out for them”.
“We [have] got to look out for our families – not DC families,” Colom said.
In a separate interview with NBC News’s Kristen Welker on Sunday, Colom added : “I’m not here to look out for the billionaires. I’m here to look out for working people.”

Those remarks from Colom came after he unseated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith during the 3 November midterm elections to become the first Black US senator from Mississippi since 1875 – during the Reconstruction period after the American civil war.

Colom’s triumph over Hyde-Smith occurred about three years after she blocked the former state prosecutor’s nomination for a federal judgeship during Joe Biden’s presidency, which interrupted Trump’s two White House terms. His victory in many ways punctuated a midterm “blue wave” that saw Trump and his Republican party lose control of Congress to their Democratic counterparts for the latter half of his second presidency beginning in January.

With the outcome of the US Senate race in Alaska still pending on Sunday, the seat to which Colom was elected was among eight that the Democrats had flipped in that congressional chamber. Democrats had also gained more than three dozen seats in the US House during the midterms while significantly expanding their control of state governors’ offices, igniting hopes among the party’s supporters that it could impede Trump’s agenda for the rest of his time in power.

Trump has responded to the new political reality for the rest of his presidency by reminding the public that he has veto powers which he can wield to dictate policy with respect to matters such as the Iran war.

Asked by Bash to reflect on the historic significance of his win over Hyde-Smith, Colom replied: “It says that we have made a lot of progress in the journey to have people judged by the content of their character and not the color of their skin.
“I had faith that Mississippians would give me a chance … if I could get my values out there and a vision for our state out there,” Colom said. “And – you know – Mississippi proved me right.”

Colom appeared on both networks remotely from Atlanta, where he was stranded after his flight to Washington DC was cancelled in the chaotic aftermath of Friday’s nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop.
From Atlanta’s airport on Saturday night, Colom documented the frustrations of fellow travelers on social media .

The senator-elect said one traveler even made a reference to his viral campaign ad criticizing Hyde-Smith for once suggesting those concerned about rising beef prices could opt for cheaper sources of protein.
The campaign ad’s tagline was: “Pick another protein? … I’d rather pick another senator instead.”

As the clock passed midnight at the airport, Colom wrote that another passenger made a joke at the expense of Trump’s transportation secretary Sean Duffy, saying, “Pick another flight? … Pick another transportation secretary.”
body_zh: 密西西比州民主党人指出特朗普做出的承诺：降低价格、停止无休止的战争并公布爱泼斯坦的文件
斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 最近成为四十多年来第一位当选美国参议院的密西西比州民主党人，他承诺将努力确保唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) “履行他在 2024 年成功竞选第二任总统时做出的承诺”。
科洛姆周日接受美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash) 采访时，提到了特朗普做出的各种竞选承诺，包括降低消费者价格、停止其他总统政府领导下看似无休无止的战争，以及全面公布与起诉已故被指控性贩运者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦 (Jeffrey Epstein) 相关的文件，后者的社交圈包括美国和全球精英。
但随着特朗普和以色列二月份在伊朗发动战争，燃料和其他商品的价格飙升，这场冲突已经持续了数月——批评者表示，许多所谓的爱泼斯坦文件被排除在总统政府据称不完整的披露之外。
科罗姆说，选民“选举我是为了确保他履行 2024 年做出的承诺”。 “嗯，我想努力……真正实现这一目标。”
科罗姆还表示，他打算支持通过限制国会议员股票交易的立法，并表示让美国人知道华盛顿特区美国国会大厦的立法者“不是在赚钱，而是在照顾他们”，这一点很重要。
“我们必须照顾我们的家庭，而不是华盛顿特区的家庭，”科洛姆说。
周日，科洛姆在接受 NBC 新闻的克里斯汀·韦尔克 (Kristen Welker) 的单独采访时补充道：“我来这里不是为了照顾亿万富翁。我来这里是为了照顾劳动人民。”
科罗姆发表上述言论之前，他在 11 月 3 日中期选举中取代了共和党现任议员辛迪·海德·史密斯，成为自 1875 年（即美国内战后重建时期）以来第一位来自密西西比州的美国黑人参议员。
科罗姆战胜海德-史密斯大约三年前，她在乔·拜登担任总统期间阻止了这位前州检察官的联邦法官提名，从而中断了特朗普的两届白宫任期。他的胜利在很多方面都标志着中期“蓝色浪潮”的到来，特朗普和他的共和党在从一月份开始的第二任总统任期后半段将国会控制权拱手让给了民主党对手。
由于阿拉斯加州的美国参议院竞选结果周日仍悬而未决，科罗姆当选的席位是民主党在国会会议厅翻转的八个席位之一。中期选举期间，民主党还在美国众议院获得了超过三打的席位，同时大幅扩大了对州长办公室的控制，这点燃了该党支持者的希望，认为这可能会阻碍特朗普余下执政时间的议程。
特朗普在其剩余的总统任期内对新的政治现实做出了回应，提醒公众他拥有否决权，他可以利用这些权力来决定有关伊朗战争等问题的政策。
当巴什要求他反思他战胜海德史密斯的历史意义时，科罗姆回答道：“这表明我们在让人们根据性格内容而不是肤色来判断的过程中取得了很大进展。
“我相信密西西比人会给我一个机会……如果我能表达我的价值观和我们州的愿景，”科洛姆说。 “而且——你知道——密西西比州证明我是对的。”
科洛姆在远离亚特兰大的两个网络上出现，周五全国联邦航空管理局（FAA）地面停留后，他飞往华盛顿特区的航班被取消，导致他被困在亚特兰大。
周六晚上，科洛姆在亚特兰大机场在社交媒体上记录了其他旅客的沮丧情绪。
这位当选参议员表示，一位旅行者甚至提到了他的病毒式竞选广告，该广告批评海德史密斯曾经建议那些担心牛肉价格上涨的人可以选择更便宜的蛋白质来源。
竞选广告的口号是：“选择另一种蛋白质？……我宁愿选择另一位参议员。”
当机场的午夜过去时，科洛姆写道，另一名乘客拿特朗普的交通部长肖恩·达菲开玩笑说：“选择另一趟航班？……选择另一位交通部长。”

title_en: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer
title_zh: 克里斯·范·霍伦表示，他有办法击败查克·舒默赢得参议院领袖
summary: Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer , assertin
summary_zh: 进步派美国参议员呼吁更多地参与民主党核心小组，理由是同行之间对变革持开放态度美国民主党参议员克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen)
body_en: Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers

Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer , asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances.

Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.
On CNN’s State of the Union, he reaffirmed that he believes he has a path to victory, citing support and a widespread openness to change within the Senate Democratic caucus.

“This really is a response to the call of the voters, who clearly rejected Donald Trump and his awful policies, but they haven’t fully hired the Democrats,” Van Hollen said, alluding to how the US president’s Republican party lost control of Congress during the 3 November midterm elections .
“They’ve given us a chance, and I think we need to earn their trust. And I think that begins by not going back to business as usual.”

Van Hollen criticized reports that Schumer’s team may move the Senate caucus leadership election date earlier than 1 December. He contended that the caucus should have a debate about the group’s direction as the Democrats assume control of Congress in January for the second half of Trump’s second presidency.
What the choice between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for Senate leader is all about | Bernie Sanders

Van Hollen also responded to a list that was reportedly leaked by Schumer’s team to the political news outlet the Hill that revealed the committed votes the New York senator claims to already have. Van Hollen said that some of those senators on the list have actually already pledged to vote for him instead of Schumer.

He also called for more “inclusion and democracy” within the Democratic caucus, accusing Schumer of trying to exclude the more progressive members of the party. Van Hollen alluded to victories by Democratic senators-elect whose candidacies Schumer did not support – Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Troy Jackson of Maine – and said they “would not be there” if Schumer had his way.
“He joined with Aipac and crypto to try to defeat them,” Van Hollen said, referring in part to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, which opposed El-Sayed and Jackson.
Appearing on ABC News’s This Week, Van Hollen accused Schumer’s team of putting out misinformation by leaking the alleged list of supporters, equating it to an intimidation tactic.

“They’re essentially trying to instill fear in people who may say that they’re going to support me as a new leader,” he said. “We just had a great day for our democracy around the country. How about a little democracy in the Senate Democratic caucus?”

On Fox News Sunday, Van Hollen responded more directly to the Hill’s report, calling it “a bunch of nonsense”. The outlet reported being told by a Schumer confidant that Van Hollen has “no chance of winning” – and that progressives are only using his candidacy to gain leverage over Schumer to sign on to a “liberal wishlist of priorities”.
“This is a wide open race,” Van Hollen said. “The other team has been putting out numbers that are flatly wrong.
“They’re trying to create this false sense of momentum. If they really believed that they were ahead, they wouldn’t be trying to move up the elections.”
Van Hollen also said that the number of senator supporters he had as of Sunday was “15 and growing”.

“I agree with the American people and all our candidates who ran across the country that this is not about left versus right. It’s not about progressives or moderates or conservatives,” he said. “Those are old Washington labels. It’s much more about taking on a rigged economy, rigged in favor of the very wealthy and fueled by political corruption.”
The race will be the first contested election for Democratic leader in decades. The closed-door, secret-ballot election is slated for early December.
body_zh: 进步的美国参议员呼吁更多地参与民主党核心小组，理由是同行之间对变革持开放态度
美国民主党参议员克里斯·范霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)周日升级了自己的竞选目标，以领导该党即将成为的参议院多数党，而不是查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)，他声称，在一场包括一系列电视露面在内的专门竞选活动中，他有一条通往胜利的道路。
马里兰州进步人士范·霍伦周日出现在美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN)、美国广播公司 (ABC) 和福克斯新闻节目中，继续阐述为什么参议院的同僚应该拒绝舒默，舒默领导了民主党核心小组近十年。
在美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的国情咨文中，他重申，他相信自己有一条通往胜利的道路，理由是参议院民主党核心小组内部的支持和对变革的广泛开放态度。
范霍伦说：“这确实是对选民呼声的回应，他们明确拒绝了唐纳德·特朗普及其可怕的政策，但他们还没有完全雇用民主党。”他暗指美国总统的共和党如何在 11 月 3 日中期选举中失去对国会的控制。
“他们给了我们机会，我认为我们需要赢得他们的信任。我认为，首先要避免一切照旧。”
范霍伦批评了有关舒默团队可能将参议院核心小组领导人选举日期提前到 12 月 1 日的报道。他认为，随着民主党在特朗普第二任总统任期的下半年控制国会，核心小组应该就该组织的方向进行辩论。
查克·舒默（Chuck Schumer）和克里斯·范·霍伦（Chris Van Hollen）作为参议院领袖的选择是什么？伯尼·桑德斯
范霍伦还对据报道由舒默团队泄露给政治新闻媒体《国会山报》的一份名单做出了回应，该名单披露了这位纽约参议员声称已经拥有的已承诺选票。范霍伦说，名单上的一些参议员实际上已经承诺投票给他而不是舒默。
他还呼吁民主党核心小组内加强“包容和民主”，指责舒默试图排除党内更进步的成员。范霍伦提到了舒默不支持的当选民主党参议员——密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·赛义德和缅因州的特洛伊·杰克逊——的胜利，并表示如果舒默按自己的方式行事，他们“就不会参加”。
范霍伦说：“他与 Aipac 和 Crypto 联合起来，试图击败他们。”他指的是反对埃尔赛义德和杰克逊的美国以色列公共事务委员会。
范霍伦在美国广播公司新闻节目《本周》中指责舒默的团队通过泄露所谓的支持者名单来散布错误信息，并将其视为一种恐吓策略。
“他们本质上是试图向那些可能会支持我作为新领导人的人灌输恐惧，”他说。 “我们刚刚为全国的民主度过了美好的一天。参议院民主党核心小组来一点民主怎么样？”
在福克斯周日新闻节目中，范霍伦对国会山的报道做出了更直接的回应，称其为“一堆废话”。据该媒体报道，舒默的一位密友告诉范霍伦“没有获胜的机会”，进步派只是利用他的候选资格来获得对舒默的影响力，以签署“自由派优先愿望清单”。
“这是一场完全开放的竞争，”范霍伦说。 “另一支球队给出的数据完全是错误的。
“他们试图制造这种错误的势头。如果他们真的相信自己领先，他们就不会试图推动选举。”
范霍伦还表示，截至周日，他拥有的参议员支持者数量“已经达到 15 名，而且还在不断增加”。
“我同意美国人民和全国各地竞选的所有候选人的观点，这不是左翼与右翼的斗争。这不是进步派、温和派或保守派的问题，”他说。 “这些都是华盛顿的老标签。这更多的是针对被操纵的经济，被操纵以支持非常富有的人，并受到政治腐败的助长。”
这次竞选将是几十年来民主党领袖首次有争议的选举。闭门、无记名投票选举定于 12 月初举行。

summary: Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a l
summary_zh: 民主党参议员克里斯·范·霍伦表示，特朗普政府没有正确投资现有资金，唐纳德·特朗普政府周日指责
body_en: Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds

Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades.

“I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop , leading to the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights.
Two planes collide on taxiway at Miami airport one day after national grounding
Meanwhile, Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland criticized how the Trump administration has managed existing funding allocated for the improvements coveted by Duffy.

“It’s really rich to hear the secretary pointing the fingers at Congress when Congress has given the administration what they asked for,” Van Hollen separately told CNN’s Bash on Sunday morning. “If they need more, they should come up and justify it. I will support what is necessary to have a safe system and a reliable system.”
Duffy claimed the congressional funding which Van Hollen mentioned – $12.5bn – was limited in scope and not nearly enough.

“I have no money in that $12.5bn that I can use for a new architecture for telecom,” said Duffy. “I can’t build new software to manage our airplanes in the airspace because it dates back to the 1990s, but there’s no money for that. There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old.”
Duffy also spent part of the interview with CNN defending Trump, who waited until Sunday to remark on the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.

The president’s comments came in the form of social media posts blaming the Biden administration and describing himself as busy “in the White House having meetings on many subjects”. They came after he had posted about what he envisioned to be a bipartisan congressional initiative to revitalize the motion picture and television industries.

“Before I even was sworn in, the president who loves the airspace was telling me we have to modernize,” Duffy said to Bash. “This is the first president we have who cares this much about modernizing the airspace.”
When asked why Trump took two days to comment on the ground stop, Duffy claimed he was in constant behind-the-scene contact with the president.
“He was fully engaged because this is important to him, and it’s important to America,” Duffy claimed. “The president is fully supportive, fully engaged, and was fully tracking what’s happening.”
In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump blamed Joe Biden and demanded funding from Congress.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad,” Trump wrote. “We have the knowledge and plan for the Flight Control Systems, we need Congress to give the money, FAST!”

In another interview on Sunday on CBS News’ Face the Nation, Duffy told host Margaret Brennan that the FAA was currently investigating the root cause of the botched maintenance work that triggered the ground stop. He said the maintenance involved – replacing telecommunication lines from old copper wire to fiber optic cables – has occurred “thousands of times” without any issues.

The contractor, L3Harris, is reportedly conducting diagnostics testing. Duffy, as he has repeatedly done, said there continued being no indication of a foreign cyberattack. Professional Aviation Safety Specialists (Pass), the AFL-CIO labor union representing more than 11,000 workers at the FAA, said technicians it represents were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.

“The issue was isolated to two contractor owned and maintained routers that were being updated midday,” the union said in a statement . “Historically, contractors have followed a protocol where FAA employees conduct a risk assessment and coordinate the maintenance of the system or equipment.”
But the union said Pass-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades at the center of Friday’s ground stop.
body_zh: 民主党参议员克里斯·范·霍伦表示，特朗普政府没有正确投资现有资金
唐纳德·特朗普政府周日将周五全国航班停飞四个小时造成的旅行混乱归咎于前任总统以及国会资金的缺乏——尽管一位民主党参议员辩称，特朗普政府尚未将已获得的所有资金用于实施所需的航空旅行基础设施升级。
美国交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 对美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash) 表示：“我对前几届政府给予我的责任负责。”一天前，他表示，由于承包商日常但必要的维护工作失误，导致美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 于周五停飞，导致数千架航班延误或取消。
国家停飞一天后，两架飞机在迈阿密机场滑行道上相撞
与此同时，马里兰州民主党参议员克里斯·范·霍伦批评特朗普政府如何管理分配给达菲所觊觎的改进的现有资金。
“当国会满足了政府的要求时，听到国务卿对国会指手画脚，真是太令人高兴了，”范霍伦周日早上单独告诉美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的巴什 (Bash)。 “如果他们需要更多，他们应该站出来证明其合理性。我将支持建立安全和可靠系统所需的一切。”
达菲声称范霍伦提到的国会拨款——125 亿美元——范围有限，而且远远不够。
“我没有那 125 亿美元的钱可以用于新的电信架构，”达菲说。 “我无法开发新的软件来管理我们在空域的飞机，因为它可以追溯到 20 世纪 90 年代，但没有钱来做这件事。没有钱建塔楼。我们的塔楼很旧了。”
达菲还在接受 CNN 采访时为特朗普辩护，特朗普直到周日才对 25 年来最长的全国停飞发表评论。
总统的评论以社交媒体帖子的形式发布，指责拜登政府，并称自己“在白宫就许多主题举行会议”很忙。在他发布了他设想的两党国会倡议以振兴电影和电视行业之后，他们就发布了这些倡议。
“在我宣誓就职之前，热爱空域的总统就告诉我，我们必须实现现代化，”达菲对巴什说。 “这是我们第一位如此关心空域现代化的总统。”
当被问及特朗普为什么花了两天时间才对地面站发表评论时，达菲声称他一直在与总统进行幕后接触。
“他全身心投入，因为这对他很重要，对美国也很重要，”达菲声称。 “总统全力支持、全力参与，并全力追踪正在发生的事情。”
特朗普周日在《真相社会》上发表文章，指责乔·拜登，并要求国会提供资金。
“拜登政府是联邦航空局的一场灾难。他们触及的一切都变得很糟糕，”特朗普写道。 “我们拥有飞行控制系统的知识和计划，我们需要国会尽快提供资金！”
在周日哥伦比亚广播公司新闻节目“面对全国”的另一次采访中，达菲告诉主持人玛格丽特·布伦南，美国联邦航空局目前正在调查导致地面停止的拙劣维护工作的根本原因。他说，涉及的维护工作——将电信线路从旧铜线更换为光缆——已经发生了“数千次”，没有出现任何问题。
据报道，承包商 L3Harris 正在进行诊断测试。达菲一再表示，没有任何迹象表明存在外国网络攻击。代表 FAA 11,000 多名员工的 AFL-CIO 工会专业航空安全专家 (Pass) 表示，其代表的技术人员没有参与导致地面停止的升级。
该问题是由两个承包商拥有和维护的路由器造成的，这些路由器正在中午进行更新。从历史上看，承包商遵循一项协议，由联邦航空局员工进行风险评估并协调系统或设备的维护。 PASS 代表的技术人员没有参与导致昨天停飞的升级工作。
但工会表示，帕斯代表的技术人员没有参与周五地面站中心的升级工作。

body_en: As Oakland residents watch ex-mayor Sheng Thao stand trial, the scandal has come to symbolise wider frustrations

Two years ago, residents of Oakland, California , woke up to a shocking scene: their mayor’s home was being raided by the FBI. Agents were seen carrying dozens of boxes from the hilltop home of Sheng Thao, the city’s 38-year-old leader, as part of an investigation constituents would later learn alleged her participation in a pay-to-play scheme with the city’s recycling contractor.

It was a stunning moment for Thao, who was elected to lead the Bay Area city in 2022 and was once seen as a promising young mayor in a city that has long grappled with economic inequality and a reputation for violent crime. Her story of growing up in a refugee family and overcoming domestic violence and homelessness to become the first person of Hmong descent to run a major US city resonated with readers confronting questions about equity and representation that came to the fore during the Covid-19 pandemic, and made her the subject of glowing media profiles .
body_zh: 当奥克兰居民目睹前市长盛涛受审时，这一丑闻已成为更广泛的挫败感的象征
两年前，加州奥克兰的居民一觉醒来，看到了令人震惊的一幕：他们市长的家遭到联邦调查局(FBI)的突击搜查。有人看到特工从该市 38 岁领导人盛涛 (Sheng Thao) 的山顶家中搬运了数十个箱子，调查的一部分选民后来得知，她涉嫌参与该市回收承包商的付费计划。
对于陶来说，这是一个令人震惊的时刻，他于 2022 年当选为湾区城市的领导人，曾被视为这座长期与经济不平等和暴力犯罪恶名作斗争的城市中一位有前途的年轻市长。她在难民家庭长大，克服家庭暴力和无家可归，成为第一个管理美国大城市的苗族后裔的故事引起了读者的共鸣，这些读者面临着 Covid-19 大流行期间出现的公平和代表性问题，并使她成为媒体报道的焦点。

title_en: ICE reports record immigration arrests, deportations since Trump White House return

body_en: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history
WASHINGTON -- U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Thursday that it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history.

ICE said it deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, up 9% from its previous high of 442,640 in the same period a year earlier and up 78% from 271,480 in 2024, the last year of Joe Biden's presidency.
ICE arrested 474,850 people in the most recent 12-month period, roughly double the 239,890 arrests a year earlier and more than quadruple the 113,430 arrests in 2024.
ICE had not released such precise counts since President Donald Trump returned to the White House, including for 2025.

title_en: ‘We gotta do something’: the coalition that helped elect Scott Colom to Senate
title_zh: “我们必须做点什么”：帮助斯科特·科洛姆当选参议员的联盟
summary: Behind the Mississippi senator-elect’s victory is a coalition of groups that didn’t have a lot of money, but had collective power and post-Callais anger Long before national political leaders and media were paying any attention, long before the Louisiana v Cal
summary_zh: 这位密西西比州当选参议员的胜利背后是一个团体联盟，这些团体没有很多钱，但拥有集体权力和后卡莱时代的影响。
body_en: Behind the Mississippi senator-elect’s victory is a coalition of groups that didn’t have a lot of money, but had collective power and post-Callais anger

Long before national political leaders and media were paying any attention, long before the Louisiana v Callais supreme court decision gutted the Voting Rights Act, Mississippi organizers were working to grow political participation and improve quality of life in a state that often ranks low on its residents’ health and wellbeing.

Activists’ momentum contributed to Democrat Scott Colom’s historic upset in the midterm elections. A loose coalition of about a dozen, mostly Black-led nonprofits or initiatives rallied residents after Callais, the April decision that set off a flurry of redistricting efforts across southern states. That case was not the sole impetus for organizing efforts across Mississippi, but it turned out thousands in the 20 May “Mississippi Fights Back” rally . Callais became the most recent opportunity to channel people’s frustrations and hopes into action – and to harness previous campaigns that go back years and even decades.
body_zh: 这位密西西比州当选参议员的胜利背后是一个团体联盟，他们没有很多钱，但拥有集体权力和后卡莱的愤怒
早在国家政治领导人和媒体对此予以关注之前，早在路易斯安那诉卡莱最高法院的判决破坏《投票权法》之前，密西西比州的组织者就一直致力于在居民健康和福祉方面排名较低的州提高政治参与度并提高生活质量。

活动人士的势头导致民主党人斯科特·科洛姆在中期选举中遭遇历史性失利。在卡莱事件之后，一个由大约十几家（主要是黑人领导的非营利组织或倡议）组成的松散联盟团结了居民，卡莱事件四月份的决定引发了南部各州一系列重新划分选区的努力。该案件并不是密西西比州各地组织行动的唯一动力，但在 5 月 20 日的“密西西比反击”集会上，有数千人参加。卡莱成为将人们的沮丧和希望转化为行动的最新机会，并利用之前几年甚至几十年前的活动。

title_en: In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a fine line with Trump
title_zh: 在呼吁结束伊朗战争时，万斯与特朗普保持着微妙的界限
summary: A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.
summary_zh: 在伊朗战争问题上，特朗普总统和万斯副总统之间出现了裂痕。 NPR 的阿耶莎·拉斯科 (Ayesha Rascoe) 与工作人员苏珊·格拉瑟 (Susan Glasser) 交谈
body_en: In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a fine line with Trump A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.
A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

The day after Republicans suffered a major defeat in the midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance posted a list of what Republicans could do to win back disillusioned voters. No. 1 - end the war in Iran. President Trump said he didn't disagree. But last week he posted, quote, "we don't need a deal with Iran." Instead of focusing on Iran, Trump said he was asking Vance to turn his complete and total attention to corruption and crime in cities and states run by Democrats.
Joining us now is Susan Glasser, staff writer at The New Yorker. Thank you so much for joining us.
RASCOE: Did you read President Trump's post as a response to Vance's criticism of the war?

GLASSER: I mean, not to be too blunt, but basically, you have the president of the United States saying to his own vice president, yeah. You're kind of fired from the most important issue that we have, which is how to resolve this unresolved and unwon conflict in the Middle East. If anything, because of how overwhelming the scale of the Democratic victory was in the elections, we've kind of understated the extent to which it is a remarkable thing to have had Vice President Vance publicly blame the president's top foreign policy priority for that overwhelming defeat. Of course, we know Donald Trump. He's furious about this.
RASCOE: When Vance said the war is the problem, one thing that stood out to me is he kind of was talking about it as if he wasn't in the administration. Like, he didn't put himself in it.

GLASSER: No. I think the big-picture context here, Ayesha, is clearly that Vice President Vance feels his chances, such as they are, for becoming president after Trump slipping away, largely due to the war. Donald Trump, of course, campaigned in 2024 saying he was the candidate of no new wars. And Vance was specifically selected from what you might call the real MAGA America First wing of the Republican Party.

For him, this is even more foundational. His people have gone to great lengths, it seems to me, to put out in news reports that he was against the war from the beginning in the private councils that the president had, even though it has technically been his portfolio since the spring to negotiate an end to the conflict with Iran. Obviously, that has not succeeded. There are very dim prospects for any kind of success in a negotiated peace anytime very soon.

I think for Vance, it just underscores the problem that American vice presidents have in general, which is to say it is very, very difficult as an incumbent vice president to win election as president. Only two presidents - George H. W. Bush managed to do this in 1988, after two terms of Ronald Reagan. You have to go all the way back to the 19th century before there's another incumbent vice president who managed the feat.
RASCOE: Do you look at this as a breakup between Vance and Trump, maybe emotionally if not publicly?

GLASSER: It certainly wouldn't be unprecedented with this particular president, who not only fell out with his first vice president. But, you know, it all ended so badly that they're chanting, hang Mike Pence, because he won't do what Donald Trump wanted him to do on January 6. So the odds, it seems to me, based on Trump's history, were always quite high for JD Vance to have a very difficult time.

RASCOE: Would it not be, I guess, the biggest irony if it were to happen that Trump leaves office, and it is up to the next president to deal with this war in the Middle East? Is that not a great irony for the president who was supposed to start no new wars?

GLASSER: Absolutely. Not only is it a great irony. I - it's a very real possibility that the Iranians may continue in this nether state over the next couple years. Often, wars and conflicts do end not by the leaders who start them. Because they have so much invested politically and in terms of their own legacy in the conflict, it's harder for them to end wars. So historically, that is an analogy.

And I'm mindful of the fact that Donald Trump - you know, he sort of came of age in the 1980s. And that image of Jimmy Carter, for him, was basically the definition of American weakness. And as you know, Donald Trump has almost a - sort of a cult of the idea of strength. So it would be a bitter pill, indeed, for him to swallow if the Iranians did to him some version of what they did to Jimmy Carter, which is to slowly strangle Carter's presidency.
RASCOE: That's Susan Glasser. She's a staff writer at The New Yorker. Thank you so much for joining us.

body_zh: 在呼吁结束伊朗战争时，万斯与特朗普保持着微妙的界限 特朗普总统和副总统万斯之间在伊朗战争问题上出现了裂痕。 NPR 的阿伊莎·拉斯科 (Ayesha Rascoe) 与《纽约客》特约撰稿人苏珊·格拉瑟 (Susan Glasser) 进行对话。
在伊朗战争问题上，特朗普总统和万斯副总统之间出现了裂痕。 NPR 的阿伊莎·拉斯科 (Ayesha Rascoe) 与《纽约客》特约撰稿人苏珊·格拉瑟 (Susan Glasser) 进行对话。
共和党在中期选举中惨败的第二天，副总统万斯发布了一份共和党可以采取哪些措施来赢回失望的选民的清单。第一——结束伊朗战争。特朗普总统表示他并不反对。但上周他发帖称，“我们不需要与伊朗达成协议。”特朗普表示，他没有把重点放在伊朗身上，而是要求万斯将全部注意力转向民主党管理的城市和州的腐败和犯罪问题。
现在加入我们的是《纽约客》特约撰稿人苏珊·格拉瑟 (Susan Glasser)。非常感谢您加入我们。
拉斯科：您是否阅读了特朗普总统的帖子作为对万斯对战争批评的回应？
格拉瑟：我的意思是，不要太直白，但基本上，美国总统对他自己的副总统说，是的。你有点被我们面临的最重要的问题解雇了，那就是如何解决中东这场未解决和未赢的冲突。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是，由于民主党在选举中取得了压倒性的胜利，我们有点低估了副总统万斯公开指责总统的首要外交政策优先事项导致了这场压倒性的失败，这在多大程度上是一件值得注意的事情。当然，我们认识唐纳德·特朗普。他对此很愤怒。
拉斯科：当万斯说战争是问题所在时，令我印象深刻的一件事是，他在谈论这个问题时就好像他不在政府中一样。比如说，他没有把自己放进去。
格拉瑟：不。我认为，阿伊莎，这里的大背景显然是，副总统万斯认为，在特朗普落选后，他有机会成为总统，这主要是由于战争。当然，唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 在 2024 年竞选时表示，他不会发起新的战争。万斯是从共和党中真正的美国第一派中特别选出的。
对于他来说，这更是基础。在我看来，他的人民不遗余力地在新闻报道中表明，他从一开始就在总统的私人委员会中反对战争，尽管从技术上讲，自春季以来谈判结束与伊朗的冲突一直是他的职责。显然，这并没有成功。短期内通过谈判达成和平的任何成功前景都非常渺茫。
我认为对万斯来说，这只是强调了美国副总统普遍存在的问题，也就是说，作为现任副总统，赢得总统选举是非常非常困难的。只有两位总统做到了这一点——1988 年乔治·H·W·布什 (George H.W. Bush) 在罗纳德·里根 (Ronald Reagan) 两届任期之后做到了这一点。你必须追溯到 19 世纪，才有另一位现任副总统实现这一壮举。
拉斯科：你是否认为这是万斯和特朗普之间的分手，即使不是公开的，也可能是情感上的？
格拉瑟：对于这位特定的总统来说，这当然不是史无前例的，他不仅与他的第一副总统发生了争执。但是，你知道，这一切的结局都很糟糕，以至于他们高呼“吊死迈克·彭斯”，因为他不会做唐纳德·特朗普在 1 月 6 日希望他做的事情。因此，在我看来，根据特朗普的历史，JD 万斯度过一段非常困难时期的可能性总是很高。
拉斯科：我想，如果特朗普卸任，由下一任总统来处理中东这场战争，这不是最大的讽刺吗？对于这位不应该发动新战争的总统来说，这不是一个极大的讽刺吗？
格拉瑟：当然。这不仅是一个极大的讽刺。我——伊朗人很有可能在未来几年继续处于这种地狱状态。通常，战争和冲突并不是由发动战争和冲突的领导人结束的。因为他们在政治上以及在冲突中留下的遗产方面投入了太多，所以结束战争对他们来说更加困难。从历史上看，这是一个类比。
我注意到唐纳德·特朗普——你知道，他是在 20 世纪 80 年代成年的。对他来说，吉米·卡特的形象基本上就是美国弱点的定义。如你所知，唐纳德·特朗普几乎有一种对力量观念的崇拜。因此，如果伊朗人像对待吉米·卡特那样对待他，那就是慢慢扼杀卡特的总统职位，这对他来说确实是一颗苦果。
拉斯科：那是苏珊·格拉瑟。她是《纽约客》的特约撰稿人。非常感谢您加入我们。

title_en: Trump administration planning to reimburse doctors treating vaccine ‘injury’
title_zh: 特朗普政府计划补偿治疗疫苗“损伤”的医生
summary: Experts warn that sweeping changes elevate health secretary RFK Jr’s anti-vaccine agenda and personal profit The Trump administration is finalizing a rule to reimburse doctors who diagnose, treat and counsel patients with side effects from vaccines in what exp
summary_zh: 专家警告称，彻底的变化将提升卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪的反疫苗议程和个人利益。
body_en: Experts warn that sweeping changes elevate health secretary RFK Jr’s anti-vaccine agenda and personal profit

The Trump administration is finalizing a rule to reimburse doctors who diagnose, treat and counsel patients with side effects from vaccines in what experts believe is an attempt to undermine trust in vaccines and to create an evidence base on their purported risks.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), also announced the creation of a vaccine “injury” research center at the National Institutes of Health and has sought to reshape the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) – actions that point to Kennedy’s longtime activism against vaccination as well as the profits he and his network have made from vaccine lawsuits.
Kennedy and his allies have also profited from growing misinformation peddled through books, paid speaking events and the supplement industry.

“I do think he’s a real ideologue – he really believes in this,” said Dorit Reiss, professor of law at UC Law San Francisco. But Kennedy and his allies are likely “very happy to make money doing it”, she said.
Senator opens investigation into evidence RFK Jr ‘unlawfully lied’ to Congress

Peter Hotez, professor and dean of Baylor College of Medicine’s National School of Tropical Medicine, agreed, saying Kennedy’s actions are likely a combination of “being an ideological zealot and making money either for himself or for his associates”.
Emily Hilliard, an HHS spokesperson, said the department “categorically reject claims that Secretary Kennedy is pursuing personal gain or seeking to dismantle American medicine”.

Prior to his confirmation hearing in January 2025, Kennedy disclosed $2.5m in income from referrals for vaccine-related lawsuits. In the hearing, Kennedy would not commit to forgoing compensation from vaccine lawsuits after he leaves office. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, listed several ways in which Kennedy’s actions, some of which have now happened, could influence future litigation.

“Kennedy can kill off access to vaccines and make millions of dollars while he does it,” Warren said at the hearing. “Kids might die. But Robert Kennedy can keep cashing in.” She pointed to Kennedy’s involvement in litigation against Merck for its HPV vaccine – lawsuits that were settled for more than $50m in June 2026. After the confirmation hearing, Kennedy said his son would receive the money, expected to be 10% of the total; it’s unclear if he did.
“For most of us, money going to our children isn’t exactly money not going to us,” Reiss said. “There’s a dozen ways he and his family could benefit” from Kennedy’s actions, she added.

Kennedy has long profited from his anti-vaccine misinformation. Tony Lyons, Kennedy’s publisher and a central figure in the constellation of Maha political organizations, reportedly paid Kennedy $4m in book advances over the past year. The publisher also paid Kennedy $451,000 in consulting fees before he became HHS secretary. That’s on top of other book sales and paid speaking engagements over the years. Kennedy also earned $326,000 for the 15 weeks he served as chairman of Children’s Health Defense in 2023 – more than half of his $510,000 salary in 2022.
More recently, he received free flights and trips on a yacht from a former donor to his presidential campaign, who is now under investigation by the Senate for the gifts totaling some $250,000.
As HHS secretary, Kennedy has also loosened regulations on peptides, a booming part of the largely unregulated wellness industry.

“I think he’s doing what everyone knew he was going to do,” said Hotez. Kennedy, before and during his tenure as leader of HHS, has been “chipping away at public confidence in vaccines and immunizations in favor of products that can be sold by the wellness industry”, he added.

Aaron Siri, Kennedy’s former lawyer who represents people who say they have experienced severe side effects, has advocated for changing all vaccines to “shared clinical decision-making”. If those changes took place, Siri could argue that the vaccines are not covered under the VICP and therefore open to litigation.
“A lot of what he is doing is geared toward setting up a more profitable litigation atmosphere,” Reiss said.

Siri did not respond to the Guardian’s question about profiting from litigation, but instead argued that “if vaccines are as ‘safe’ as touted by the government, then there should be no need for immunity to liability and, likewise, there should be very few, if any, successful cases”.
The most common claim to VICP – making up more than half – has to do with where the vaccine is administered, not the vaccines themselves.
body_zh: 专家警告说，彻底的变化会提升卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪的反疫苗议程和个人利益
特朗普政府正在敲定一项规则，向诊断、治疗和咨询疫苗副作用患者的医生提供补偿，专家认为此举试图破坏人们对疫苗的信任，并为其所谓的风险建立证据基础。
美国卫生与公众服务部 (HHS) 部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F Kennedy Jr) 也宣布在美国国立卫生研究院建立疫苗“伤害”研究中心，并寻求重塑疫苗伤害补偿计划 (VICP)，这一行动表明肯尼迪长期以来反对疫苗接种的行动，以及他和他的网络从疫苗诉讼中获取的利润。
肯尼迪及其盟友还从通过书籍、付费演讲活动和补充剂行业兜售的越来越多的错误信息中获利。
“我确实认为他是一个真正的理论家——他真的相信这一点，”加州大学法学院旧金山分校法学教授多里特·赖斯(Dorit Reiss)说。但她说，肯尼迪和他的盟友可能“非常乐意通过这样做赚钱”。
参议员对小罗伯特·肯尼迪向国会“非法撒谎”的证据展开调查
贝勒医学院国家热带医学院教授兼院长彼得·霍特兹对此表示同意，他说肯尼迪的行为很可能是“作为一个意识形态狂热者，为自己或为他的同事赚钱”的结合。
美国卫生与公众服务部发言人艾米丽·希利亚德表示，该部门“断然否认肯尼迪部长正在追求个人利益或试图瓦解美国医学的说法”。
在 2025 年 1 月的确认听证会之前，肯尼迪披露了来自疫苗相关诉讼转介的 250 万美元收入。在听证会上，肯尼迪不会承诺在卸任后放弃疫苗诉讼的赔偿。来自马萨诸塞州的民主党人伊丽莎白·沃伦列出了肯尼迪行为可能影响未来诉讼的几种方式（其中一些已经发生）。
沃伦在听证会上表示：“肯尼迪这样做可以阻止疫苗的获得，并赚取数百万美元。” “孩子们可能会死。但罗伯特·肯尼迪可以继续赚钱。”她指出，肯尼迪参与了针对默克公司 HPV 疫苗的诉讼，该诉讼于 2026 年 6 月以超过 5000 万美元和解。在确认听证会后，肯尼迪表示，他的儿子将收到这笔钱，预计将占总额的 10%；目前尚不清楚他是否这样做了。
“对于我们大多数人来说，给孩子的钱并不完全是不给我们的钱，”赖斯说。她补充说，“他和他的家人可以通过多种方式从肯尼迪的行动中受益”。

肯尼迪长期以来一直从他的反疫苗错误信息中获利。据报道，肯尼迪的出版商托尼·莱昂斯 (Tony Lyons) 在过去一年向肯尼迪支付了 400 万美元的图书预付款，也是玛哈政治组织的核心人物。在肯尼迪成为 HHS 部长之前，出版商还向他支付了 451,000 美元的咨询费。这还不包括多年来的其他图书销售和付费演讲活动。肯尼迪在 2023 年担任儿童健康保护组织主席的 15 周内还获得了 326,000 美元的收入，这是他 2022 年 510,000 美元工资的一半以上。
最近，他从一位前总统竞选捐助者那里获得了免费航班和游艇旅行的机会，该捐助者目前正因总计约 25 万美元的礼物而受到参议院的调查。
作为美国卫生与公众服务部部长，肯尼迪还放松了对肽的监管，肽是基本上不受监管的健康行业的一个蓬勃发展的部分。
“我认为他正在做每个人都知道他会做的事情，”霍特兹说。他补充说，肯尼迪在担任美国卫生与公众服务部领导人之前和期间，一直“削弱公众对疫苗和免疫接种的信心，转而支持健康行业销售的产品”。
肯尼迪的前律师亚伦·西里（Aaron Siri）代表那些自称经历过严重副作用的人，主张将所有疫苗改为“共同临床决策”。如果发生这些变化，Siri 可能会辩称这些疫苗不在 VICP 的涵盖范围内，因此可能会受到诉讼。
“他所做的很多事情都是为了营造一种更有利可图的诉讼氛围，”赖斯说。
Siri没有回答《卫报》关于从诉讼中获利的问题，而是辩称“如果疫苗像政府吹捧的那样‘安全’，那么就不需要免责，同样，成功的案例也应该很少”。
最常见的 VICP 主张（占一半以上）与疫苗接种地点有关，而不是疫苗本身。

title_zh: 美国官员从“密西西比奇迹”游轮和油轮事故中恢复了音频
summary: Tank vessel suffered sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into docked riverboat near New Orleans Federal safety investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recovered audio and released a preliminary timeline on Sunday of a
summary_zh: 油轮突然转向失灵，两分钟后撞上新奥尔良附近停靠的河船 联邦安全调查人员与
body_en: US officials recover audio from ‘Mississippi miracle’ cruise ship and tanker crash | New Orleans
Tank vessel suffered sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into docked riverboat near New Orleans

Federal safety investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recovered audio and released a preliminary timeline on Sunday of a collision between a cruise ship and a tanker vessel in the Mississippi River on Friday.

The data was retrieved after more than 30 people were injured when a tanker collided with a docked cruise ship – American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage riverboat – near the port of New Orleans on Friday at about 12.30pm. All passengers aboard the cruise ship have been accounted for, officials said.
The tank vessel suffered a sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into the docked riverboat, causing it to tip on to its side, officials said.
New Orleans officials file $1m lawsuit after ‘Mississippi miracle’ tanker crash

“It experienced the steering casualty, resulting in the rudder remaining to starboard,” said Bart Barnum, senior marine accident investigator for the NTSB’s office of marine safety, during a media briefing on Sunday. “Following the steering casualty, the Atlantic Asphalt veered to starboard toward the east bank of the river.”

Before the collision, audio collected by officials captured “the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance broadcasted over the vessel’s marine radio, commands to deploy the vessel’s anchors, and emergency ship handling orders”, according to Barnum.
The NTSB is leading the safety investigation alongside the US Coast Guard, as well as American Cruise Lines and representatives from the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the tanker’s flag state.
A preliminary report is expected to be published within 30 days.

Images and videos of the collision have been circulating online. The father of a cruise ship worker who survived the collision spoke about the moment his daughter called him in the middle of the incident.

“She’s FaceTiming me hysterically in a lifejacket in the middle of the Mississippi River crying, ‘Dad, dad, I had to jump off the boat,’” said Wayne Hager in an interview with Good Morning America over the weekend. “I’m hearing people screaming and yelling in the background and kind of like some, I don’t know, like metal grinding noises or whatever.”

Video of Leelah Hager posted on social media later shows her in the water wearing a life vest immediately after the collision between the Atlantic Asphalt tanker and the cruise ship, which had about 190 passengers and crew aboard. Other images of the incident show how the tanker caused the American Heritage to capsize.

New Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit seeking more than $1m in damages from the owner and operator of the asphalt tanker. Four crew members of the American Heritage filed a separate lawsuit against Nave Shipping and Thome Ship Management, which oversee the tanker, claiming they “suffered significant and life changing injuries to their mind and body”, according to the suit.

According to the document, the collision caused the cruise ship to partially sink, throwing the crew members and passengers of the American Heritage “overboard into the Mississippi River, not knowing if they were going to live or die”, the lawsuit reads.
The crew members of American Heritage are alleging negligence, gross negligence, carelessness or fault of the managers of the tanker.
body_zh: 美国官员从“密西西比奇迹”游轮和油轮事故中恢复了音频新奥尔良
油轮在新奥尔良附近撞上停靠的河船前两分钟突然转向失灵
周日，美国国家运输安全委员会 (NTSB) 的联邦安全调查人员找到了音频，并发布了周五密西西比河上一艘游轮与一艘油轮相撞的初步时间表。
周五中午 12 点 30 分左右，一艘油轮在新奥尔良港附近与一艘停靠的游轮（美国游轮公司的 American Heritage 河船）相撞，造成 30 多人受伤，随后检索到了这些数据。官员称，游轮上的所有乘客均已下落不明。
官员称，这艘油轮在撞上停靠的河船前两分钟突然转向失灵，导致其侧翻。
新奥尔良官员在“密西西比奇迹”油轮失事后提起 100 万美元诉讼
美国国家运输安全委员会海上安全办公室高级海上事故调查员巴特·巴纳姆在周日的媒体吹风会上表示：“它发生了转向事故，导致舵留在右舷。” “在转向事故发生后，大西洋沥青号向右舷转向河东岸。”
巴纳姆表示，在碰撞之前，官员收集的音频捕捉到了“船舶的汽笛、通过船舶海上无线电广播的警告和援助请求、部署船舶锚的命令以及紧急船舶处理命令”。
美国国家运输安全委员会正在与美国海岸警卫队、美国邮轮公司以及油轮船旗国马绍尔群岛共和国的代表一起领导这项安全调查。
初步报告预计将在 30 天内发布。
碰撞的图像和视频已在网上流传。一名在碰撞中幸存的游轮工人的父亲谈到了他的女儿在事故发生时给他打电话的那一刻。
“她穿着救生衣在密西西比河中央歇斯底里地对我进行视频通话，哭喊着，‘爸爸，爸爸，我不得不跳下船，’”韦恩·哈格周末在接受《早安美国》采访时说道。 “我听到人们在背景中尖叫和大喊，有点像金属摩擦声或其他什么声音，我不知道。”
Leelah Hager 后来在社交媒体上发布的视频显示，在大西洋沥青油轮与游轮相撞后，她立即穿着救生衣下水，游轮上约有 190 名乘客和船员。该事件的其他图像显示了油轮如何导致美国遗产号倾覆。
新奥尔良港口官员提起诉讼，要求沥青油轮的船东和运营商赔偿超过 100 万美元的损失。诉讼称，美国遗产号的四名船员对负责监管这艘油轮的 Nave Shipping 和 Thome Ship Management 分别提起诉讼，声称他们“身心遭受了严重且改变生活的伤害”。
诉讼称，碰撞导致游轮部分下沉，美国遗产号的船员和乘客“被抛入密西西比河，不知道自己是生还是死”。
美国遗产号的船员指控油轮管理人员存在疏忽、重大过失、粗心或过错。

title_en: Trump plans to take Qatari jet to Asia, but it’s unclear whether it’s been ‘maxed out’
title_zh: 特朗普计划乘坐卡塔尔飞机飞往亚洲，但尚不清楚它是否已“超载”
summary: President Donald Trump is expected to take the Qatari-gifted Air Force One to Asia on Monday as questions linger about upgrades the White House said were needed after a security threat from Iran forced the president to fly home from Turkey on a secret military
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统预计将于周一乘坐卡塔尔赠送的空军一号前往亚洲，因为有关白宫所说的升级的疑问仍然存在。
body_en: By Monica Alba , Courtney Kube and Casey Wooten

President Donald Trump is expected to take the Qatari-gifted Air Force One to Asia on Monday as questions linger about upgrades the White House said were needed after a security threat from Iran forced the president to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane in July, according to two U.S. officials.

For months, Trump has said the jet from the Qataris would be “going away” to get “maxed out” so it could “go into any territory.” In September, he said those changes to the plane would “take about 60 days.” The president flew on the new Air Force One to Ireland that month without any issues. He then used the plane regularly during a midterm travel blitz in October, which meant it was not out of commission for an extended period.

Instead, the plane has received some improvements and periodic maintenance, but it is unclear whether it has been fully “maxed out,” per the officials. A longer upgrade period is expected in the future, according to one of the officials, but those upgrades will not take a full 60 days.

In recent months, the plane has received some “cosmetic” enhancements to the interior, the other U.S. official said, but that did not cover the larger work that the White House said would take place eventually.

“We don’t comment on specific upgrades or modifications to Air Force Once,” a senior administration official told NBC News in a statement. “We maintain a consistent posture that ensures a safe, secure, and reliable capability for the President of the United States and routinely evolve the capability as required to maintain that posture. It is the greatest Presidential plane ever built.”
In July, Trump said the plane “has a lot of capability.”

“But as I understand it, in about a month ​or so, they’re gonna send it to have it be maxed out,” he said. “It’ll take about a month.” Trump did not detail the nature of the work, and the White House has not explained why the original assessment of 30 days later doubled to 60 days.

At the time, then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement that the new Air Force One was “perfectly safe” for domestic and overseas travel but noted in July that the plane would “receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete.”
Monica Alba is a White House correspondent for NBC News.
Courtney Kube is a correspondent covering national security and the military for the NBC News Investigative Unit.
Casey Wooten is a breaking news editor for the politics team at NBC News.
body_zh: 作者：莫妮卡·阿尔芭、考特尼·库贝和凯西·伍滕
据两名美国官员称，唐纳德·特朗普总统预计将于周一乘坐卡塔尔赠送的空军一号前往亚洲，因为在伊朗的安全威胁迫使总统于 7 月乘坐秘密军用飞机从土耳其飞回国后，白宫表示需要进行升级，但仍存在疑问。
几个月来，特朗普一直表示卡塔尔的飞机将“离开”以达到“最大功率”，以便它可以“进入任何领土”。 9 月，他表示对飞机的这些改动将“大约需要 60 天”。当月，总统乘坐新的空军一号飞往爱尔兰，没有出现任何问题。然后，他在 10 月份的中期旅行闪电战中定期使用这架飞机，这意味着这架飞机不会在很长一段时间内停止使用。
相反，这架飞机已经进行了一些改进和定期维护，但据官员称，尚不清楚它是否已完全“达到极限”。一位官员表示，预计未来的升级周期会更长，但这些升级不会花费整整 60 天。
另一位美国官员表示，近几个月来，这架飞机的内部进行了一些“外观”改进，但这并不包括白宫所说的最终将进行的更大规模的工作。
一位高级政府官员在一份声明中告诉 NBC 新闻：“我们不会对空军一次的具体升级或修改发表评论。” “我们保持一致的姿态，确保美国总统拥有安全、可靠的能力，并根据需要定期发展能力以保持这种姿态。这是有史以来最伟大的总统专机。”
7月，特朗普表示这架飞机“具有很多能力”。
“但据我了解，大约一个月左右，他们就会将其发送至最大，”他说。 “大约需要一个月的时间。”特朗普没有详细说明工作的性质，白宫也没有解释为何原来评估的30天后加倍至60天。
当时，时任白宫新闻秘书卡罗琳·莱维特在一份声明中表示，新的空军一号对于国内和海外旅行“非常安全”，但在 7 月份指出，这架飞机将“在秋季接受额外的升级和增强，大约需要一个月的时间才能完成。”
莫妮卡·阿尔芭 (Monica Alba) 是 NBC 新闻的白宫记者。
Courtney Kube 是 NBC 新闻调查组报道国家安全和军事事务的记者。
凯西·伍滕 (Casey Wooten) 是 NBC 新闻政治团队的突发新闻编辑。

title_en: Somali-American Uber driver brutally assaulted in alleged hate crime in Minnesota
title_zh: 索马里裔美国优步司机因涉嫌仇恨犯罪在明尼苏达州遭到残酷袭击

summary_zh: 穆罕默德·优素福 (Mohamed Yusuf) 据称遭到乘客袭击，这名乘客称他不喜欢司机的名字，一名索马里裔美国 Uber 司机
body_en: Somali-American Uber driver brutally assaulted in alleged hate crime in Minnesota | Minnesota
Mohamed Yusuf is fighting for his life after alleged attack by passenger who said he did not like driver’s first name
A Somali-American Uber driver was allegedly brutally assaulted by a passenger in Hopkins, Minnesota , on Saturday, in what his family says “appears to be a hate crime”.

The driver, Mohamed Yusuf, is currently hospitalized and fighting for his life, his family told the Somali Brief , a digital news site run by two Somali American journalists . The driver’s cousin, Abdinasir Ali told the outlet that the alleged attack took place early Saturday after a passenger in Hopkins, a suburban city south-west of Minneapolis, asked Yusuf’s name and then said he did not like the name Mohamed.

The passenger allegedly then choked the driver from behind, took control of the car and used it to assault the driver. “He was run over multiple times with his own vehicle,” Yusuf’s son, Mustafa Osman, told the Somali Brief.
The badly injured driver was later found “a mile down the road in a ditch”, with broken legs and ribs, two collapsed lungs and a spinal injury, his son said.
The Hopkins police department said in a statement they are investigating the assault after officers responded to a report of a suspicious vehicle at 1.20am on Saturday.

“Officers located an adult male suspect nearby and took him into custody,” the police department stated. They noted preliminary information indicates the incident involved an Uber ride share interaction and that the investigation remains ongoing.
“This is a pure hate crime,” one member of Yusuf’s family at the hospital told the Somali Brief. “Our politicians created this hostile environment.”

The alleged assault comes after Donald Trump made racist rhetoric and lies about Somali Americans in Minnesota a central focus of his midterm campaign rallies, and the president’s inflammatory claims have been echoed by Minnesota Republicans.
House majority whip Tom Emmer of Minnesota, recently said on a conservative podcast: “I’ve got basically the Somali civil war that’s come to the state of Minnesota.”

The Minnesota chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (Cair-MN), community leaders, elected officials and ride-share driver groups were planning a press conference on Monday at the Hennepin County Medical Center to call for justice.

“Mohamed Yusuf should be home safe with his family, not fighting for his life after an attack fueled by hatred towards his Somali identity,” said Omar Fateh, a state senator in Minnesota, in a statement on social media. “We need answers and an immediate and transparent investigation.”

SEIU Local 26, a local labor union that organizes rideshare drivers, said in a social media post on the alleged attack: “We are shocked, angered and saddened by the news of the alleged attack that happened this weekend on Mohamed, a Minnesotan and Uber driver.”

A GoFundMe created on behalf of Yusuf and his family has already raised over $140,000. “As a result of this senseless assault, he suffered severe injuries and is now in a coma, fighting for his life,” the family wrote in the appeal for financial support.
“We are shocked and horrified by the details of this senseless attack,” a spokesperson for Uber said in an email.
“We banned the rider from the Uber platform, and we are keeping the driver and his loved ones in our thoughts. We stand ready to assist law enforcement with their investigation.”
body_zh: 索马里裔美国优步司机在明尼苏达州因涉嫌仇恨犯罪而遭到残酷袭击明尼苏达州
穆罕默德·优素福（Mohamed Yusuf）因声称不喜欢司机的名字而遭到乘客袭击，目前正在为自己的生命而战
据称，一名索马里裔美国优步司机周六在明尼苏达州霍普金斯市遭到一名乘客的残酷袭击，他的家人称这“似乎是仇恨犯罪”。
司机穆罕默德·优素福（Mohamed Yusuf）的家人告诉《索马里简报》（Somali Brief），该网站是由两名索马里裔美国记者运营的数字新闻网站，他目前正在医院接受治疗，正在为生命而战。司机的表弟阿卜迪纳西尔·阿里告诉媒体，所谓的袭击发生在周六早些时候，当时明尼阿波利斯西南部郊区城市霍普金斯的一名乘客询问优素福的名字，然后说他不喜欢穆罕默德这个名字。
据称，这名乘客随后从后面掐住了司机的脖子，控制了汽车并用它袭击了司机。优素福的儿子穆斯塔法·奥斯曼 (Mustafa Osman) 告诉《索马里简报》，“他多次被自己的车辆碾压”。
他的儿子说，这名受重伤的司机后来被发现“在路边一英里的沟里”，他的腿和肋骨骨折，两个肺部塌陷，脊椎受伤。
霍普金斯警察局在一份声明中表示，周六凌晨 1 点 20 分，警察接到可疑车辆的报告后，他们正在调查这起袭击事件。
警察局表示：“警方在附近找到了一名成年男性嫌疑人并将其拘留。”他们指出，初步信息表明该事件涉及优步拼车互动，调查仍在进行中。
“这是纯粹的仇恨犯罪，”优素福在医院的家人告诉《索马里简报》。 “我们的政客创造了这种敌对的环境。”
唐纳德·特朗普将有关明尼苏达州索马里裔美国人的种族主义言论和谎言作为其中期竞选集会的中心焦点，而总统的煽动性言论得到了明尼苏达州共和党人的响应。
明尼苏达州众议院多数党党鞭汤姆·埃默最近在一个保守派播客上表示：“我基本上已经看到索马里内战已经蔓延到明尼苏达州了。”
美国伊斯兰关系委员会 (Cair-MN) 明尼苏达州分会、社区领袖、民选官员和拼车司机团体计划周一在亨内平县医疗中心举行新闻发布会，呼吁伸张正义。
明尼苏达州参议员奥马尔·法塔赫在社交媒体上的一份声明中表示：“穆罕默德·优素福应该安全地与家人在一起，而不是在因索马里身份的仇恨而遭到袭击后为生命而战。” “我们需要答案以及立即、透明的调查。”
SEIU Local 26 是一个组织拼车司机的当地工会，在社交媒体上就这起袭击事件发帖表示：“我们对本周末发生在明尼苏达州和 Uber 司机穆罕默德身上的据称袭击事件感到震惊、愤怒和悲伤。”
代表 Yusuf 及其家人创建的 GoFundMe 已经筹集了超过 14 万美元。 “由于这次毫无意义的袭击，他受了重伤，现在处于昏迷状态，正在为生命而战，”家人在寻求经济支持的呼吁中写道。
Uber 发言人在一封电子邮件中表示：“我们对这一毫无意义的攻击的细节感到震惊和恐惧。”
“我们禁止该乘客使用 Uber 平台，我们会时刻关注这名司机和他的亲人。我们随时准备协助执法部门进行调查。”

title_en: Texas puts to death man who beheaded three children, hours after Oklahoma execution
title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州执行死刑几小时后，得克萨斯州处决了斩首三名儿童的男子
summary: Oklahoma man, 73, executed for killing ex’s estranged husband, as US nears 40 executions for second straight year A Texas man convicted of fatally stabbing and beheading his three young children in a squalid, windowless apartment in 2003 was recently executed.
summary_zh: 俄克拉荷马州 73 岁男子因杀害前夫分居的丈夫而被处决，美国连续第二年处决 40 人 德克萨斯州一名男子被判犯有致命罪
body_en: Oklahoma man, 73, executed for killing ex’s estranged husband, as US nears 40 executions for second straight year
A Texas man convicted of fatally stabbing and beheading his three young children in a squalid, windowless apartment in 2003 was recently executed.

John Allen Rubio, 46, was pronounced dead at 6.47 pm on Thursday after a lethal injection at the state prison in Huntsville, Texas. His killings of his baby girl and two toddlers so rocked the city of Brownsville on the US border with Mexico that the apartment building was later demolished – and the land turned into a park and community garden.

After a spiritual adviser prayed over him briefly, Rubio thanked friends and family for their “love and understanding” and said he was “not the same person I once was”. He thanked prison staff for teaching him how to find God and also expressed love for Angela Camacho, his common-law wife who is serving life in prison for her role in the slayings.
“I want to say I’m sorry to my wife’s family,” he said. “I can’t change the past but I can tell you my life is going to be over. But that’s not going to make you happy.”
Former death row prisoners call Byron Donalds to halt future Florida executions
“I’m going to be with my kids in a little bit,” he added. “I’m ready to go to heaven to be with my lord and savior.”

As the lethal dose of the sedative pentobarbital began taking effect, Rubio took three breaths and began what sounded like snoring. All movement ceased after, and a physician pronounced him dead 21 minutes after the injection began.

Also on Thursday, 73-year-old James Pavatt received a lethal injection at an Oklahoma prison for the fatal shooting of his girlfriend’s estranged husband in 2001. The victim was killed as he arrived to pick up his two young children before Thanksgiving.
Thursday’s executions were the 36th and 37th this year, with the US on track to surpass 40 executions for a second consecutive year – a pace driven by Florida .

The death penalty has drawn renewed attention since the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee in September. And on 5 November, California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, announced he would commute hundreds of death sentences before leaving office in January – what experts say would be the largest mass clemency in American history.

In Texas , Rubio and Camacho were accused of killing three-year-old Julissa Quesada, 14-month-old John E Rubio and two-month-old Mary Jane Rubio in the apartment they shared in Brownsville. Camacho received a life sentence after pleading guilty.

An appeals court overturned Rubio’s first capital murder conviction, ruling Camacho’s statements were improperly admitted as evidence in his trial. At his second trial, Rubio again pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity but again was convicted and sentenced to death.
According to court records, Rubio wasn’t the biological father of the two older children but raised them as his own.
At various points, Rubio claimed the children were possessed and that he was the “chosen one” intended to save the world.

Defense experts diagnosed him with paranoid schizophrenia, a finding prosecution experts rejected. The defense experts also testified his childhood – marked by violence at home, “toxic” parents, drug use and prostitution – damaged him developmentally.
Gavin Newsom commutes more than 500 death sentences in California

Meanwhile, in Oklahoma , Pavatt was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder in the killing of Rob Andrew, a 39-year-old advertising executive. Pavatt attended the same church as the Andrew family and had been having an affair with Rob Andrew’s wife, Brenda Andrew. She was convicted at a separate trial and is the only woman currently on Oklahoma’s death row.

Weeks before the shooting, Rob Andrew told police someone was trying to kill him after the brake lines on his car were cut. Brenda Andrew told police after her husband was killed that masked intruders shot her in the arm and fatally shot him.
body_zh: 俄克拉荷马州73岁男子因杀害前夫分居丈夫而被处决，美国连续第二年处决40人
一名得克萨斯州男子于 2003 年在一间肮脏、无窗的公寓里刺死并斩首了他的三个年幼的孩子，最近被处决。
周四下午 6 点 47 分，46 岁的约翰·艾伦·卢比奥 (John Allen Rubio) 在德克萨斯州亨茨维尔州立监狱注射死刑后被宣布死亡。他杀害自己的女婴和两个幼儿，震惊了美国与墨西哥边境的布朗斯维尔市，以至于公寓楼后来被拆除，土地变成了公园和社区花园。
在一位精神顾问为他短暂祈祷后，卢比奥感谢朋友和家人的“爱和理解”，并表示他“不再是以前的我了”。他感谢监狱工作人员教他如何寻找上帝，并表达了对他的普通法妻子安吉拉·卡马乔的爱，她因在屠杀中所扮演的角色而在监狱中终身服刑。
“我想对我妻子的家人说声抱歉，”他说。 “我无法改变过去，但我可以告诉你我的生命即将结束。但这不会让你快乐。”
前死囚呼吁拜伦唐纳德停止未来佛罗里达州的处决
“我很快就会和我的孩子们在一起，”他补充道。 “我已经准备好去天堂与我的主和救世主在一起了。”
当致命剂量的镇静剂戊巴比妥开始生效时，卢比奥吸了三口气，开始打鼾。注射开始 21 分钟后，所有活动都停止了，医生宣布他死亡。
同样在周四，73 岁的詹姆斯·帕瓦特 (James Pavatt) 在俄克拉荷马州的一所监狱因 2001 年枪杀女友分居的丈夫而被注射死刑。受害者在感恩节前去接两个年幼的孩子时被杀。
周四的处决是今年的第 36 起和第 37 起，美国有望连续第二年超过 40 起处决——这一速度由佛罗里达州推动。
自九月份田纳西州克里斯塔·派克处决失败以来，死刑再次引起人们的关注。 11 月 5 日，加利福尼亚州州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 宣布，他将在 1 月份卸任前对数百名死刑犯进行减刑 — — 专家称，这将是美国历史上规模最大的大规模赦免。
在得克萨斯州，卢比奥和卡马乔被指控在布朗斯维尔合住的公寓里杀害了三岁的朱莉莎·克萨达、14个月大的约翰·E·卢比奥和两个月大的玛丽·简·卢比奥。卡马乔认罪后被判处无期徒刑。
上诉法院推翻了卢比奥的首例死刑谋杀罪判决，裁定卡马乔的陈述在审判中被不当接受为证据。在第二次审判中，卢比奥再次以精神错乱为由拒不不认罪，但再次被定罪并判处死刑。
根据法庭记录，卢比奥不是两个大孩子的亲生父亲，而是将他们当作自己的孩子抚养长大。
卢比奥多次声称孩子们被附身，他是旨在拯救世界的“被选中者”。
辩护专家诊断他患有偏执型精神分裂症，但检方专家否认了这一结论。辩护专家还证实，他的童年——以家庭暴力、“有毒”父母、吸毒和卖淫为特征——对他的发育造成了损害。
加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 在加州减刑了 500 多名死刑犯
与此同时，在俄克拉荷马州，帕瓦特因杀害 39 岁的广告主管罗布·安德鲁而被判犯有一级谋杀罪和共谋谋杀罪。帕瓦特与安德鲁一家参加同一家教堂，并与罗布·安德鲁的妻子布伦达·安德鲁有染。她在另一次审判中被定罪，是目前俄克拉荷马州死囚牢房中唯一的女性。
枪击事件发生几周前，罗布·安德鲁告诉警方，在他汽车的刹车线被切断后，有人试图杀死他。布伦达·安德鲁（Brenda Andrew）在她丈夫被杀后告诉警方，蒙面入侵者向她的手臂开枪，并开枪打死了他。

title_en: US judge blocks Trump’s plan to renovate historic DC golf course
title_zh: 美国法官阻止特朗普翻新历史悠久的华盛顿高尔夫球场的计划
summary: Order by judge Ana Reyes is the latest instance of the federal judiciary pushing back against Trump’s efforts to redesign the nation’s capital A federal judge has ordered a temporary suspension of any work at a historic Washington public golf course, in the la
summary_zh: 安娜·雷耶斯法官的命令是联邦司法部门反对特朗普重新设计国家首都的努力的最新实例
body_en: Order by judge Ana Reyes is the latest instance of the federal judiciary pushing back against Trump’s efforts to redesign the nation’s capital

A federal judge has ordered a temporary suspension of any work at a historic Washington public golf course, in the latest setback for US president Donald Trump’s plan to turn it ⁠into a championship-level course.

In a 30-page decision, US district judge Ana Reyes temporarily blocked the federal government from moving forward with a plan that would have closed East Potomac Park on Sunday. Trump said in an 18 ⁠October social media post that the closure would last 15 months and transform the park’s golf offerings into “one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World”.
Reyes ruled that the Trump administration’s stated reasons for closing the park were “pretextual” ⁠and that the government violated at least two federal laws “to meet an arbitrary deadline”.
Judge to appoint special master to determine whether Trump lawyers purposely misled her over golf course
“The government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all ​stripes, indefinitely,” Reyes wrote.
The plaintiffs argue that Trump’s plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something the president denies.

Although Reyes ordered that the park – near the Jefferson Memorial, ‌2 miles (3km) south of the ‌White House – remain open, the Trump administration does not have to maintain golf operations at the site, the judge wrote. But the government “cannot use the absence ‌of golf operations as a reason to exclude the public,” she added.

The ruling by Reyes, who was appointed by Joe Biden and whom Trump has called a “lunatic”, is the latest instance of the federal judiciary pushing back against Trump’s sweeping efforts to redesign the nation’s capital through major construction projects.

Many of his projects, including plans for a huge ballroom at the White House , the installation of his own name on the Kennedy Center and construction of a massive arch , have been challenged in courts.
The ruling came in a lawsuit brought by the DC Preservation League, a historic preservation group that says Trump’s plan to redevelop the park violates various federal regulations and statutes.

The group’s lawyers earlier won a ruling from Reyes that blocked the National Park Service, part of the Interior Department, ‌from cutting down trees at the park or making other irreversible modifications without advance notice.

Democracy Forward, which is representing the preservation league and two local residents in the case, said in a statement it was grateful that Reyes stopped “another one of ​the president’s vanity projects”.
The group’s senior legal adviser, Catherine Carroll, said: “The administration’s inexplicable drive to destroy East Potomac Park would have taken away a treasured park that could never be replaced.”
The Interior Department, Justice Department and the White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Judge orders Trump administration to halt work on historic DC golf course

The lawsuit has produced several heated confrontations between Reyes and Justice Department lawyers. The judge said last month that the government’s removal of hundreds of trees from the course and failure to tell the preservation group ⁠about the work “has cost the government all of its credibility” in the case.
Reyes has ordered an ethics investigation into ​whether government lawyers have repeatedly misled her about the timeline for ​the park’s closure.
The Justice Department has accused Reyes ​of overstepping her authority and inappropriately belittling government lawyers. It demanded her recusal from the case, a request she denied.
body_zh: 安娜·雷耶斯法官的命令是联邦司法部门反对特朗普重新设计国家首都的努力的最新例子
一名联邦法官下令暂停华盛顿一座历史悠久的公共高尔夫球场的所有施工，这是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将其打造成锦标赛级球场的计划的最新挫折。
在一份长达 30 页的决定中，美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 暂时阻止联邦政府推进一项将于周日关闭东波托马克公园的计划。特朗普在 10 月 18 日的社交媒体帖子中表示，关闭将持续 15 个月，并将该公园的高尔夫设施转变为“世界上最好、最壮观的高尔夫球场之一”。
雷耶斯裁定，特朗普政府所说的关闭公园的理由是“借口”，并且政府“为了满足任意期限”违反了至少两项联邦法律。
法官将任命特别法官来确定特朗普律师是否故意在高尔夫球场上误导她
雷耶斯写道：“政府提议无限期关闭一座历史悠久的公园，华盛顿各种阶层的人每天都可以享受这个公园。”
原告辩称，特朗普的计划将改变无障碍高尔夫球场的特征，并使其变得难以负担，但总统否认了这一点。
法官写道，尽管雷耶斯下令位于白宫以南 2 英里（3 公里）处的杰斐逊纪念堂附近的公园保持开放，但特朗普政府不必维持该地点的高尔夫运营。但她补充说，政府“不能以没有高尔夫运营作为排除公众的理由”。
雷耶斯由乔·拜登任命，被特朗普称为“疯子”，他的裁决是联邦司法部门反击特朗普通过重大建设项目重新设计国家首都的全面努力的最新实例。
他的许多项目，包括在白宫建造一个巨大宴会厅的计划、在肯尼迪中心安装他自己的名字以及建造一个巨大拱门的计划，都在法庭上受到了质疑。
这项裁决是在华盛顿特区保护联盟提起的诉讼中做出的，该联盟是一个历史保护组织，称特朗普重新开发公园的计划违反了多项联邦法规和法规。
该组织的律师早些时候赢得了雷耶斯的一项裁决，禁止内政部下属的国家公园管理局在没有事先通知的情况下砍伐公园内的树木或进行其他不可逆转的改造。
代表保护联盟和两名当地居民参与此案的民主前进组织在一份声明中表示，它很感激雷耶斯停止了“总统的另一个虚荣项目”。
该组织的高级法律顾问凯瑟琳·卡罗尔表示：“政府莫名其妙地摧毁了东波托马克公园，这将夺走一座永远无法取代的珍贵公园。”
内政部、司法部和白宫没有立即回应置评请求。
法官命令特朗普政府停止历史悠久的华盛顿高尔夫球场的施工
该诉讼在雷耶斯和司法部律师之间引发了多次激烈对抗。法官上个月表示，政府从球场上移走了数百棵树，并且没有向保护组织告知这项工作，“使政府在此案中失去了所有可信度”。
雷耶斯已下令进行道德调查，调查政府律师是否在公园关闭时间表上多次误导她。
司法部指控雷耶斯越权并不当贬低政府律师。它要求她回避此案，但她拒绝了这一要求。

title_en: Trump blasts judge for halting his Washington golf project and says he will appeal
title_zh: 特朗普抨击法官暂停他的华盛顿高尔夫项目，并表示他将上诉
summary: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.
summary_zh: 周六，一名联邦法官下令将距离白宫不远的历史悠久的华盛顿公共高尔夫球场的任何施工推迟两周。
body_en: Trump blasts judge for halting his Washington golf project and says he will appeal A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House.
Temporary fencing is seen at East Potomac Park, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Washington. Tom Brenner/AP hide caption

WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump on Sunday decried a "highly destructive and political decision" from a federal judge after she ordered a two-week delay on renovations at a historic Washington public golf course that he has been trying to redevelop into a championship-level venue.

In a social media post, Trump said his administration will "immediately appeal, on an expedited basis" the temporary restraining order from U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes, which she issued just before East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months.
The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?

"It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court," said Trump, who spent much of the weekend posting photos on his social media site of the golf course. "They don't call it Trash Island for no reason!"

Trump had announced work on the site along the Potomac River would begin that day despite the legal challenge initiated against the project in February by the DC Preservation League and two local golfers.

The plaintiffs argue that the president's plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something Trump has denied. They had sought the stop-work order, saying that closing the course and launching work on the project would "irreparably injure plaintiffs and the public interest."

The president's public announcements on social media last month outlining the date of the closure of East Potomac Park and linking it to the renovation of the golf course weighed heavily in the judge's decision.

Reyes, in her ruling Saturday, noted that those posts presented a problem for the government, indicating that Trump's redevelopment plan was final and that the National Park Service "will close the Park to implement it."
Both points, she wrote, "favor granting Plaintiffs' motion for another temporary restraining order."

The order is in effect through Nov. 28. The park's redevelopment is one of multiple projects in the nation's capital that Trump has championed to remake the city. They include a large memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, among others.

Reyes' order was the latest in a series of rulings in lawsuits challenging Trump's projects that were issued just hours before construction was expected to begin. A different judge recently ordered a 14-day delay on work for the arch, a decision that came shortly after a key planning commission stacked with Trump appointees approved plans for the project.

body_zh: 特朗普谴责法官叫停了他的华盛顿高尔夫项目，并表示他将上诉。周六，一名联邦法官下令将距离白宫不远的一座历史悠久的华盛顿公共高尔夫球场的所有工程推迟两周。
2026 年 11 月 14 日星期六，华盛顿东波托马克公园设置了临时围栏。汤姆·布伦纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
华盛顿——周日，唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责一名联邦法官做出的“极具破坏性和政治性的决定”，此前她下令推迟两周对华盛顿一座历史悠久的公共高尔夫球场进行翻修，而特朗普一直试图将这座高尔夫球场改造成冠军级场馆。
特朗普在社交媒体帖子中表示，他的政府将“立即快速上诉”美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯的临时限制令，她是在东波托马克高尔夫球场周日关闭 15 个月之前发布的。
政府表示将于周日关闭一个受人喜爱的华盛顿公园。法官会介入吗？
特朗普说：“它处于年久失修的可怕状态，任何人只要看看现在在全国各地和法庭上流传的照片就可以看出这一点。”周末的大部分时间他都在自己的社交媒体网站上发布高尔夫球场的照片。 “他们不会无缘无故地称它为垃圾岛！”
尽管华盛顿特区保护联盟和两名当地高尔夫球手在二月份对该项目提出了法律挑战，但特朗普仍宣布波托马克河沿岸工地的施工将于当天开始。
原告辩称，总统的计划将改变无障碍高尔夫球场的特征，使其变得难以负担，但特朗普否认了这一点。他们曾寻求停工令，称关闭路线并启动该项目将“对原告和公共利益造成不可挽回的损害”。
总统上个月在社交媒体上发布的公告概述了东波托马克公园的关闭日期，并将其与高尔夫球场的翻修联系起来，这对法官的决定产生了重大影响。
雷耶斯在周六的裁决中指出，这些帖子给政府带来了问题，表明特朗普的重建计划已经最终确定，国家公园管理局“将关闭公园以实施该计划”。
她写道，这两点“都赞成批准原告提出的另一项临时限制令动议”。
该命令的有效期至 11 月 28 日。该公园的重建是特朗普倡导的重建城市的多个项目之一。其中包括大型纪念拱门、白宫宴会厅和约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心等。
雷耶斯的命令是针对特朗普项目的一系列诉讼裁决中的最新一项，这些裁决是在预计施工开始前几个小时发布的。另一位法官最近下令拱门施工推迟 14 天，这一决定是在由特朗普任命的重要规划委员会批准该项目计划后不久做出的。
