title_en: Trump's border crackdown faces a new blue wall of governors and House members
title_zh: 特朗普的边境镇压面临州长和众议院议员的新蓝墙
summary: Voters have handed Democrats every House district touching Mexico and all four border-state governorships. Why it matters: Starting next year, the sweep gives Democrats new leverage over state resources, border spending and legal challenges during President Tr
summary_zh: 选民已将涉及墨西哥的每个众议院选区以及所有四个边境州的州长职位都交给了民主党人。为什么重要：从明年开始，瑞典
body_en: Voters have handed Democrats every House district touching Mexico and all four border-state governorships.
Why it matters: Starting next year, the sweep gives Democrats new leverage over state resources, border spending and legal challenges during President Trump's final two years.
By the numbers: Democrats last held all four governorships — California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas — in January 1979, according to National Governors Association records .
10 for 10: Democrats swept all 10 House districts touching Mexico for the first time since 2008, according to an Associated Press analysis .
Three flips: JoAnna Mendoza ousted Republican Rep. Juan Ciscomani in Arizona. Bobby Pulido and Katy Padilla Stout flipped Republican-held seats in Texas.
Four attorneys general: Democrats also won the top legal offices in all four border states, including Texas , where the party hadn't won an attorney general race since 1994.

State of play: Trump built his immigration crackdown around the southern border. He declared a national emergency on his first day back, expanded the military's role and border barriers, and launched a sweeping deportation campaign.
Southwest border apprehensions dropped roughly 91% in the 12 months through August compared with Biden's final 12 months, according to FactCheck.org's October analysis .
The crackdown has also reached further into American communities, with ICE arrests surging during the summer of 2026.
Zoom in: Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa's defeat of Gov. Greg Abbott could bring the most immediate border changes.
Abbott spent about $11 billion on Operation Lone Star, deploying state police and National Guard troops and building Rio Grande barriers, according to the Texas Tribune .
Hinojosa, Texas' first Latina governor-elect, has questioned that spending. She can rethink state deployments and enforcement priorities, though existing laws and federal authority limit her options.
Democrats also flipped the Texas House and elected a Democratic attorney general, giving Hinojosa allies in funding and legal battles. Republicans retained the state Senate.
The intrigue: Outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed more than 20 lawsuits against Democratic immigration policies and defended Gov. Greg Abbott's border crackdown.
His Democratic successor, Nathan Johnson, has vowed to challenge unconstitutional federal border tactics — potentially turning the office from a powerful Trump ally into an adversary.

What we're watching: Several Democrats newly elected to represent border districts in Washington campaigned on both strong border security and pathways to citizenship for longtime undocumented immigrants.

Bobby Pulido, who flipped a Texas GOP-held seat, said in his launch video : "Yes, we have to get the criminals out and secure the border. But we can do that without destroying families and our South Texas economy." He also told the Texas Tribune that one of his congressional priorities will be codifying a pathway to citizenship.
JoAnna Mendoza, who flipped an Arizona seat, also backs a strong border and legal pathways to citizenship.

An October N+ Univision/YouGov survey found 56% of Texas Hispanic voters thought immigration enforcement had gone too far. Yet 62% wanted border security and a pathway to citizenship for longtime undocumented immigrants pursued together — suggesting Democrats can make gains without abandoning enforcement.
Zoom out: Trump's tariffs and immigration crackdown have rattled businesses that depend on trade and shoppers from Mexico, giving Democratic governors another reason to challenge Washington.
body_zh: 选民已将涉及墨西哥的每个众议院选区以及所有四个边境州的州长职位都交给了民主党人。
重要性：从明年开始，这次横扫将给民主党在特朗普总统最后两年的国家资源、边境支出和法律挑战方面带来新的影响力。
从数字来看：根据全国州长协会的记录，民主党最后一次担任全部四个州长——加利福尼亚州、亚利桑那州、新墨西哥州和德克萨斯州——是在 1979 年 1 月。
10 对 10：据美联社分析，民主党自 2008 年以来首次横扫涉及墨西哥的全部 10 个众议院选区。
三个翻转：乔安娜·门多萨 (JoAnna Mendoza) 驱逐了亚利桑那州的共和党众议员胡安·西斯科马尼 (Juan Ciscomani)。鲍比·普利多 (Bobby Pulido) 和凯蒂·帕迪拉·斯托特 (Katy Padilla Stout) 推翻了共和党在德克萨斯州占据的席位。
四位总检察长：民主党还赢得了所有四个边境州的最高法律职位，其中包括德克萨斯州，该党自 1994 年以来就没有在该州的总检察长竞选中获胜。
现状：特朗普在南部边境周围展开了移民镇压行动。他回来的第一天就宣布全国进入紧急状态，扩大了军队的作用和边境屏障，并发起了全面的驱逐行动。
根据 FactCheck.org 10 月份的分析，与拜登上任后的最后 12 个月相比，截至 8 月份的 12 个月内，西南边境的逮捕人数下降了约 91%。
打击行动还进一步深入到美国社区，2026 年夏季 ICE 逮捕人数激增。
放大：德克萨斯州民主党人吉娜·伊诺霍萨击败州长格雷格·阿博特可能会带来最直接的边界变化。
据《德克萨斯论坛报》报道，阿博特在“孤星行动”上花费了约 110 亿美元，部署了州警察和国民警卫队，并修建了里奥格兰德路障。
德克萨斯州首位拉丁裔当选州长伊诺霍萨对这一支出提出了质疑。尽管现有法律和联邦权力限制了她的选择，但她可以重新考虑州部署和执法优先事项。
民主党还推翻了德克萨斯州众议院，并选举了一位民主党总检察长，这为伊诺霍萨在资金和法律斗争中提供了盟友。共和党保留了州参议院的席位。
阴谋：即将离任的得克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿针对民主党移民政策提起了 20 多起诉讼，并为州长格雷格·阿博特的边境镇压行为进行了辩护。
他的民主党继任者内森·约翰逊(Nathan Johnson)发誓要挑战违宪的联邦边境策略——这可能会使该办公室从特朗普的强大盟友变成对手。
我们正在关注的内容：新当选代表华盛顿边境地区的几名民主党人在竞选活动中主张加强边境安全和为长期无证移民提供公民身份的途径。
推翻德克萨斯州共和党席位的鲍比·普利多(Bobby Pulido)在他的启动视频中表示：“是的，我们必须把犯罪分子赶出去并确保边境安全。但我们可以在不破坏家庭和南德克萨斯州经济的情况下做到这一点。”他还告诉《德克萨斯论坛报》，他的国会优先事项之一将是编纂获得公民身份的途径。
乔安娜·门多萨 (JoAnna Mendoza) 推翻了亚利桑那州的一个席位，她也支持强有力的边境和获得公民身份的合法途径。
N+ Univision/YouGov 10 月份的一项调查发现，56% 的德克萨斯州拉美裔选民认为移民执法做得太过分了。然而，62% 的人希望共同追求边境安全和长期无证移民获得公民身份的途径——这表明民主党可以在不放弃执法的情况下取得成果。
缩小范围：特朗普的关税和移民打击令依赖墨西哥贸易和购物者的企业感到不安，这给了民主党州长挑战华盛顿的另一个理由。

title_en: Two planes collide on taxiway at Miami airport one day after national grounding
title_zh: 国家停飞一天后，两架飞机在迈阿密机场滑行道上相撞
summary: Two people injured after wingtip of Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck nose of United Parcel Service Boeing 767 Two planes collided with one another on a taxiway at Miami’s international airport on Saturday night – a day after the Federal Aviation Administration
summary_zh: 巴拿马航空波音 737 飞机翼尖撞上联合包裹服务公司波音 767 机头，造成两人受伤 两架飞机在一架飞机上相撞
body_en: Two people injured after wingtip of Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck nose of United Parcel Service Boeing 767

Two planes collided with one another on a taxiway at Miami’s international airport on Saturday night – a day after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued an hours-long nationwide ground stop due to communication issues affecting multiple air traffic control centers.

In a statement, the Trump administration-led FAA said the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a United Parcel Service Boeing 767 “while the airplanes were taxiing at Miami International Airport”.
Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage
Two people reportedly had minor injuries in the collision and subsequently received medical treatment.
The FAA said it was investigating the matter, which was reported at about 9pm local time.

According to the FAA, air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight before the collision. “The Copa flight was taxiing to the gate and the UPS flight was taxiing for departure to Bogotá, Colombia,” the FAA said.
A passenger on the Copa flight, Cesar Ferreira, spoke to CNN about how screams from those around him clued him in to the emergency.

“We were taxiing after landing at a normal speed when, all of a sudden, I heard the chatter around me getting louder – followed by a collective scream and then the impact of another aircraft hitting ours,” Ferreira said. “Inside the cabin, we felt the plane jerk abruptly sideways. At first, some passengers started freaking out, but the Copa crew reacted quickly, getting everyone to remain seated.”
Copa Airlines said in a statement that it “regrets the disruption this incident may cause our passengers”.
“The safety of our passengers and crew is our top priority, and we will cooperate with authorities as they investigate,” the airline said.
The airport said flights were directed to other taxiways, so airport operations were not affected.

“We are aware of an incident involving one of our aircraft on the ground in Miami ,” UPS said in a statement. “Our crew is safe, and we are committed to working with authorities to determine what happened. The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority.”

The weekend was marked by thousands of flight delays and cancelations in the wake of a four-hour FAA ground stop on Friday which the Trump administration said stemmed from routine but botched maintenance aiming to switch telecommunication lines from old copper wire to fiber optic cables.

Trump administration transportation secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday and Sunday blamed the need for the maintenance on a lack of congressional funding – though critics have said the White House has not spent the money it has been apportioned to upgrade the infrastructure supporting the US’s air travel system.
body_zh: 巴拿马航空波音 737 的翼尖撞上联合包裹服务公司波音 767 的机头，造成两人受伤
周六晚上，两架飞机在迈阿密国际机场的滑行道上相撞。一天前，由于影响多个空中交通管制中心的通信问题，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 发布了长达数小时的全国地面停飞令。
特朗普政府领导的美国联邦航空局在一份声明中表示，巴拿马航空公司一架波音 737 飞机的翼尖撞到了联合包裹服务公司一架波音 767 飞机的机头，“当时飞机正在迈阿密国际机场滑行”。
交通部长肖恩·达菲指责前任总统和国会造成航班中断
据报道，两人在碰撞中受轻伤，随后接受了治疗。
美国联邦航空局表示正在调查此事，消息于当地时间晚上 9 点左右报道。
据美国联邦航空局称，在碰撞发生前，空中交通管制员已告知 UPS 机组人员为 Copa 航班让路。美国联邦航空局表示：“Copa 航班正在滑行至登机口，UPS 航班正在滑行，准备飞往哥伦比亚波哥大。”
巴拿马杯航班上的一名乘客塞萨尔·费雷拉 (Cesar Ferreira) 向美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 讲述了周围人的尖叫声如何让他意识到紧急情况。
费雷拉说：“我们以正常速度着陆后滑行，突然，我听到周围的说话声越来越大，随后是集体尖叫声，然后是另一架飞机撞上我们的飞机。” “在机舱内，我们感觉到飞机突然向一侧猛烈地晃动。起初，一些乘客开始惊慌失措，但 Copa 机组人员反应很快，让所有人都留在座位上。”
巴拿马航空公司在一份声明中表示，“对这一事件可能给我们的乘客造成的干扰感到遗憾”。
该航空公司表示：“乘客和机组人员的安全是我们的首要任务，我们将配合当局进行调查。”
机场表示，航班被引导至其他滑行道，因此机场运营没有受到影响。
UPS 在一份声明中表示：“我们了解到我们的一架飞机在迈阿密地面上发生了一起事件。” “我们的船员很安全，我们致力于与当局合作确定发生了什么。我们员工和公众的安全是我们的首要任务。”
上周五美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 进行了四个小时的地面停留后，周末出现了数千次航班延误和取消，特朗普政府表示，这是由于旨在将电信线路从旧铜线更换为光纤电缆的例行但拙劣的维护所致。
特朗普政府交通部长肖恩·达菲（Sean Duffy）周六和周日将维护的需要归咎于缺乏国会资金，尽管批评人士表示，白宫尚未花费分配的资金来升级支持美国航空旅行系统的基础设施。

title_en: Trump's handpicked party chair faces a rebellion as midterm losses challenge president's grip on GOP
title_zh: 中期选举失败挑战总统对共和党的控制，特朗普亲自挑选的党主席面临叛乱
summary: A rebellion is forming against President Donald Trump’s handpicked chairman at the Republican National Committee
summary_zh: 针对唐纳德·特朗普总统亲自挑选的共和党全国委员会主席的叛乱正在形成
body_en: A rebellion is forming against President Donald Trump’s handpicked chairman at the Republican National Committee
By STEVE PEOPLES Associated Press and JILL COLVIN Associated Press
NEW YORK -- A nascent rebellion is underway against President Donald Trump's handpicked chairman at the Republican National Committee, and it’s already getting ugly.

Some members are calling for a forensic audit of spending decisions, including hair and makeup services for Trump and other officials, as well as the hiring of the daughter of Trump's former chief of staff . Feuding Republicans are leaking emails and opposition research on rival factions. The White House is threatening to cut off fundraising assistance if the rebels don’t fall in line.

The emerging fight, which will shape the 2028 presidential nominating contest, represents a rare challenge to Trump's dominance, even after the party's worst midterm performance in a generation. Despite the heavy losses , Republican leaders across Washington have shown little desire to move past Trump and have largely stood behind his most unpopular policies.

But inside the RNC, an organization of 168 members elected from every state who oversee the party’s national political operation, a small yet growing group is backing an attempt to depose Joe Gruters . Trump wants to keep him in charge.

The dissidents are rallying behind Kentucky’s KC Crosbie, the RNC's second-in-command, who launched her bid just two days after the Nov. 3 election in a letter that drew the fury of both the White House and Gruters' allies.
Crosbie remains a vocal Trump supporter who backs his “Make America Great Again” agenda, but her opponents view her gambit as a direct challenge to the president and his power.

“We have an obligation to serve the Republican Party the most effective way we can. And if all we do is say yes to what the White House wants, I’m not sure that’s doing what’s best for the Republican Party,” said RNC member Oscar Brock of Tennessee, who is supporting Crosbie’s candidacy. “Our job is to elect Republicans broadly, not to support one man all the time.”
He said that requires a change in leadership.
“There’s so much frustration that Chairman Gruters didn’t pull his weight in this election, that the RNC was far less effective than it should have been,” he said.
In her letter, Crosbie described the midterms as “a serious setback" and called for the RNC to provide “an honest account” of what went wrong.
“We should preserve what we built and be equally willing to confront where we fell short,” she wrote.
Crosbie declined to be interviewed. The leadership election will be held in January at the RNC’s winter meeting in Arizona.

It’s unclear how many RNC members will back Crosbie, although the number so far is believed to be small. Some would-be supporters privately acknowledge that they're worried about a backlash from the White House, especially with Stephen Miller taking over as Trump's new White House chief of staff. Others believe in the committee's tradition of having presidents pick their own party chiefs.

Lauren LePage, an RNC member from Maine, praised the chairman's leadership and his efforts to help her father, Paul LePage, flip a congressional seat — a rare bright spot for Republicans this election cycle.
She described Gruters as “highly responsive” during the campaign and praised his “record-setting fundraising."
“From my perspective, as chairman, he did his job," she said, adding that Trump's endorsement is “something that the committee should take very seriously.”
Nevada Republican Party Chairman Michael McDonald called Crosbie a “dear friend," but said Trump is “the leader of our party” and “you always have to fall in line with the leader.”
body_zh: 针对唐纳德·特朗普总统亲自挑选的共和党全国委员会主席的叛乱正在形成
作者：STEVE PEOPLES 美联社和 JILL COLVIN 美联社
纽约——一场针对唐纳德·特朗普总统亲自挑选的共和党全国委员会主席的反抗正在兴起，而且已经变得越来越丑陋。
一些成员呼吁对支出决定进行法证审计，包括特朗普和其他官员的发型和化妆服务，以及雇用特朗普前幕僚长的女儿。争斗不断的共和党人正在泄露有关敌对派系的电子邮件和反对派研究报告。如果叛军不听话，白宫威胁将切断筹款援助。
这场即将影响 2028 年总统提名竞赛的斗争，即使在该党经历了一代人以来最糟糕的中期表现之后，也对特朗普的统治地位构成了罕见的挑战。尽管损失惨重，华盛顿各地的共和党领导人并没有表现出超越特朗普的意愿，并且在很大程度上支持他最不受欢迎的政策。
但在共和党全国委员会（RNC）这个由各州选举产生的 168 名成员组成的组织，负责监督该党的全国政治运作时，一个规模虽小但不断壮大的团体正在支持推翻乔·格鲁特斯 (Joe Gruters) 的企图。特朗普想让他继续掌权。
持不同政见者正在团结起来支持肯塔基州的共和党全国委员会二把手克罗斯比(KC Crosbie)，克罗斯比在11月3日大选后两天就发起了竞选，这封信引起了白宫和格鲁特斯盟友的愤怒。
克罗斯比仍然是特朗普的直言不讳的支持者，支持他的“让美国再次伟大”议程，但她的对手认为她的策略是对总统及其权力的直接挑战。
“我们有义务以最有效的方式为共和党服务。如果我们所做的只是答应白宫的要求，我不确定这是否对共和党最有利，”支持克罗斯比候选资格的田纳西州共和党全国委员会成员奥斯卡·布罗克(Oscar Brock)表示。 “我们的工作是广泛选举共和党人，而不是一直支持一个人。”
他说，这需要改变领导层。
他说：“令人非常沮丧的是，格鲁特斯主席在这次选举中没有发挥自己的作用，共和党全国委员会的效率远没有达到应有的水平。”
克罗斯比在信中将中期选举描述为“一次严重的挫折”，并呼吁共和党全国委员会对出现的问题提供“诚实的说明”。
“我们应该保留我们所建立的东西，并同样愿意面对我们的不足，”她写道。
克罗斯比拒绝接受采访。领导人选举将于一月份在亚利桑那州举行的共和党全国委员会冬季会议上举行。
目前尚不清楚有多少共和党全国委员会成员会支持克罗斯比，但据信目前人数还很少。一些潜在的支持者私下承认，他们担心白宫的强烈反对，尤其是斯蒂芬·米勒接任特朗普新任白宫办公厅主任后。其他人则相信该委员会的传统，即由总统挑选自己的党魁。
来自缅因州的共和党全国委员会成员劳伦·勒佩奇(Lauren LePage)赞扬了主席的领导才能以及他为帮助她的父亲保罗·勒佩奇(Paul LePage)翻转国会席位所做的努力——这是共和党本次选举周期中罕见的亮点。
她形容格鲁特斯在竞选期间“反应敏捷”，并赞扬他“创纪录的筹款活动”。
“从我的角度来看，作为主席，他做了他的工作，”她说，并补充说特朗普的支持是“委员会应该非常认真对待的事情。”
内华达州共和党主席迈克尔·麦克唐纳称克罗斯比为“亲爱的朋友”，但表示特朗普是“我们党的领导人”，“你必须始终与领导人保持一致”。

title_en: Poll: Republicans have a MAGA dilemma after their midterm losses
title_zh: 民意调查：共和党在中期失败后面临“让MAGA再次伟大”的困境
summary: For a party that has spent the last decade united around a singular figure, new results from The POLITICO Poll reveal tension over where it should go next.
summary_zh: 对于一个在过去十年里一直团结在一个单一人物周围的政党来说，政治民意调查的新结果揭示了它应该走向何方的紧张局势
body_en: The Republican Party’s midterm wipeout has torn apart President Donald Trump’s coalition.

For months, polling has shown cracks among Trump’s 2024 voters over immigration , the Iran war and the president’s influence. Now, new results from The POLITICO Poll , conducted just days after the election, reveal a deep chasm between Trump’s self-identified MAGA base and the non-MAGA voters who helped fuel his return to the White House.

The two camps hold sharply different interpretations of the GOP’s historic midterm defeat and what comes next for their party, according to the survey conducted by PF Global. MAGA Trump loyalists were more likely to say the president is not to blame for the losses — that things would have gone better if he was on the ballot — and that the party should now move closer to Trump.
Non-MAGA Trump voters starkly disagreed, saying they are ready to move away from him and his unpopular agenda. About one in five said they voted for Democratic candidates this cycle.

The fault line is a fresh warning sign that Republicans, desperate to stitch back together a winning coalition after their midterm calamity, may struggle to keep the voters that powered Trump’s victory in 2024 in the fold.

And it calls into question just how loyal the party should be to a leader — and movement — it has spent the last decade united around. Overall, just over half of all Trump voters said the president will be able to make a comeback from the election losses.
“As the [GOP] spends the next two years figuring out who it is and what it stands for, these divisions will only be further exposed,” said Republican strategist Doug Heye.
Here are four charts that show just how much the midterms have divided Trump’s own voters.

A majority of non-MAGA Trump voters blamed Republicans' loss of the House and the Senate on Trump’s actions since taking office, with far fewer saying the campaigns themselves were responsible. A 59% majority also said the president is a loser of the midterms, a striking rebuke from a group of voters who helped his return to the White House.
But MAGA Trump voters are torn over who they blame for their losses.

The divide mirrors disagreements happening at the top levels of the Republican Party. In the immediate aftermath of the election, some Republicans, at least tepidly, began pointing fingers at the president. Others have called for a “reckoning” without explicitly laying the blame at Trump’s feet or articulating an alternative vision for the GOP.

“There is no way to sugarcoat what happened on Election Day. From coast to coast, and in some of the reddest parts of the country, Republicans were humiliated,” 31 Republican National Committee members wrote in a letter to GOP lawmakers this week.

Trump, who ahead of the midterms repeatedly urged voters to “pretend” he was on the ballot, insisted in a Truth Social post after the election that, “I JUST WASN’T ON THE BALLOT. IF I WERE, WE WOULD HAVE WON IN A LANDSLIDE!”

“President Trump will never stop delivering results for the American people and he will undoubtedly go down as the most successful and consequential president in American history,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement.
As Republican Party leaders grapple with how to rebound from the midterms, MAGA isn’t ready to move on from Trump: They said the path forward is embracing Trump and his agenda.
Non-MAGA Trump voters said the opposite — and nearly half of them think their Republican candidates should have broken with the president on the economy this cycle.

“It is very clear that Election Day 2026 was an unequivocal rebuke of Donald Trump, both him personally and his policies,” said one national GOP operative who worked on midterm races, granted anonymity to speak candidly about the landscape. “MAGA needs a serious rebrand if it is going to have any success in the future.”

That presents a complicated picture for Republican leaders, who will have to find a way to appeal to Trump’s fiercely loyal MAGA base without alienating the less committed voters who helped deliver his 2024 victory.

On Election Night, as the scale of Republican losses was becoming clear, POLITICO asked GOP operatives who worked on midterm races whether the defeat meant it was time for Republicans to consider a new vision for the party.
“How can it not be?” one person responded. It’s “the worst defeat a party has taken in 50 years.”
body_zh: 共和党中期选举的惨败导致唐纳德·特朗普总统的联盟四分五裂。
几个月来，民意调查显示，特朗普的 2024 年选民在移民、伊朗战争和总统影响力等问题上存在分歧。现在，选举几天后进行的《政治民意调查》的新结果揭示了特朗普自称的“让MAGA”的支持者与帮助他重返白宫的非“MAGA”选民之间存在深刻的分歧。
PF Global 进行的调查显示，两大阵营对共和党历史性中期失败以及该党下一步的发展持有截然不同的解读。 MAGA 特朗普的忠实支持者更有可能表示，总统不应为失败负责——如果他参加选票，情况会更好——而且该党现在应该向特朗普靠拢。
非“让特朗普再次伟大”的选民坚决不同意，称他们准备放弃他和他不受欢迎的议程。大约五分之一的人表示，他们在本周期投票给了民主党候选人。
这条断层线是一个新的警告信号，表明在中期灾难后急于组建获胜联盟的共和党人可能很难留住那些推动特朗普在 2024 年获胜的选民。
这让人质疑该党应该对过去十年团结起来的领导人和运动有多忠诚。总体而言，超过一半的特朗普选民表示，总统将能够从选举失利中东山再起。
共和党策略师道格·海耶表示：“随着[共和党]在接下来的两年里弄清楚自己是谁、代表什么，这些分歧只会进一步暴露。”
以下四张图表显示了中期选举对特朗普自己选民的分歧有多大。
大多数非“让特朗普再次伟大”的选民将共和党在众议院和参议院的失利归咎于特朗普上任以来的行为，而认为竞选活动本身负有责任的人要少得多。 59%的多数人还表示，总统是中期选举的失败者，这是一群帮助他重返白宫的选民的强烈谴责。
但让特朗普再次伟大的选民对于他们的损失归咎于谁，感到左右为难。
这种分歧反映了共和党高层的分歧。选举结束后，一些共和党人，至少不温不火地开始指责总统。其他人则呼吁进行“清算”，但没有明确将责任归咎于特朗普，也没有为共和党阐明替代愿景。
“没有办法粉饰选举日发生的事情。从一个海岸到另一个海岸，在全国一些最红的地区，共和党人都受到了羞辱，”31 名共和党全国委员会成员本周在给共和党立法者的一封信中写道。
特朗普在中期选举前多次敦促选民“假装”他参加了选票，他在选举后在《真相社会》的一篇帖子中坚称，“我只是没有参加选票。如果我参加了，我们就会以压倒性优势获胜！”
白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔在一份声明中表示：“特朗普总统永远不会停止为美国人民带来成果，他无疑将成为美国历史上最成功、最有影响力的总统。”
当共和党领导人努力解决如何从中期选举中反弹时，MAGA 还没有准备好摆脱特朗普：他们表示，前进的道路是拥抱特朗普和他的议程。
非“让特朗普再次伟大”的选民则持相反观点，其中近一半认为他们的共和党候选人应该在本周期的经济问题上与总统决裂。
“很明显，2026 年选举日是对唐纳德·特朗普个人和政策的明确谴责，”一位从事中期选举工作的全国共和党特工表示，他不愿透露姓名，坦率地谈论了形势。 “如果 MAGA 想要在未来取得成功，就需要进行认真的品牌重塑。”
这对共和党领导人来说是一幅复杂的图景，他们必须找到一种方法来吸引特朗普极其忠诚的 MAGA 基础，同时又不疏远那些帮助他赢得 2024 年胜利的不太忠诚的选民。
在选举之夜，随着共和党损失的规模变得越来越明显，《政治》杂志向从事中期选举工作的共和党工作人员询问，这次失败是否意味着共和党人是时候考虑该党的新愿景了。
“怎么可能不是呢？”一个人回应道。这是“一个政党50年来最严重的失败”。

title_en: Politics chat: Duffy calls for more funding, Democrats plans for accountability
title_zh: 政治聊天：达菲呼吁更多资金，民主党计划问责
summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy demands more money for the country's air travel control systems. Democrats plan for accountability, but not enough of them showed up for an impeachment vote.
summary_zh: 交通部长肖恩·达菲要求为该国的航空旅行控制系统提供更多资金。民主党计划问责，但还不够
body_en: Politics chat: Duffy calls for more funding, Democrats plans for accountability Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy demands more money for the country's air travel control systems. Democrats plan for accountability, but not enough of them showed up for an impeachment vote.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy demands more money for the country's air travel control systems. Democrats plan for accountability, but not enough of them showed up for an impeachment vote.

If you were supposed to fly this weekend, our sympathies are with you, given the disruptions caused by Friday's nationwide ground stop. Federal officials say things should be back to normal by the end of today. Speaking to reporters yesterday, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said communication systems work by a contractor was the culprit, not new AI tools or a cyberattack.
SEAN DUFFY: We don't believe this was cyber at all. This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment.
RASCOE: And that's where we begin with NPR senior national political correspondent Mara Liasson. Good morning, Mara.

RASCOE: Duffy also laid blame on Congress for not giving the FAA more money for upgrades. He's been trying to get $30 billion for months, but on Friday after the ground stop, he demanded 50 billion. Does this crisis increase the chances that he'll get what he's asking for?

LIASSON: Well, that's hard to say. Right now, Republicans, who are in charge of Congress until January, have already approved $12 1/2 billion in that One Big Beautiful Bill for safety upgrades. And ranking Democrats on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee said that the administration has only spent $1 billion of those funds. Meanwhile, the president hasn't spoken publicly or posted about this ground stop or the request for more money.

RASCOE: Democrats are also calling for a full investigation into the ground stop, so that's another one to add to a growing list. But on this issue of accountability, Democrats fell short last week when there weren't enough House Democrats on a procedural vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hesgeth.

LIASSON: That's right, and it wasn't a good look. Eleven Democrats were missing from that vote for various reasons. Several of them have apologized for it. But one thing we've heard in our swing voter focus groups is that voters are worried that Democrats will focus too much effort on investigations and not enough effort on affordability, on bringing prices down.

Democratic leaders say they understand voters want them to focus on affordability first. Congressman Jamie Raskin, who will lead a lot of these investigations, says he wants to make a connection between corruption and high prices and also propose legislative fixes for the problems that the investigations uncover. But there are barriers to what Democrats can do with legislation. They don't have a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate, and President Trump can still veto any bill that both chambers pass.

RASCOE: Before they take charge of Congress, Democrats have to vote on their leadership. So do you think that Hakeem Jeffries is a shoo-in for House speaker or that Chuck Schumer will be the Senate majority leader again? I'm putting you on the spot.

LIASSON: Well, there are Democrats who feel neither Jeffries nor Schumer fought as hard as they should have against Trump for the last two years. But it's hard to imagine that Jeffries won't be elected speaker. He just presided over the most dramatic victory Democratic House members have had in a generation. Even if some progressives in the House caucus want someone else, he has a very big majority. And the majority makers were those blue dogs and centrist Democrats that flipped red state seats. They made the majority in the House, not the liberals.

LIASSON: Well, that's a little different. Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging Schumer. Some Democratic freshmen say they don't want to support Schumer for majority leader. He represents the Democratic establishment. But to his credit, he did recruit the candidates who won in red states and made the new Senate Democratic majority. And as Arizona Senator Ruben Gallego said, when the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract.
RASCOE: And we're still getting results from the election. The big news last week - Mississippi is getting a new Democratic senator.

LIASSON: That's right. This is history-making. Scott Colom will be Mississippi's first Black senator since Reconstruction. This was a race that was won by several thousand votes, one that surprised a lot of people who thought Mississippi was solidly Republican. Still outstanding is Alaska's Senate race. Democrat Mary Peltola has the lead there, but not enough yet to determine if rank choice voting will be triggered.

RASCOE: And President Trump is meeting with Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi this week on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China. This is coming on the heels of the Nvidia scandal. Do you think that'll come up?

LIASSON: The White House says it won't. The White House says Trump is going to discuss the war in Iran and nuclear weapons at the meeting and not bring up former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman who is suspected to be a Chinese spy. The New York Times has reported that Trump was told about this on more than one occasion and did nothing.
body_zh: 政治聊天：达菲呼吁更多资金，民主党计划问责 运输部长肖恩·达菲要求为该国的航空旅行控制系统提供更多资金。民主党人计划追究责任，但没有足够多的人参加弹劾投票。
交通部长肖恩·达菲要求为该国的航空旅行控制系统提供更多资金。民主党人计划追究责任，但没有足够多的人参加弹劾投票。
鉴于周五全国范围内的地面停留造成的干扰，如果您本周末要乘坐飞机，我们对您表示同情。联邦官员表示，到今天年底，情况应该会恢复正常。运输部长肖恩·达菲昨天对记者表示，罪魁祸首是承包商的通信系统，而不是新的人工智能工具或网络攻击。
肖恩·达菲：我们根本不相信这是网络。这是一个不符合当时情况的联邦航空局系统。
拉斯科：这就是我们从 NPR 高级国家政治记者 Mara Liasson 开始的地方。早上好，玛拉。
拉斯科：达菲还指责国会没有给美国联邦航空管理局更多的升级资金。几个月来，他一直试图获得 300 亿美元，但在周五停顿后，他要求获得 500 亿美元。这场危机是否会增加他得到他所要求的东西的机会？
利亚森：嗯，这很难说。目前，负责国会直到一月的共和党人已经批准了一项价值 12.5 亿美元的美丽法案，用于安全升级。众议院交通和基础设施委员会的民主党高层人士表示，政府只花费了其中 10 亿美元。与此同时，总统尚未公开发表讲话或发布有关这一停留或要求更多资金的信息。
拉斯科：民主党人还呼吁对地面站进行全面调查，因此这是另一个要添加到不断增长的名单中的调查。但在问责问题上，民主党上周表现不佳，因为没有足够多的众议院民主党人进行程序性投票来弹劾国防部长皮特·赫斯盖斯。
利亚森：是的，但看起来不太好看。由于各种原因，有 11 名民主党人缺席了这次投票。他们中的一些人已经为此道歉。但我们在摇摆选民焦点小组中听到的一件事是，选民担心民主党会在调查上投入太多精力，而在负担能力和降低价格方面投入不够。
民主党领导人表示，他们理解选民希望他们首先关注负担能力。将领导大量此类调查的国会议员杰米·拉斯金 (Jamie Raskin) 表示，他希望将腐败与高物价联系起来，并针对调查发现的问题提出立法解决方案。但民主党在立法方面存在障碍。他们在参议院没有能够阻止阻挠的多数席位，特朗普总统仍然可以否决参众两院通过的任何法案。
拉斯科：在掌管国会之前，民主党必须对其领导层进行投票。那么，您认为哈基姆·杰弗里斯（Hakeem Jeffries）是众议院议长的必胜者，还是查克·舒默（Chuck Schumer）将再次成为参议院多数党领袖？我把你置于当场。
利亚森：嗯，有些民主党人认为，杰弗里斯和舒默在过去两年里都没有像他们应有的那样努力反对特朗普。但很难想象杰弗里斯不会当选议长。他刚刚主持了民主党众议院议员一代人以来最戏剧性的胜利。即使众议院核心小组中的一些进步人士想要其他人，他也拥有绝大多数。多数票的制定者是那些推翻了红色州席位的蓝狗和中间派民主党人。他们在众议院占多数，而不是自由派。
利亚森：嗯，有点不同。马里兰州参议员克里斯·范霍伦正在挑战舒默。一些民主党新人表示，他们不想支持舒默担任多数党领袖。他代表民主党建制派。但值得赞扬的是，他确实招募了在红色州获胜的候选人，并使新的参议院民主党成为多数派。正如亚利桑那州参议员鲁本·加莱戈所说，当经理带你参加世界职业棒球大赛时，你就给了他另一份合同。
拉斯科：我们仍在获取选举结果。上周的重大新闻 - 密西西比州将迎来一位新的民主党参议员。
利亚森：没错。这是创造历史的。斯科特·科洛姆将成为密西西比州重建以来第一位黑人参议员。这是一场以数千张选票获胜的竞选，这让许多认为密西西比州坚定的共和党人感到惊讶。阿拉斯加州的参议员竞选仍然悬而未决。民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉在这方面领先，但还不足以确定是否会触发排名选择投票。
拉斯科：特朗普总统本周将在中国举行的亚太经合组织峰会期间会见俄罗斯总统普京和中国国家主席习近平。这是继英伟达丑闻之后发生的。你认为这会出现吗？
利亚森：白宫表示不会。白宫表示，特朗普将在会议上讨论伊朗战争和核武器问题，而不会提及英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋与一名疑似中国间谍的女性的恋情。据《纽约时报》报道，特朗普不止一次被告知此事，但他什么也没做。

title_en: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
title_zh: 这是您本周末错过的最大新闻
summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy declined to apologize for the nationwide ground stop on Friday that stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers.
summary_zh: 交通部长肖恩·达菲拒绝就周五全国范围内的地面停车导致数十万旅客滞留一事道歉。
body_en: Nov. 15 – Sean Duffy, Scott Colom and Mike Pence
By Amina Kilpatrick , Mark Hodge and Kayla Hayempour

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy declined to apologize for the nationwide ground stop on Friday that stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers across the country following a router issue that derailed air traffic control communications.

Instead, the secretary blamed his predecessors for “30 years of a lack of investment,” telling NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that previous presidential administrations did not do enough to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system.

“It happened on my watch, but we have to be clear: I am moving at an incredible speed that no one has done at the FAA or in decades, and I’m proud of the work we’re doing, the attention we’re bringing to this issue,” Duffy said.

Federal Aviation Administration contractor L3Harris was working on replacing a copper line with a fiber line at a remote site when the work led a router to overwhelm the national FAA telecommunications network, Duffy said Saturday.

On “Meet the Press,” the transportation secretary reiterated a call he’s made all weekend for more funding from Congress to modernize the nationwide air traffic control system, which has long been outdated and faced problems.
Duffy expects airports and airlines to resume normal operations by the end of the day or early Monday morning.
Sen.-elect Scott Colom says investing in the South can help Democrats
Scott Colom says he notched his upset victory ‘the Mississippi way’: Full interview

Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., emphasized on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that Democrats need to invest more in Southern states like Mississippi , where he flipped a seat blue for the first time in decades.
“What we need to do now as a Democratic Party is understand we can’t continue to allow that lack of investment to occur,” he said.

Colom’s projected win brings Democrats to a 55-seat majority in the Senate, with Alaska’s Senate race yet to be called. His victory over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, a Republican, marked a seismic political shift in a state that last elected a Democrat to the Senate 44 years ago and has not had a Black senator since the Reconstruction period.
Mike Pence says GOP voters ‘didn’t turn left’ but were ‘turned off’ in midterms
Mike Pence says GOP voters ‘didn’t turn left’ but were ‘turned off’ in midterms: Full interview

Former Vice President Mike Pence said on “Meet the Press” he disagrees with Vice President JD Vance’s assessment of Republican midterm losses, saying that the problem Americans have with the Iran war is that the U.S. “stopped short.”
“We sunk their navy, we had complete air superiority, took down 15,000 military sites in Iran. And then, we paused and began to embrace the politics of appeasement,” Pence said.
Why Democrat Mary Peltola is likely to win Alaska’s Senate race
As Alaska continues to count and report votes weeks after Election Day, it is increasingly unlikely that Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan will hang on to his job.

His Democratic challenger, Mary Peltola, is on track to win the still-unresolved Senate race under either possible scenario — with an outright majority, or if the race goes to ranked choice ballots, according to an NBC News Decision Desk analysis of outstanding and tabulated votes.

作者：阿米娜·基尔帕特里克、马克·霍奇和凯拉·海耶姆普尔
周五，由于路由器问题导致空中交通管制通信脱轨，导致全国数十万旅客滞留，运输部长肖恩·达菲拒绝就该次全国性地面停靠道歉。
相反，国务卿指责他的前任“30年来缺乏投资”，并在NBC新闻的“会见媒体”节目中表示，前几届总统政府在国家空中交通管制系统现代化方面做得不够。
达菲说：“这件事发生在我的任期内，但我们必须明确：我正在以令人难以置信的速度前进，这是联邦航空局或几十年来没有人做到的，我为我们正在做的工作以及我们对这个问题的关注感到自豪。”
达菲周六表示，美国联邦航空管理局承包商 L3Harris 正在远程站点用光纤线路替换铜线，结果导致路由器淹没了美国联邦航空局国家电信网络。
在“会见媒体”节目中，交通部长重申了他整个周末发出的呼吁，要求国会提供更多资金，以实现全国空中交通管制系统的现代化，该系统早已过时并面临问题。
达菲预计机场和航空公司将在当天结束或周一凌晨恢复正常运营。
当选参议员斯科特·科洛姆表示，投资南方可以帮助民主党
斯科特·科洛姆表示，他以“密西西比方式”取得了令人沮丧的胜利：完整采访
密西西比州民主党参议员当选参议员斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在 NBC 新闻节目《与媒体会面》中强调，民主党需要在密西西比州等南部各州进行更多投资，他几十年来首次将密西西比州的席位转为蓝色。
“作为民主党，我们现在需要做的是明白，我们不能继续允许投资不足的情况发生，”他说。
科罗姆的预计胜利将使民主党在参议院获得 55 个多数席位，而阿拉斯加的参议院竞选尚未结束。他对共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯的胜利，标志着该州发生了一场巨大的政治转变，该州上次选举民主党参议员是在 44 年前，自重建时期以来就没有黑人参议员。
迈克·彭斯表示共和党选民“没有左转”，但在中期选举中“失去了兴趣”
迈克·彭斯表示共和党选民“没有左转”，但在中期选举中“被关闭”：完整采访
前副总统迈克·彭斯在“会见媒体”节目中表示，他不同意副总统万斯对共和党中期损失的评估，并表示美国人在伊朗战争中遇到的问题是美国“突然停下来”。
“我们击沉了他们的海军，我们拥有完全的空中优势，摧毁了伊朗的 15,000 个军事基地。然后，我们暂停并开始拥抱绥靖政治，”彭斯说。
为什么民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉有可能赢得阿拉斯加参议员竞选
随着阿拉斯加州在选举日几周后继续计票和报告选票，共和党参议员丹·S·沙利文保住自己职位的可能性越来越小。
根据 NBC 新闻决策台对未决选票和列表选票的分析，他的民主党挑战者玛丽·佩尔托拉有望在两种可能的情况下赢得尚未解决的参议院竞选——以绝对多数票，或者如果比赛进入排名选择选票。

title_en: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
title_zh: 政治周：参议院领袖之战；年轻且独立的中期投票率
summary: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.
summary_zh: 美国参议院下一任多数党领袖的争夺反映了中期选举中年轻和独立选民的投票率。
body_en: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.
The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.
Democratic senators gathered in Colorado yesterday, among them, Chris Van Hollen.

CHRIS VAN HOLLEN: This is about answering the call of the American people, because what I'm very afraid of is that their calls to end political corruption, their calls to end a rigged economic system will require that we organize the Senate in a different way.

SIMON: And that's the Maryland senator on his bid to try to replace New York's Chuck Schumer as the Democratic leader in the U.S. Senate. NPR senior contributor Ron Elving joins us. Ron, thanks so much for being with us.
RON ELVING, BYLINE: Good to be with you, Scott.
SIMON: What do you make of the senator's argument here?

ELVING: It has a lot of appeal, especially to younger voters, first-time voters, independents - the people who fueled this extraordinary Democratic surge, especially in the Senate races that Democrats won when nobody thought they were even close. And yes, the voters want an end to corruption and a rigged economy. But when Van Hollen says he wants to organize the Senate in a different way to achieve those ends, does he just mean a new leader, someone other than the longtime leader Chuck Schumer? What else do we know will change? And how do we know it will be better?

Schumer says he has the vote commitments for most of the Senate Democrats already. He needs 29. Some of his allies are saying he'll have 40 votes or more. But Van Hollen still has time to make his case, and in the end, the vote is cast by secret ballot. And I've seen leadership elections in the past where someone claimed to have the votes before they were cast but did not have a majority when the votes were counted.

SIMON: Let me ask about the House. What does it mean that a week after they won a majority, House Democrats couldn't pass a motion to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth because 11 Democrats didn't make it to the chambers to vote, which, of course, is what they're elected to do?

ELVING: There's a lot of anger about this out there, especially among people who wanted the Democrats to do a lot on Day 1. The problem is they won't actually have the majority in the House until January 3, when the new Congress convenes. So Day 1 for the new majority is still seven weeks away.

This week's vote on Hegseth was forced by a rogue Republican but scheduled and managed by the current Republican leadership. They got every other Republican who voted to oppose the impeachment - they are still the majority party. That's what made the difference. But there were no-shows for the vote in both parties. And in the final tally, it appeared that, had all the Democrats gotten there, they could have prevailed. And that, of course, assumes that the current GOP leadership would allow the vote to end that way when they had more Republican votes available, as well.

So how much difference did this vote make? Hegseth will still face investigations and impeachment when the Democrats actually do take over, and then the Senate will need two-thirds to convict and remove him. The Senate is more likely to do that in January with its new Democratic majority than it would have been with its current majority right now.
SIMON: You say Hegseth impeachment will be back on the agenda in January - perhaps also one for Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.?

ELVING: Those two names leap out - Hegseth for Iran, to be sure, but also for his wholesale demotion of generals and admirals and his efforts to instill his notion of warrior culture throughout the armed forces, Kennedy for some recent issues that have come up about his travels, but perhaps mostly because the measles outbreak has brought us fatalities and thousands of new cases, sometimes more than 200 in a week. In the first four years of this decade, we did not see 200 new cases of measles in a whole year.

Now, Trump has stood by both Hegseth and Kennedy in a way he didn't when the pressure was on some other members of his Cabinet, such as Kristi Noem with Homeland Security and Lori Chavez-DeRemer at Labor. So we'll see if he stands by these men in January, as well.
SIMON: And tell us about the mutual finger-pointing of the Trump administration over Nvidia and China and chip sales.
body_zh: 政治周：参议院领袖之战；年轻和独立的中期选举投票率 美国参议院下一任多数党领袖的争夺反映了中期选举中年轻和独立选民的投票率。
美国参议院下一任多数党领袖的争夺反映了中期选举中年轻和独立选民的投票率。
民主党参议员昨天聚集在科罗拉多州，其中包括克里斯·范·霍伦。
克里斯·范·霍伦：这是为了回应美国人民的呼吁，因为我非常担心的是，他们呼吁结束政治腐败、结束受操纵的经济体系，这将要求我们以不同的方式组织参议院。
西蒙：马里兰州参议员试图取代纽约州的查克·舒默成为美国参议院的民主党领袖。 NPR 高级撰稿人 Ron Elving 加入我们。罗恩，非常感谢你和我们在一起。
罗恩·埃尔文连线：很高兴和你在一起，斯科特。
西蒙：你对参议员的论点有何看法？
埃尔文：它有很大的吸引力，特别是对年轻选民、首次选民、独立人士——这些人推动了民主党的非凡崛起，尤其是在参议院竞选中，民主党赢得了胜利，而当时没有人认为他们接近。是的，选民希望结束腐败和受操纵的经济。但是，当范霍伦说他希望以不同的方式组织参议院以实现这些目标时，他是否只是指一位新领导人，而不是长期领导人查克·舒默？我们还知道还有什么会改变吗？我们怎么知道它会更好？
舒默表示，他已经承诺为大多数参议院民主党人投票。他需要 29 票。他的一些盟友表示他将获得 40 票或更多。但范霍伦还有时间阐明自己的观点，最终，投票以无记名投票方式进行。我过去见过领导人选举，有人在投票前声称拥有选票，但在计票时并未获得多数票。
西蒙：让我问一下众议院的情况。在赢得多数席位一周后，众议院民主党人无法通过弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格斯的动议，因为 11 名民主党人未能进入众议院投票，这意味着什么？这当然是他们当选的结果？
埃尔文：对此有很多人感到愤怒，尤其是那些希望民主党在第一天就做很多事情的人。问题是，直到 1 月 3 日新国会召开时，他们实际上才能在众议院获得多数席位。因此，距离新多数派的第一天还有七周时间。
本周对赫格塞斯的投票是由一位流氓共和党人强迫进行的，但却是由现任共和党领导层安排和管理的。他们吸引了所有投票反对弹劾的共和党人——他们仍然是多数党。这就是造成差异的原因。但双方都没有出席投票。在最终的计票中，似乎如果所有民主党人都到达那里，他们就可以获胜。当然，这是假设当前的共和党领导层也会允许投票以这种方式结束，因为他们也有更多的共和党选票。
那么这次投票产生了多大的差异呢？当民主党真正接管时，赫格斯塞斯仍将面临调查和弹劾，然后参议院将需要三分之二的票数才能对他定罪并罢免他。参议院在民主党新占多数的情况下，一月份这样做的可能性比目前占多数的情况要大。
西蒙：你说赫格斯弹劾案将在一月份重新提上议程——也许还有卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的弹劾案？
埃尔文：这两个名字脱颖而出——赫格赛斯代表伊朗，当然，也因为他对将军和海军上将的大规模降级，以及他努力在整个武装部队中灌输战士文化的观念；肯尼迪是因为他旅行中最近出现的一些问题，但也许主要是因为麻疹疫情给我们带来了死亡和数千例新病例，有时一周就超过 200 例。在本十年的前四年里，全年新增麻疹病例并没有达到200例。
现在，特朗普以一种在其他内阁成员面临压力时（例如国土安全部的克里斯蒂·诺姆和工党的洛里·查韦斯-德雷默）所没有的方式支持赫格塞斯和肯尼迪。所以我们会在一月份看看他是否也支持这些人。
西蒙：请告诉我们特朗普政府在英伟达和中国以及芯片销售问题上的相互指责。

title_en: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
title_zh: 离家很远。旅行者一号现在比人类送入太空的任何东西都更远
summary: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.
summary_zh: 美国宇航局航海者一号是距离地球最远的人造物体，本周将达到一个新的里程碑。周三，调查将大致进行
body_en: Voyager 1 is the furthest man-made object from Earth : NPR

Voyager 1 is the furthest man-made object from Earth NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.
This illustration provided by NASA depicts Voyager 1. AP/NASA hide caption

NASA's Voyager 1 has traveled farther than anything else that humans have launched into space. On Wednesday, it's set to reach a new milestone: reaching a distance that is one-light day away from Earth.

NASA is celebrating the occasion with the "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day . " Calling it a symbolic celebration, NASA is asking the public on Tuesday night to send Voyager's call sign V-G-R into the sky in morse code. Use a flashlight, phone light or anything that can blink a sequence.
R - One quick flash, one long flash, one quick flash
A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, or more than 16 billion miles.
This NASA spacecraft has traveled for nearly 50 years, launching Sept. 5, 1977.

Over the course of its mission, Voyager 1 has conducted flybys of Jupiter and Saturn. In 1979, it discovered a faint ring system on Jupiter. In 1980, the spacecraft took detailed photos of Saturn's rings and moons.

While on its journey, on Feb. 17, 1998, Voyager 1 overtook the U.S. space probe, Pioneer 10, becoming the most distant human-made object in existence. It and its twin, Voyager 2, are the only spacecraft to have operated outside of the heliosphere, which acts like a protective shield of the solar system.
The Little Probe That Could: Why Voyager 1 Matters, and Why NASA Just Switched Part of It Off

Voyager 1 reached the interstellar boundary in 2012. Its interstellar mission continues to chart and measure the magnetic fields, particles and plasma waves outside the sun's heliosphere and the atmosphere of other stars.

Earlier this year, NASA elected to shut off Voyager 1's Low-energy Charged Particles experiment, or LECP, which has helped scientists map the structure of space, in order to save power. Scientists said this could keep the probe alive longer..
Voyager 1 has two science instruments still running: one that measures magnetic fields and another that listens for plasma waves.
In addition, the Voyager spacecraft is carrying the Golden Record – an interstellar "time capsule" to communicate Earth's story to extraterrestrials.
This undated handout image provided by NASA shows the Voyager Golden Record Album. NASA/JPL-Caltech/via AP hide caption

The gold-plated record contains 115 images, natural sounds such as surf, wind and animals, and spoken greetings in 35 different languages. Included are instructions, in symbols, on how to play the record and the origin of the probe.
Voyager 1 is estimated to reach "light-day status" at 5:16 a.m. ET on Wednesday, after 49 years, two months and 11 days of travel.

NASA 提供的这幅插图描绘了航行者 1 号。美联社/NASA 隐藏标题栏
美国宇航局航海者一号的飞行距离比人类发射到太空的任何其他东西都远。周三，它将达到一个新的里程碑：到达距地球一光日的距离。
美国宇航局正在以“航行者号光日闪耀”来庆祝这一时刻。美国宇航局称其为象征性的庆祝活动，并要求公众在周二晚上将航行者号的呼号 V-G-R 用莫尔斯电码发送到天空。使用手电筒、手机灯或任何可以按顺序闪烁的东西。
R - 一次快闪、一次长闪、一次快闪
一光日是光在 24 小时内传播的距离，即超过 160 亿英里。
这艘 NASA 航天器自 1977 年 9 月 5 日发射以来，已经飞行了近 50 年。
在其任务过程中，航海家一号飞越了木星和土星。 1979年，它在木星上发现了一个微弱的光环系统。 1980年，航天器拍摄了土星环和卫星的详细照片。
1998 年 2 月 17 日，航行者 1 号在旅途中超越了美国太空探测器先锋 10 号，成为现存距离最远的人造物体。它和它的双胞胎航海者二号是唯一在日光层之外运行的航天器，日光层就像太阳系的保护罩。
小探测器可以：为什么航海者一号很重要，为什么 NASA 只是关闭它的一部分
航海者一号于 2012 年到达星际边界。它的星际任务继续绘制和测量太阳日光层外和其他恒星大气层外的磁场、粒子和等离子体波。
今年早些时候，美国宇航局选择关闭旅行者一号的低能带电粒子实验（LECP），以节省电力，该实验帮助科学家绘制太空结构图。科学家表示，这可以使探测器的寿命更长。
航行者一号有两台仍在运行的科学仪器：一台测量磁场，另一台监听等离子体波。
此外，航行者号飞船还携带着金唱片——一个星际“时间胶囊”，用于向外星人传达地球的故事。
这张由美国宇航局提供的未注明日期的讲义图片展示了航行者金唱片专辑。 NASA/JPL-Caltech/via AP 隐藏标题栏
这张镀金唱片包含 115 个图像、海浪、风和动物等自然声音，以及 35 种不同语言的口头问候语。其中包括有关如何播放唱片和探头起源的符号说明。
经过 49 年零两个月零 11 天的旅行后，航行者 1 号预计将于美国东部时间周三上午 5 点 16 分达到“光日状态”。

title_en: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
title_zh: 中期选民结束了共和党在州立法机构的长期统治地位
summary: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.
summary_zh: 在几个州，民主党控制了分裂的立法机构，并削弱了共和党在其他州的主导地位。议程上的问题：更多
body_en: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP control in states : NPR

Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP control in states In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers.
Democrats made gains in legislatures across the country
Georgia state Rep. Carolyn Hugley, the party's nominee for speaker of the state House, speaks in front of members of the Democratic caucus Thursday in the capitol. Sarah Kallis/GPB News hide caption
The midterm elections saw historic changes in state legislatures.

Pennsylvania voters elected a Democratic majority in the state Senate for the first time since Jimmy Carter was president. Democrats in Texas will run the state House there for the first time in 24 years . The Georgia House will have a Democratic majority for the first time in more than 20 years .
The results reversed a GOP dominance in legislatures that began in 2010 and had solidified since.

Going into the midterms, Republicans controlled legislatures in 28 states and Democrats held 18 . The remaining few were divided. Now, with some votes still being counted, it looks likely the Democrats will hold a 24-to-22 lead with others divided .

So far, Democrats have picked up seats in nearly every state that held legislative elections, according to data compiled by NPR. Democrats gained significant ground in unexpected, reliably Republican states, like Texas, Utah and Florida.

The shift could mean real change in people's lives as legislatures rewrite laws on taxes, reproductive rights, access to health care, school funding and other issues. Legislatures have also been important in promoting or blocking President Trump's agenda.
New Democratic 'trifectas,' controlling the legislature and governor's office

The Republican State Legislative Committee, which coordinates support for GOP candidates, blamed the losses on the national anti-incumbent mood and heavy spending for Democrats. "Ultimately, the results of this cycle underscore both the challenges Republicans face and the importance of maintaining a strong, sustained presence in the states," the group's president. Edith Jorge-Tuñón, wrote.

The president of their rival organization , Heather Williams of the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, said their wins "proved what is possible when you put statehouses at the center of a national strategy."
Democrats seek to weaken the Republican lead in state legislatures
Some of the biggest changes could come in states where Democrats now control both chambers of the legislature and the governor's office. They gained six new "trifectas."
In Arizona, Democrats will have the majorities in the state House and Senate and hold the governor's office — a trifecta — for the first time since 1966.

One possible policy change could be on school vouchers. Gov. Katie Hobbs has repeatedly tried to reform and limit the state's billion-dollar voucher program , which provides public money for private school tuition regardless of family income. But the Republican-run legislature had blocked her. Arizona Democrats have said they also hope to provide financial relief on rent, utilities and childcare.

In Pennsylvania, Democratic Gov. Josh Shapiro has promised to work with a newly Democratic legislature to raise the minimum wage to $15 an hour, strengthen abortion rights and increase affordable housing.
Democrats also won trifectas in Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin and in Nevada, where they won the governor's office. They broke Republican trifectas in Georgia, Iowa, New Hampshire, Ohio and Texas.
body_zh: 中期选民结束了共和党对各州的长期控制：NPR
中期选民结束了共和党对各州的长期控制在几个州，民主党控制了分裂的立法机构，并削弱了共和党在其他州的主导地位。议程上的问题：更多获得医疗保健的机会、学校优惠券的新限制。
民主党在全国立法机构中取得进展
佐治亚州众议员卡罗琳·休格利 (Carolyn Hugley) 是该党提名的州众议院议长，周四在国会大厦向民主党核心小组成员发表讲话。莎拉·卡利斯/GPB 新闻隐藏标题栏
中期选举见证了州立法机构的历史性变化。
自吉米·卡特就任总统以来，宾夕法尼亚州选民首次选举民主党在州参议院取得多数席位。得克萨斯州的民主党人将在 24 年来首次掌管该州的州议会。佐治亚州众议院将在 20 多年来首次获得民主党多数席位。
结果扭转了共和党自 2010 年开始并在立法机构中占据主导地位的局面。
进入中期选举，共和党控制了 28 个州的立法机构，民主党控制了 18 个州。剩下的几个人也分了。现在，由于一些选票仍在清点中，民主党可能会以 24 比 22 领先，而其他人则出现分歧。
根据美国国家公共广播电台(NPR)编制的数据，到目前为止，民主党几乎在每个举行立法选举的州都获得了席位。民主党在德克萨斯州、犹他州和佛罗里达州等出人意料、可靠的共和党州取得了重大进展。
随着立法机构重写有关税收、生殖权利、医疗保健、学校经费和其他问题的法律，这种转变可能意味着人们的生活发生真正的变化。立法机构在推动或阻止特朗普总统的议程方面也发挥着重要作用。
新民主党“三连胜”，控制立法机关和州长办公室
负责协调对共和党候选人支持的共和党州立法委员会将损失归咎于全国反现任情绪和民主党的巨额支出。该组织主席表示：“最终，这一周期的结果强调了共和党面临的挑战以及在各州保持强大、持续存在的重要性。”伊迪丝·豪尔赫-图尼翁写道。
他们的竞争对手组织的主席、民主党立法竞选委员会的希瑟·威廉姆斯表示，他们的胜利“证明了当你将州议会大厦置于国家战略的中心时，一切皆有可能。”
民主党寻求削弱共和党在州立法机构中的领先地位
一些最大的变化可能发生在民主党现在控制立法机关和州长办公室的州。他们获得了六个新的“三连胜”。
在亚利桑那州，民主党将在州参众两院占据多数席位，并自 1966 年以来首次三连掌州长职位。
一项可能的政策变化可能是学券。州长凯蒂·霍布斯多次尝试改革和限制该州数十亿美元的学券计划，该计划为私立学校学费提供公共资金，无论家庭收入如何。但共和党控制的立法机构阻止了她。亚利桑那州民主党人表示，他们还希望在租金、水电费和儿童保育方面提供财政减免。
在宾夕法尼亚州，民主党州长乔什·夏皮罗 (Josh Shapiro) 承诺与新成立的民主党立法机构合作，将最低工资提高到每小时 15 美元，加强堕胎权并增加经济适用房。
民主党还在密歇根州、明尼苏达州、威斯康星州和内华达州三连胜，并赢得了州长职位。他们打破了共和党在佐治亚州、爱荷华州、新罕布什尔州、俄亥俄州和德克萨斯州的三连胜。

title_en: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
title_zh: 新墨西哥州希望为所有人提供免费托儿服务。这是有效的方法，也是无效的方法
summary: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.
summary_zh: 一年前的 11 月，新墨西哥州成为第一个向每个符合条件的家庭（无论收入多少）提供免费托儿服务的州。
body_en: What to know about New Mexico’s first year of free childcare : NPR
What to know about New Mexico’s first year of free childcare A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income.
What universal free childcare is costing New Mexico
Children wearing Halloween costumes play on the playground of Kids Campus in Santa Fe, N.M. Nina Alexandria Riggio for NPR hide caption
It's a hazy August morning, and Judyn Martinez is dropping her daughter off at Kids Campus, a sought-after childcare center in Santa Fe that is now free for any eligible family in New Mexico.
"It's an amazing school so far. She loves it. I love it," Martinez said. "Everyone's nice. She's learning, growing already."

A year ago this month, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every family, regardless of income. To qualify, families must be residents of New Mexico and adults in the house must be working, looking for work, in school or unable to work.
Many parents, including Martinez, told NPR that it's been life-changing.
"I'm really grateful for universal childcare because I wouldn't have been able to send her," Martinez said.

There's just one drawback for families: Right now, the state doesn't have the capacity to meet the demand, which has left some families waiting without childcare. Martinez said it took her about a year and half to get off the waitlist for Kids Campus — a waitlist that, today, has nearly 700 children on it.
When she first spoke with NPR in September, Lilia Doyle said her 2-year-old son was on six different waitlists.
U.S. childcare costs are astronomical. More families are turning to grandparents
"I'm 97th on a multi-hundred person waitlist. I'm 75th on something. And some, I'm not even getting calls back," Doyle said.

Doyle, a children's librarian with a background in early childhood education, lives in Santa Fe. She acknowledged that she's selective when it comes to childcare. Still, she said, it should be easier.
"I have great belief in this program, but as it currently stands, I think the rollout needs a lot, a lot of help."
Kids Campus is a sought-after childcare center, with a waitlist nearly 700 children long. Nina Alexandria Riggio for NPR hide caption

According to the state, New Mexico has about 67,000 children 5 and under, and about 50% of them are enrolled in the universal childcare program. Some of the remaining families participate in other free public programs, like New Mexico PreK and Head Start.

But many children aren't enrolled in any public, free childcare program, and it's hard to know exactly how many are in Doyle's position, unable to access universal childcare because of limited capacity. New Mexico officials acknowledged to NPR that the program needs to expand.
In order to work for every family, the program will have to overcome both a shortage of childcare workers and childcare slots — two challenges that are also playing out at the national level.
body_zh: 关于新墨西哥州免费托儿服务第一年的知识：NPR
关于新墨西哥州第一年免费托儿服务的了解 一年前的 11 月，新墨西哥州成为第一个向每个符合条件的家庭（无论收入如何）提供免费托儿服务的州。
新墨西哥州全民免费托儿服务的成本是多少
穿着万圣节服装的孩子们在新墨西哥州圣达菲儿童校园的操场上玩耍。Nina Alexandria Riggio 接受 NPR 隐藏标题栏
这是一个雾蒙蒙的八月早晨，朱丁·马丁内斯 (Judyn Martinez) 将她的女儿送到儿童校园 (Kids Campus)，这是圣达菲 (Santa Fe) 的一个热门托儿中心，现在对新墨西哥州任何符合条件的家庭免费开放。
“到目前为止，这是一所很棒的学校。她喜欢它。我喜欢它，”马丁内斯说。 “每个人都很好。她已经在学习、成长了。”
一年前的这个月，新墨西哥州成为第一个向每个家庭提供免费托儿服务的州，无论收入如何。为了符合资格，家庭必须是新墨西哥州居民，并且家里的成年人必须正在工作、正在寻找工作、在校或无法工作。
包括马丁内斯在内的许多家长告诉 NPR，这改变了他们的生活。
“我真的很感激全民托儿服务，因为我无法送她去，”马丁内斯说。
对于家庭来说，只有一个缺点：目前，国家没有能力满足这一需求，这使得一些家庭无法获得托儿服务，只能等待。马丁内斯说，她花了大约一年半的时间才摆脱了“儿童校园”的候补名单——如今，这个候补名单上有近 700 名孩子。
莉莉娅·多伊尔 (Lilia Doyle) 9 月份首次接受 NPR 采访时表示，她 2 岁的儿子在 6 个不同的候补名单上。
美国的儿童保育费用是天文数字。更多家庭转向祖父母
“在数百人的候补名单上，我排在第 97 位。在某些事情上，我排在第 75 位。有些人，我什至没有接到回电，”多伊尔说。
多伊尔是一位拥​​有幼儿教育背景的儿童图书管理员，住在圣达菲。她承认自己在照顾孩子方面是有选择性的。不过，她说，这应该更容易。
“我对这个计划充满信心，但就目前情况而言，我认为推出需要很多很多帮助。”
Kids Campus 是一家广受欢迎的托儿中心，等候名单上有近 700 名儿童。尼娜·亚历山大·里吉奥 (Nina Alexandria Riggio) 为 NPR 隐藏标题栏
据该州称，新墨西哥州约有 67,000 名 5 岁及以下儿童，其中约 50% 参加了全民儿童保育计划。剩下的一些家庭参加其他免费公共计划，例如新墨西哥州学前班和启蒙计划。
但许多儿童没有参加任何公共免费托儿计划，而且很难确切知道有多少儿童处于多伊尔的处境，由于能力有限而无法获得全民托儿服务。新墨西哥州官员向全国公共广播电台承认，该计划需要扩大。
为了惠及每个家庭，该计划必须克服儿童保育人员和儿童保育名额的短缺——这两个挑战也在国家层面上出现。

title_en: Russell Brand says ‘I am not guilty’ in statement from prison read by his wife
title_zh: 拉塞尔·布兰德在妻子宣读的狱中声明中称“我无罪”
summary: Russell Brand declared “I am not guilty” in a new statement read by his wife on his YouTube channel Sunday, days after a London court sentenced him to prison on rape and sexual assault charges.
summary_zh: 拉塞尔·布兰德 (Russell Brand) 周日在他的 YouTube 频道上宣读了一份新声明，宣布“我无罪”。几天前，伦敦一家法院判处他有罪
body_en: Russell Brand declared “I am not guilty” in a new statement read by his wife on his YouTube channel Sunday, days after a London court sentenced him to prison on rape and sexual assault charges.

The 51-year-old comedian and former actor was sentenced Nov. 9 to 10 1/2 years in prison after a London court found him guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He pleaded not guilty to all counts and denied all of the allegations.
In a new YouTube video, Brand’s wife, Laura Brand, read the statement on his behalf.

“So, Russell has asked me to read something to you today: ‘Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,’” she said.

“I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey. ... I’m in the biggest sex offenders prison in Europe. The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated,” she continued, reading his statement.

“And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone. I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me. Let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us,” the statement said.
Brand closed by asking the public to support his wife and family. “I feel your prayers,” the statement said.

Brand’s YouTube channel features Christian-themed content, including a “Sunday Service” series he hosts with his wife. At the start of the video, Laura Brand said she would continue the series. Sunday’s episode included prerecorded video of the couple discussing faith and morality.
“Even though it’s painful, and obviously will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my my companion, my person, with me, but I want to continue,” she said.

Justice Joel Bennathan called Brand a “sexual predator” before delivering his sentence. At sentencing, Brand’s victims shared in-person and written statements about the trauma and its effects on their daily lives.

Brand was convicted of raping a female fan at his home in 2009 after she met him at one of his shows. He was also found guilty of sexually assaulting three other women: one whose breasts he grabbed at a party in 2004; one who said he kissed and groped her at a London radio station in 2004 or 2005; and one who said he pressed his face into her groin during the recording of an advertisement in 2009.
He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The sentence marked a stunning fall from grace for Brand, who rose to fame as a broadcaster and stand-up comedian and went on to a Hollywood career, starring in films including “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” and “Get Him to the Greek.”

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 . The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at https://www.rainn.org/get-help.
Marlene Lenthang is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 周日，拉塞尔·布兰德 (Russell Brand) 的妻子在他的 YouTube 频道上宣读了一份新声明，宣布“我无罪”。几天前，伦敦一家法院因强奸和性侵犯指控判处他入狱。
这位 51 岁的喜剧演员兼前演员于 11 月 9 日被伦敦一家法院判定犯有一项强奸罪和三项性侵犯罪，并被判处 10.5 年监禁。他对所有罪名均表示不认罪，并否认所有指控。
在 YouTube 上的一段新视频中，布兰德的妻子劳拉·布兰德 (Laura Brand) 代表他宣读了这份声明。
“所以，拉塞尔今天让我读一些东西给你们听：‘亲爱的基督里的兄弟姐妹，上帝保佑你们的支持。如你们所知，我对自己入狱的罪行并无罪，所以奇怪的事情发生了，’”她说。
“我被关押在 HMP Littlehey 监狱……我在欧洲最大的性犯罪者监狱。好消息是，我已经看到这里的工作人员很强大，他们很友善，而且很敬业，”她继续读着他的声明。
“至于我的狱友，我现在知道我没有资格评判任何人。我不知道这里还有哪些人是无罪的，而那些有罪的人，他们是基督为拯救而死的人，就像你和我一样。让我们大家彼此相爱、互相祈祷、互相宽恕，就像上帝宽恕了我们一样，”声明说。
布兰德最后请求公众支持他的妻子和家人。声明称：“我感受到你们的祈祷。”
布兰德的 YouTube 频道以基督教为主题的内容，包括他与妻子主持的“周日礼拜”系列节目。在视频开始时，劳拉·布兰德表示她将继续这个系列。周日的节目包括这对夫妇讨论信仰和道德的预先录制的视频。
“尽管这很痛苦，而且显然我需要一些时间来适应坐在这里，没有我的同伴、我的人陪伴，但我想继续，”她说。
法官乔尔·本纳森在宣判前称布兰德为“性掠夺者”。在宣判时，布兰德的受害者亲自分享了有关创伤及其对日常生活影响的书面陈述。
2009 年，布兰德因在他的一场演出中认识一名女粉丝而在家中强奸一名女粉丝而被定罪。他还被判对另外三名女性进行性侵犯：其中一名是他在 2004 年的一次聚会上抓住了她的胸部；另一名是他在 2004 年的一次聚会上抓住了她的胸部。一位自称2004年或2005年在伦敦一家广播电台亲吻并抚摸她的人；还有一个人说，2009年录制广告时，他把脸贴在她的腹股沟上。
他被判犯有另外两项强奸罪和一项未遂猥亵罪。
这句话标志着布兰德的失宠，他以播音员和单口喜剧演员的身份而声名鹊起，随后进入好莱坞，主演了《忘记莎拉·马歇尔》和《带他去希腊》等电影。
