title_en: The biggest move of the NFL trade deadline paid immediate dividends
title_zh: NFL 交易截止日的最大举措立即带来了红利
summary: Making his first start for the Minnesota Vikings since 2023, quarterback Kirk Cousins picked up where he left off — almost literally.
summary_zh: 四分卫柯克·考辛斯 (Kirk Cousins) 自 2023 年以来首次代表明尼苏达维京人队 (Minnesota Vikings) 首发，几乎从字面上看，他接续了他上次离开的地方。
body_en: Vikings vs. Packers: Kirk Cousins trade paid immediate dividends
Making his first start for the Minnesota Vikings since 2023, quarterback Kirk Cousins picked up where he left off — almost literally.
Cousins led the Vikings to a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, ending Minnesota’s two-game losing streak and improving the team’s record to 7-2.
Cousins’s most recent start for the Vikings prior to Sunday also came at Green Bay. It was in 2023, and he tore his Achilles during that game, and Minnesota moved on from him the following offseason.

The Vikings have been looking for an answer at quarterback since, and they eventually came back around to Cousins at this year’s trade deadline. Cousins got the start Sunday only five days after he was acquired from the Las Vegas Raiders, and he made some big throws as he led Minnesota to its highest scoring output since Week 1.
“I didn’t even know what my code was to get into the building on Wednesday,” Cousins said postgame. “It took a village. I’m just grateful for all the people that stepped up to help.”

Cousins finished the game completing 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception. While his stats weren’t spectacular, he made a meaningful impact on money downs, as the Vikings finished the game converting eight of 16 on third down. (Entering Sunday, Minnesota was ranked 30th in third-down conversion percentage at 33.3%.)

Minnesota’s first touchdown came on a third and 23, as Cousins made a beautiful, drop-in-the-bucket throw to Myles Price, who bounced off defenders en route to the end zone. Cousins described it as a “big-time” play by Price.

Cousins made another great throw on a third-and-long later in the game, connecting with Tai Felton on a wheel route on a third and 15 in the second quarter. The pass set up a one-yard touchdown run on the next play.
Later, after the Packers had cut the Vikings’ 20-0 lead to 20-10, Cousins picked up another massive first, checking into a screen pass on third and 12 and finding Justin Jefferson for a first down.
“It was fun, it felt like old times watching Justin do what he just did on that play,” Cousins said. “It was like, ‘I remember that guy. He’s pretty special.’”
Five plays later, Cousins threw his second touchdown of the game and effectively iced any chances of a Green Bay comeback.

“[He] just brought a certain amount of poise, leadership, execution,” head coach Kevin O’Connell said postgame. “Ran the show incredibly clean. Can’t say enough about him, I know everybody in the organization felt it this week.”
Jefferson, one of the game’s top receivers, was perhaps the biggest individual beneficiary of his old quarterback’s return. Jefferson’s nine receptions and 13 targets were both season highs.

Though Cousins didn’t exactly light the box score on fire, his presence Sunday made Minnesota’s championship formula incredibly clear: Play lights out defense, and do just enough on offense with above-average quarterback play.

With Cousins helping push the Vikings out to an early lead, Minnesota’s defense pinned its ears back and got after Jordan Love. The Vikings finished the game with eight sacks, and limited the Packers to only 56 yards rushing.
Love, one of the game’s great deep-ball throwers, finished the game with 220 yards, his fewest since Week 4. His 46.6 QBR was also his third-worst mark of the season.
“For one of the first times this year, I thought we played complementary football,” O’Connell said.

The win was an important one for Minnesota. The Vikings are now two games clear of Green Bay in loss column in the loaded NFC North, and now also own the tiebreaker between the two teams. Minnesota kept pace with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, both of whom are also 7-2.

The Vikings’ offense didn’t necessarily look perfect Sunday. But their quarterback making big throws and providing a steady hand while the defensedefense continued to dominate showed exactly why Minnesota decided to bring Cousins back.
body_zh: 维京人队对阵包装工队：柯克·考辛斯的交易立即带来红利
四分卫柯克·考辛斯 (Kirk Cousins) 自 2023 年以来首次代表明尼苏达维京人队 (Minnesota Vikings) 首发，几乎从字面上看，他接续了他上次离开的地方。
周日，考辛斯带领维京人队以30-10战胜绿湾包装工队，结束了明尼苏达队的两连败，并将球队战绩提高到7胜2负。
考辛斯在周日之前为维京人队最近一次首发也是在绿湾。那是在 2023 年，他在那场比赛中跟腱撕裂，森林狼在接下来的休赛期离开了他。
从那以后，维京人队一直在寻找四分卫的答案，他们最终在今年的交易截止日期之前回到了考辛斯身边。考辛斯在从拉斯维加斯突袭者队收购后仅五天就在周日开始了比赛，他在带领明尼苏达取得自第一周以来的最高得分的同时，还做出了一些精彩的投篮。
“我什至不知道周三进入大楼的密码是什么，”考辛斯赛后说道。 “这需要整个村庄的努力。我非常感谢所有挺身而出提供帮助的人。”
考辛斯全场比赛31次传球21次推进207码，取得2次达阵和1次拦截。虽然他的数据并不引人注目，但他对输球产生了有意义的影响，维京人队在第三次进攻中完成了 16 场比赛中的 8 场比赛。 （进入周日，明尼苏达州的三档转换率排名第 30 位，为 33.3%。）
明尼苏达队的第一次达阵是在第三次和23号球上，考辛斯向迈尔斯·普莱斯投出一记漂亮的投球，后者在到达达阵区的途中从防守者身上弹开。考辛斯将其描述为普莱斯的一场“精彩”表演。
比赛后期，考辛斯再次投出一记漂亮的三分球，并在第二节的三分球和 15 分中与泰·费尔顿 (Tai Felton) 接球。这次传球为下一场比赛奠定了一个一码达阵的基础。
后来，在包装工队将维京人队20-0的领先优势缩小到20-10后，考辛斯又取得了一个巨大的第一，在第三个和第12个位置检查掩护传球，并找到贾斯汀·杰弗森率先进攻。
“这很有趣，看着贾斯汀在那场比赛中所做的事情感觉就像回到过去一样，”考辛斯说。 “就像是，‘我记得那个人。他很特别。’”
五场比赛后，考辛斯投出了本场比赛的第二次达阵，有效地阻止了绿湾队翻盘的机会。
“（他）带来了一定的沉着、领导力和执行力，”主教​​练凯文·奥康奈尔赛后说道。 “整个演出非常干净。关于他，我不能说太多，我知道组织中的每个人本周都感受到了这一点。”
杰弗森是比赛中顶级的接球手之一，也许是他的老四分卫回归的最大个人受益者。杰弗森的 9 次接球和 13 次进球均为赛季新高。
尽管考辛斯并没有完全点燃得分，但他周日的出现让明尼苏达州的冠军公式变得异常清晰：打出防守，并以高于平均水平的四分卫表现在进攻上做得足够好。
随着考辛斯的帮助，维京人队早早取得领先，明尼苏达队的防守队员紧盯乔丹·乐福。维京人队以 8 次擒杀结束了比赛，并将包装工队的冲球距离限制在 56 码。
乐福是比赛中最出色的远投手之一，他以 220 码结束了比赛，这是他自第四周以来的最低码数。他的 46.6 QBR 也是他本赛季第三差的成绩。
“这是今年第一次，我认为我们踢的是互补足球，”奥康奈尔说。
这场胜利对于明尼苏达来说是一场重要的胜利。维京人队现在在国联北区的输球榜上领先绿湾队两场，现在也拥有两队之间的决胜局。明尼苏达队与底特律雄狮队和芝加哥熊队并驾齐驱，这两支球队的战绩也是7胜2负。
周日维京人队的进攻看起来并不完美。但他们的四分卫在防守继续占据主导地位的情况下投出大力球并提供了稳定的手感，这正是明尼苏达州决定将考辛斯带回来的原因。

title_en: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans. Who made them? (Psst: Workers)
title_zh: 悉尼·斯威尼（Sydney Sweeney）有很棒的牛仔裤。谁制造了它们？ （注意：工人）
summary: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?
summary_zh: American Eagle Outfitters 告诉我们，Sydney Sweeney 的牛仔裤很棒。但谁制造了它们呢？服装厂的工作条件是怎样的？
body_en: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans. Who made them? : NPR

Sydney Sweeney has great jeans. Who made them? Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?
Sydney Sweeney has great jeans. Who made them? (Hint: Workers)

KARACHI, Pakistan — In a slum dotted with shimmering pools of sewage, a garment worker nods in recognition as Sydney Sweeney slowly zips up her jeans in an American Eagle Outfitters advertisement playing on a smartphone.

But it's not Sweeney she recognizes — it's the jeans and jacket. This woman, a single mother, has worked on American Eagle production lines and seen those denim styles and similar models. "I know how all of them are made, because I have worked on them," she says.

Workers like that single mother. She asks that we refer to her as S., the initial of her first name, because she fears her bosses at the garment factory where she works will fire her if she's identified. "If you raise your voice, they'll push you out," she says. "We are helpless."
S., a young woman, works at a factory run by a company called Artistic Garment Industries, where she says she's paid about $144 a month, a sum that supports her son and her mother.
There are many garment factories in this industrial area in Karachi, Pakistan. Workers interviewed by NPR said that conditions are often "oppressively hot." Betsy Joles for NPR hide caption

She says the factory is "oppressively hot." It was 106 F outside when we met her, and she says the factory inside is even hotter. She says it's hard to leave her workstation to drink water because she has to meet her production targets. She says she has to check the quality of 1,000 to 1,600 pieces of clothing a day — and she's fainted three times this year. "I feel faint, and I can barely stand. I have no energy in my hands and feet," S. says. "They don't even let us sit down." But S. says she has no other options.

Artistic Garment Industries confirmed it makes clothes for American Eagle but tells NPR that it does not push out workers who complain about their working conditions. The company says it has a robust complaints system that workers can use and says it frequently checks on temperatures inside different parts of its factories.

In response to questions NPR sent to American Eagle, the company says it's "committed to working directly with our suppliers to protect the health, safety, and rights of workers. We take the concerns raised by workers — and those whom NPR interviewed — very seriously."

S. is one of around 20 workers we interviewed over the spring and summer in Bangladesh and Pakistan, two of the world's biggest global garment production hubs outside of China. Those men and women worked in five different factories. All of those workers asked NPR not to use their full names and to use only the initial of their first name, worried they'd lose their jobs or be blacklisted from future jobs if they were identified.

Although we focused on the American Eagle jeans worn by Sweeney for the 2025 campaign, the reporting led to a bigger issue: how fast fashion is made, because garment factories make clothes for multiple brands at once. Workers we met told us they made clothes for Levi's, Massimo Dutti, The Gap, H&M and American Eagle. They said it's common knowledge at the factories which brands they are making clothes for, in part because some workers are stitching on the labels.

The garment workers we spoke to offered strikingly similar accounts. And they echoed worker testimonies in multiple reports by labor and climate rights groups. The workers told us they're paid low wages, even as they're expected to reach what they say are unreasonably high production targets, often laboring in sweltering factories.

These are production targets like stitching 200 sleeves an hour or checking the quality of a thousand pieces of clothing a day. The workers we interviewed say they are unable to hydrate or cool down properly, even as extreme heat caused by climate change makes their workplaces and homes even hotter.

It can be four to six degrees hotter inside a factory, says Jason Judd , executive director of the Global Labor Institute at Cornell University, which researched heat inside garment factories and worker homes . "You've got all those bodies, all that material, all that machinery putting off heat. You've got ventilation problems."

"We're starting to see fainting, heat illness, exacerbation of chronic disease, even death," says Cara Schulte, a re searcher at Climate Rights International. She authored two reports on the impacts of heat on garment workers.

Schulte says workers are put under that extreme pressure to reach production targets. A major reason is that brands demand their suppliers make enormous volumes of clothes on tight deadlines and on thin profit margins. And she says garment workers are vulnerable to the heat because they're clustered in countries like Bangladesh and Pakistan. She cites U.N. publications stating that t hose factories are "in areas that are warming faster than the global average, that are [already] incredibly hot and humid. "

H&M, one of the brands that workers identified making, said it "put great effort" in ensuring fair payment to its suppliers and that labor costs are "excluded from the price negotiations of our product orders" to ensure that worker wages were not driven down.
body_zh: 悉尼·斯威尼（Sydney Sweeney）有很棒的牛仔裤。谁制造了它们？ ： 美国国家公共电台
悉尼·斯威尼（Sydney Sweeney）有很棒的牛仔裤。谁制造了它们？ American Eagle Outfitters 告诉我们，Sydney Sweeney 的牛仔裤很棒。但谁制造了它们呢？巴基斯坦和孟加拉国的服装厂的工作条件如何？
悉尼·斯威尼（Sydney Sweeney）有很棒的牛仔裤。谁制造了它们？ （提示：工人）
巴基斯坦卡拉奇——在智能手机上播放的 American Eagle Outfitters 广告中，西德尼·斯威尼 (Sydney Sweeney) 慢慢拉上牛仔裤的拉链时，在布满闪闪发光的污水池的贫民窟里，一名制衣工人点头表示认可。
但她认得的不是斯威尼，而是牛仔裤和夹克。这位女士是一位单身母亲，曾在 American Eagle 生产线上工作，并见过那些牛仔款式和类似款式。 “我知道它们是如何制作的，因为我曾经研究过它们，”她说。
工人们喜欢那个单亲妈妈。她要求我们用 S.（她名字的首字母）称呼她，因为她担心如果她的身份被曝光，她工作的服装厂的老板会解雇她。 “如果你提高声音，他们就会把你赶出去，”她说。 “我们很无助。”
S. 是一名年轻女性，在一家名为 Artistic Garment Industries 的公司经营的工厂工作，她说她每月的工资约为 144 美元，这笔钱可以养活她的儿子和母亲。
巴基斯坦卡拉奇这个工业区有许多服装厂。接受美国国家公共广播电台采访的工人们表示，工作环境往往“酷热难受”。 NPR 的贝齐·乔尔斯隐藏标题栏
她说工厂“闷热难受”。我们见到她时，外面的温度是 106 华氏度，她说工厂里面更热。她说，离开工作台喝水很困难，因为她必须完成生产目标。她说她每天必须检查 1,000 到 1,600 件衣服的质量 - 今年她已经晕倒了 3 次。 “我感到头晕，几乎无法站立。我的手脚没有力气，”S. 说。 “他们甚至不让我们坐下。”但 S. 说她没有其他选择。
Artistic Garment Industries 证实它为 American Eagle 生产衣服，但告诉 NPR，它不会驱逐那些抱怨工作条件的工人。该公司表示，它有一个强大的投诉系统可供工人使用，并表示它经常检查工厂不同区域的温度。
在回答 NPR 向 American Eagle 提出的问题时，该公司表示“致力于与我们的供应商直接合作，以保护工人的健康、安全和权利。我们非常重视工人以及接受 NPR 采访的人提出的担忧。”
S. 是我们春季和夏季在孟加拉国和巴基斯坦采访的约 20 名工人之一，这两个国家是中国以外最大的全球服装生产中心。这些男人和女人在五个不同的工厂工作。所有这些工人都要求 NPR 不要使用他们的全名，而只使用他们名字的首字母，担心如果他们的身份被发现，他们会失去工作或被列入未来工作的黑名单。

尽管我们关注的是 Sweeney 在 2025 年广告活动中穿着的 American Eagle 牛仔裤，但该报道引发了一个更大的问题：时尚的制作速度有多快，因为服装工厂同时为多个品牌生产衣服。我们遇到的工人告诉我们，他们为 Levi's、Massimo Dutti、The Gap、H&M 和 American Eagle 制作服装。他们表示，工厂里都知道他们为哪些品牌生产衣服，部分原因是一些工人负责缝制标签。
我们采访的服装工人提供了惊人相似的说法。他们在劳工和气候权利组织的多份报告中呼应了工人的证词。工人们告诉我们，他们的工资很低，尽管他们预计要达到他们所说的不合理的高生产目标，而且经常在闷热的工厂里劳动。
这些生产目标包括每小时缝制 200 个袖子或每天检查 1000 件衣服的质量。我们采访的工人表示，他们无法适当补充水分或降温，尽管气候变化引起的极端高温使他们的工作场所和家变得更加炎热。
康奈尔大学全球劳工研究所执行主任贾森·贾德（Jason Judd）表示，工厂内的温度可能会高出四到六度，该研究所研究了服装厂和工人住宅内的热量。 “你有这么多的身体，所有的材料，所有的机器都会散发热量。你有通风问题。”
“我们开始看到昏厥、中暑、慢性病恶化，甚至死亡，”气候权利国际研究员卡拉·舒尔特说。她撰写了两份关于高温对制衣工人影响的报告。
舒尔特表示，工人们为了达到生产目标而承受着巨大的压力。一个主要原因是品牌要求其供应商在紧迫的期限内生产大量服装，并且利润微薄。她说，服装工人很容易受到高温的影响，因为他们聚集在孟加拉国和巴基斯坦等国家。她援引联合国出版物的说法，称这些工厂“位于升温速度快于全球平均水平的地区，[已经]非常炎热和潮湿。”
H&M 是工人确认制造的品牌之一，该公司表示，它“付出了巨大努力”，以确保向供应商公平付款，并且劳动力成本“被排除在我们产品订单的价格谈判之外”，以确保工人工资不会被压低。

title_en: Transcript: Sen. Bill Cassidy on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Nov. 15, 2026
title_zh: 文字记录：参议员比尔·卡西迪 (Bill Cassidy) 的“与玛格丽特·布伦南 (Margaret Brennan) 一起面对国家”，2026 年 11 月 15 日
summary: The following is the transcript of the interview with Sen. Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Nov. 15, 2026.
summary_zh: 以下是对路易斯安那州共和党参议员比尔·卡西迪的采访记录，该采访在“与玛格丽特·布伦南一起面对国家”节目中播出
body_en: The following is the transcript of the interview with Sen. Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Nov. 15, 2026.
MARGARET BRENNAN: We go now to the chairman of the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, Republican Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana. Good morning to you, Doctor.

MARGARET BRENNAN: You may have seen these headlines that it is now official that the U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, our partners at KFF report. And as you know, babies don't get their measles shot until they're around a year old, and so that means this regular transmission of measles throughout the country can leave parents with- with risks of exposing their kids and- and little that they can do to protect them in these cold weather months. Do you think that the current health officials are doing enough to educate the public about the risk of transmission?

SEN. CASSIDY: First, let me emphasize what you just said. Speaking as a physician, you may decide not to be vaccinated because it's your free will, but the child who's too young to be vaccinated is vulnerable if you come into that child's presence, and we're seeing children die from measles who are too young to be vaccinated. By the way, it's also true for the immunocompromised, which might be a woman who is pregnant and her immunity falls. It might be- it might be someone on cancer chemotherapy. So if you've not been vaccinated, you could be the person that brings death to another. That's something to remember. Your specific question- question, are public health officials doing enough? I think if I were president, I'd be saying, stand on the mountaintop, give that message, that you may decide that this is just your body, do what you want, but you can bring measles or some other disease into the- into the health space of a child who's not- who's not old enough to be vaccinated. I think that should be the message going out. It should be pounded, pounded, pounded.
MARGARET BRENNAN: You have oversight of these health institutions. In- in the next few weeks, do you plan action? I mean, why aren't we hearing from the CDC director?

SEN. CASSIDY: So I'm in regular contact with the CDC director. For example, there was a broken link where you fill in your zip code and it tells you where to get the flu shot. And I- somebody informed me it was broken. I texted her. She responded quickly and saying that she didn't know about it, she would look into it. And then she texted back to say it's been broken for a year, and so she's working to fix it. There's a lot of things to fix, and Dr. Schwartz is, as best I can tell, doing her best. But there will be more comments about this. It is- we've got four to six weeks left. No, we got about four weeks left, and so there's a limited time
SEN. CASSIDY: --to have a public hearing, but there's contact going on in the background.

MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, you have shared with us previously that when you voted to confirm Secretary Kennedy, you believed that he would have more oversight in that Senate confirmed position. You also said that he's broken promises to you. This past week, Secretary Kennedy said while Senate Republicans used to threaten not to confirm his appointees, now that Democrats will be in the majority, his gloves will be off. Take a listen.

HHS SECRETARY ROBERT F. KENNEDY JR.: The Senate no longer has any leverage over me, and you know- and that's a big deal. And then we have Stephen Miller in, who's a- a friend of our movement. And I don't think anything is going to get in our way now.
MARGARET BRENNAN: The Senate has no leverage over me. What do you make of that?

SEN. CASSIDY: Well, first, he's obviously trying to provide cover for failure as Secretary of Health and Human Services. He was supposed to be doing something positive on ultra-processed foods. That's what MAHA moms wanted. There's been minimal progress, and now we've lost our measles elimination status, and we have infants dying from measles. So, if you're a MAHA mom and you are hoping for something better- and hundreds of them contacted me during this debate about whether to support the secretary for HHS secretary- that's what they wanted. They have every right to be disappointed, and the logic that because Republicans have been there, but now Democrats are in charge, will make it easier for him? There is no logic. This is about covering a series of failures. And by the way, I should also say that healthcare expenses are sky-high, going higher. Small businesses dropping coverage, employees unable to afford their deductible. This has been a failure. If I were president, I would choose someone else because there needs to be accountability for higher healthcare costs, more measles deaths, losing elimination status, and no progress on processed foods.

MARGARET BRENNAN: So, a number of Democrats, including Senator Alsobrooks and Warnock, have said RFK must resign or be fired. One of the incoming senators, Dr. Annie Andrews from South Carolina, she actually ran on a platform of impeaching RFK. When I've asked you in the past about that possibility, you told me you didn't see an impeachable offense. Is that still the case?

SEN. CASSIDY: Well, it's up to the president. This is ultimately the president's legacy. The impeachment. As regards impeachment, you know, you can impeach, I guess, over a ham sandwich, so they'll have to decide what to do on that. But I do think it's more importantly the president's decision. The president may want a legacy of higher health care costs, losing measles elimination status, and no progress on addressing ultra-processed foods and other things. If so, that'll taint the president's legacy. If the president wants actually something positive, he should change. And that's just that's just speaking politically. The American voters signaled at the midterm they don't like status quo, particularly in healthcare, and I think it's time for something different.

MARGARET BRENNAN: So Republicans are racing to confirm nominees before Democrats take office in January, and this Wednesday is the vote on the nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton, the president's nominee to become the FDA commissioner. You've previously said her role in crafting the Trump administration's childhood vaccine policies was almost disqualifying. Senator Collins has raised concern about the FDA's authorization of flavored vapes and nicotine. Senator Murkowski has worried about political pressure on scientific review and the FDA-approved abortion drug mifepristone. Given all this, do you still expect that Dr. Overton will be approved by your committee?
body_zh: 以下是对路易斯安那州共和党参议员比尔·卡西迪的采访记录，该采访于 2026 年 11 月 15 日在“与玛格丽特·布伦南一起面对国家”节目中播出。
玛格丽特·布伦南：现在请健康、教育、劳工和养老金委员会主席、路易斯安那州共和党参议员比尔·卡西迪发言。早上好，医生。
玛格丽特·布伦南：您可能已经看到了这些头条新闻，据我们 KFF 的合作伙伴报告，美国现已正式失去麻疹消除国家的地位。如您所知，婴儿直到一岁左右才会注射麻疹疫苗，因此这意味着麻疹在全国范围内的定期传播可能会让父母面临感染孩子的风险，并且在寒冷的天气里几乎无法保护他们。您认为目前的卫生官员在教育公众有关传播风险方面做得足够吗？

森。卡西迪：首先，我要强调一下你刚才所说的内容。作为一名医生，您可能会决定不接种疫苗，因为这是您的自由意志，但如果您出现在太小而无法接种疫苗的孩子面前，那么他们很容易受到伤害，而且我们看到一些太小而无法接种疫苗的儿童死于麻疹。顺便说一句，对于免疫功能低下的人来说也是如此，这可能是怀孕后免疫力下降的女性。可能是——可能是某个正在接受癌症化疗的人。因此，如果您没有接种疫苗，您可能会成为导致他人死亡的人。这是值得记住的事情。你的具体问题是，公共卫生官员做得足够吗？我想，如果我是总统，我会说，站在山顶上，发出这样的信息，你可以决定这只是你的身体，做你想做的事，但你可以把麻疹或其他疾病带入一个孩子的健康空间，而这个孩子的年龄还不足以接种疫苗。我认为这应该是要传达的信息。应该敲打、敲打、敲打。
玛格丽特·布伦南：您对这些卫生机构有监督权。在接下来的几周内，您计划采取行动吗？我的意思是，为什么我们没有收到疾病预防控制中心主任的消息？

森。卡西迪：所以我与疾病预防控制中心主任保持定期联系。例如，您填写邮政编码的链接有一个损坏的链接，它会告诉您在哪里可以注射流感疫苗。我——有人告诉我它坏了。我给她发短信。她很快回应说她不知道这件事，她会调查一下。然后她回短信说它已经坏了一年了，所以她正在努力修复它。有很多事情需要解决，据我所知，施瓦茨博士正在尽力而为。但对此会有更多评论。是的——我们还剩下四到六周的时间。不，我们还剩大约四个星期，所以时间有限
森。卡西迪：——举行公开听证会，但背后有联系。
玛格丽特·布伦南：嗯，您之前曾与我们分享过，当您投票确认肯尼迪国务卿时，您相信他会对参议院确认的职位进行更多监督。你还说他违背了对你的承诺。上周，肯尼迪国务卿表示，虽然参议院共和党人过去常常威胁不确认他的任命人选，但现在民主党将占多数，他将脱下手套。听听。
美国卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪：参议院对我不再有任何影响力，你知道，这是一件大事。然后我们邀请了斯蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller），他是我们运动的朋友。我认为现在没有任何事情会妨碍我们。
玛格丽特·布伦南：参议院对我没有影响力。你对此有何看法？

森。卡西迪：嗯，首先，他显然是在试图为卫生与公众服务部部长的失败提供掩护。他应该对超加工食品做一些积极的事情。这就是 MAHA 妈妈们想要的。进展甚微，现在我们已经失去了消除麻疹的状态，并且有婴儿死于麻疹。所以，如果你是一位 MAHA 妈妈，并且你希望得到更好的东西——在这场关于是否支持卫生与公众服务部部长的辩论期间，数百人联系了我——这就是他们想要的。他们完全有权利感到失望，而因为共和党人一直在那里，但现在民主党人掌权，这样的逻辑会让他的处境变得更容易吗？没有逻辑。这是关于掩盖一系列的失败。顺便说一句，我还应该说医疗费用非常高，而且还在不断上升。小企业放弃承保，员工无力承担免赔额。这是一个失败。如果我是总统，我会选择其他人，因为需要对更高的医疗费用、更多的麻疹死亡、失去消除状态以及加工食品没有进展负责。
玛格丽特·布伦南：因此，包括参议员艾尔索布鲁克斯和沃诺克在内的许多民主党人都表示，罗伯特·肯尼迪必须辞职或被解雇。其中一位即将上任的参议员，来自南卡罗来纳州的安妮·安德鲁斯博士，她实际上是以弹劾罗伯特·肯尼迪为竞选纲领的。当我过去问过你这种可能性时，你告诉我你没有看到可弹劾的罪行。现在还是这样吗？

森。卡西迪：嗯，这取决于总统。这最终是总统的遗产。弹劾。至于弹劾，你知道，我想你可以通过火腿三明治进行弹劾，所以他们必须决定对此采取什么行动。但我确实认为更重要的是总统的决定。总统可能希望留下更高的医疗保健费用、失去消除麻疹的地位以及在解决超加工食品和其他问题上没有进展等问题。如果是这样，那将玷污总统的遗产。如果总统真正想要一些积极的东西，他应该做出改变。这只是政治上的说法。美国选民在中期选举时表示，他们不喜欢现状，尤其是在医疗保健领域，我认为是时候采取一些不同的措施了。

玛格丽特·布伦南：因此，共和党人正在竞相在民主党一月份上任之前确认提名人，本周三将对总统提名的 FDA 专员海蒂·奥弗顿博士的提名进行投票。您之前曾说过，她在制定特朗普政府儿童疫苗政策方面的作用几乎是不合格的。参议员柯林斯对 FDA 对调味电子烟和尼古丁的授权表示担忧。参议员穆尔科斯基担心科学审查和 FDA 批准的堕胎药物米非司酮面临政治压力。鉴于这一切，您仍然期望奥弗顿博士会得到您的委员会的批准吗？

title_en: Cassidy slams RFK Jr. for "series of failures" as HHS secretary
title_zh: 卡西迪抨击小罗伯特·肯尼迪作为卫生与公众服务部部长的“一系列失败”
summary: GOP Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana railed against Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for what he called a "series of failures" at the helm of the Department of Health and Human Services.
summary_zh: 路易斯安那州共和党参议员比尔·卡西迪指责小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪在领导卫生部时遭遇了“一系列失败”
body_en: Sen. Bill Cassidy slams RFK Jr. for "series of failures" as Health Secretary - CBS News
Washington — GOP Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana on Sunday railed against Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for what he called a "series of failures" at the helm of the Department of Health and Human Services.

"This has been a failure. If I were president, I would choose someone else because there needs to be accountability for higher health care costs, more measles deaths, losing elimination status, and no progress on processed foods," Cassidy said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan ."

Cassidy, a medical doctor who's leaving the Senate early next year after losing his reelection bid, has been locked in a bitter disagreement with the HHS secretary for months over his vaccine policy and other stances. Kennedy's confirmation last year hinged on Cassidy's support, and the Louisiana Republican ultimately backed the nomination after receiving what he called "serious commitments" from the administration. But the "collaborative working relationship" that Cassidy said he was promised has not appeared to pan out.

Last week, Kennedy suggested that Republicans had been holding back his Make America Healthy Again Agenda. And with the Senate GOP set to lose the majority in the new year, he said Republicans would no longer have leverage over him, while also pointing to a "friend of our movement" in President Trump's new chief of staff , Stephen Miller.
"The Senate no longer has any leverage over me. And that's a big deal," Kennedy said on Nov. 9. "I don't think anything is going to get in our way now."
When asked about the comments, Cassidy said Kennedy is "obviously trying to provide cover for failure as Secretary of Health and Human Services."

"He was supposed to be doing something positive on ultra-processed foods — that's what MAHA moms wanted. There's been minimal progress, and now we've lost our measles elimination status, and we have infants dying from measles," Cassidy said. "So if you're a MAHA mom and you are hoping for something better — and hundreds of them contacted me during this debate about whether to support the secretary for HHS secretary, that's what they wanted — they have every right to be disappointed."
Cassidy questioned the logic that with Democrats in charge, things will be easier for Kennedy, saying, "There is no logic. This is about covering a series of failures."

Asked about the possibility of impeachment, which some Democrats have floated, Cassidy said, "You can impeach, I guess, over a ham sandwich, so they'll have to decide what to do on that." But Cassidy indicated that the attention should be on "the president's decision."

The Louisiana Republican argued that higher healthcare costs, losing measles elimination status, and seeing little progress on addressing ultra-processed foods, among other things, will "taint the president's legacy."

"If the president wants actually something positive, he should change," Cassidy said. "And that's just speaking politically. The American voters signaled at the midterm they don't like status quo, particularly in health care, and I think it's time for something different."

Cassidy also responded to the U.S. losing its measles elimination status, saying that for unvaccinated adults, "You could be the person that brings death to another," with implications for young children, pregnant women and immunocompromised individuals. He encouraged the president to speak out about how individuals can do as they wish, "but you can bring measles or some other disease into the health space of a child who's not old enough to be vaccinated," saying the message should be "pounded, pounded, pounded."

The comments come as the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions, which Cassidy helms, is set to vote on Heidi Overton's nomination for FDA commissioner this week. Asked whether he expects Overton's nomination to advance out of committee, Cassidy said he wasn't sure.

"I've been working the phones all week, both speaking with Dr. Overton, speaking with others. I still have questions, and so I cannot tell you the outcome of that vote right now," Cassidy said. "But I spoke to four or five of my down-dias Republican members, as well as continuing to discuss things with my advisers. So I can't tell you that answer yet."

title_en: Vulcan rocket fails in major setback for United Launch Alliance
title_zh: 火神火箭失败，联合发射联盟遭遇重大挫折
summary: The loss of its new Vulcan rocket was the first outright failure for United Launch Alliance, a major setback in the commercial launch industry.
summary_zh: 新型火神火箭的损失是联合发射联盟的第一次彻底失败，这是商业发射行业的重大挫折。
body_en: United Launch Alliance loses Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites in launch mishap - CBS News

In a major setback for United Launch Alliance , the company's new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites malfunctioned during the climb to space on Sunday, dooming the payload and throwing a costly wrench into both companies' launch schedules.

"Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 (at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station) suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a statement some 50 minutes after liftoff.
"We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action and return to flight as quickly as possible."
It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006.

It wasn't immediately known what went wrong, but the Vulcan, the rocket replacing ULA's fleet of Atlas 5 rockets, will face a potentially significant grounding while engineers review telemetry and implement fixes for whatever caused the mishap.

"There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01," Amazon Leo said in a post on X, using a designation meaning Leo Vulcan flight 1. "ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they'll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan."

It was only the fifth flight of a Vulcan rocket and the first in nine months as ULA and booster-supplier Northrop Grumman worked to resolve problems with nozzles used by strap-on solid-fuel boosters that marred two earlier flights.

The solids appeared to work normally Sunday, helping boost the rocket out of the dense lower atmosphere before burning out and falling away. The two methane-burning BE-4 engines powering the Vulcan's first stage then continued the climb toward orbit, but they appeared to fire longer than expected based on ULA's pre-launch timeline.

After stage separation, the Vulcan's hydrogen-fueled Centaur upper stage engines took over for a planned 12-minute and 15-second burn. According to ULA's update, something went wrong during that Centaur firing, but no additional details were immediately provided.

Sunday's launch was the first of 38 Vulcan flights purchased by Amazon to launch its Leo satellites, designed to compete head-to-head with Elon Musk's Starlink and other space-based internet providers. ULA has already launched eight Leo flights using Atlas 5 rockets.

Amazon has also booked 24 Leo launches aboard Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket , 24 aboard the European Ariane 6, and 13 aboard SpaceX's Falcon 9. More than 3,300 Leo satellites will be needed to complete the constellation. Sunday's flight would have pushed the total number launched to date to 436.

Instead, Amazon Leo will now have to wait on ULA's failure investigation to run its course before trying again with a Vulcan. The company also is waiting for Jeff Bezos-owned Blue Origin to get its New Glenn rocket flying again after a catastrophic on-pad explosion last May.

That failure was caused by a problem with an oxygen valve in one of New Glenn's seven BE-4 first-stage engines. The BE-4, also built by Blue Origin, powers the Vulcan's first stage, but the engines used Sunday had been retrofitted with a fix by Blue Origin engineers.

While the cause of the failure is not yet publicly known, "ULA is committed to full transparency with our customers, and they will have visibility into the investigation process, which utilizes rigorous methodology and corrective action," the company said.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman promised assistance if needed.

"Appreciate you quickly keeping the public and your partners informed," Isaacman wrote on the social media platform X. "The team at @NASA is available to assist in all matters related to the investigation and remediation effort. Artemis, Moon Base, and the nation need ULA. We are in your corner and here to help."

The 214-foot-tall Vulcan blasted off from pad 41 at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 12:40 p.m. ET, thundering away on a northeasterly trajectory atop 3.8 million pounds of thrust from six Northrop Grumman strap-on solid-fuel boosters and two methane-burning BE-4s.

A launch attempt Friday was scrubbed after problems knocked out a gaseous nitrogen plant that serves multiple launch providers. Another delay was ordered Saturday because of network problems between the Vulcan and ground systems.

On Sunday, launch controllers called a hold at the T-minus 20-second mark because of an unexplained technical issue with the rocket. Re-targeting the end of the launch window, ULA resolved the problem, and the rocket roared to life and climbed away at the end of the launch window.
body_zh: 联合发射联盟在发射事故中失去了火神火箭和 40 颗亚马逊 Leo 互联网卫星 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
联合发射联盟遭遇重大挫折，该公司搭载 40 颗亚马逊 Leo 互联网卫星的新型重型火神火箭在周日爬升太空时发生故障，导致有效载荷失效，并给两家公司的发射计划造成了代价高昂的影响。
ULA 在升空约 50 分钟后在一份声明中表示：“根据我们的发射总监收到的数据，我们确认从 41 号太空发射场（位于卡纳维拉尔角太空部队站）发射的火神运载火箭在飞行 10 分钟后出现异常，未能将亚马逊任务送入轨道。”
“我们将与客户和其他相关组织密切合作，找出原因，确定适当的纠正措施，并尽快恢复航班。”
这是波音公司和洛克希德·马丁公司于 2006 年成立联合发射联盟公司以来首次彻底失败的火箭。
目前尚不清楚到底出了什么问题，但取代 ULA Atlas 5 火箭队的火神号火箭将面临潜在的重大停飞，同时工程师将审查遥测数据并针对导致事故的原因实施修复。
亚马逊 Leo 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“任何发射都存在风险，对于 LV-01 这样的首次任务尤其如此。”“ULA 一直是亚马逊值得信赖的合作伙伴，我们相信他们会从这次任务中吸取教训，并实现 Vulcan 的长期计划。”
这只是火神火箭的第五次飞行，也是九个月来的第一次飞行，ULA 和助推器供应商诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司正在努力解决绑带式固体燃料助推器使用的喷嘴问题，这些问题曾困扰了之前的两次飞行。
周日，这些固体似乎正常工作，帮助火箭脱离稠密的低层大气，然后燃烧并坠落。为火神号第一级提供动力的两台燃烧甲烷的 BE-4 发动机随后继续向轨道爬升，但根据 ULA 的发射前时间表，它们的点火时间似乎比预期的要长。
级分离后，Vulcan 的半人马座上级氢燃料发动机接管了计划中的 12 分钟 15 秒的燃烧。根据 ULA 的最新消息，半人马发射期间出现了问题，但没有立即提供更多细节。
周日的发射是亚马逊购买的 38 架 Vulcan 航班中的第一架，用于发射其 Leo 卫星，旨在与埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 Starlink 和其他太空互联网提供商展开正面竞争。 ULA 已经使用 Atlas 5 火箭发射了八次 Leo 飞行。
亚马逊还预订了利用蓝色起源的新格伦火箭进行 24 次 Leo 发射、利用欧洲阿丽亚娜 6 号进行 24 次发射、利用 SpaceX 的猎鹰 9 号进行 13 次发射。完成该星座需要超过 3,300 颗 Leo 卫星。周日的飞行将使迄今为止发射的总数达到 436 架。
相反，亚马逊 Leo 现在必须等待 ULA 的失败调查结束，然后才能再次尝试使用 Vulcan。该公司还在等待杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 旗下的蓝色起源公司 (Blue Origin) 的新格伦火箭 (New Glenn Rocket) 在去年 5 月发生灾难性的发射台爆炸后再次升空。
这次故障是由新格伦号的七个 BE-4 第一级发动机之一的氧气阀问题引起的。同样由 ​​Blue Origin 制造的 BE-4 为 Vulcan 的第一级提供动力，但周日使用的发动机已经由 Blue Origin 工程师进行了改装和修复。
该公司表示，虽然失败的原因尚未公开，但“ULA 致力于对客户完全透明，他们将了解调查过程，该过程采用严格的方法和纠正措施。”
美国宇航局局长贾里德·艾萨克曼承诺在需要时提供援助。
艾萨克曼在社交媒体平台 X 上写道：“感谢您迅速向公众和您的合作伙伴通报情况。@NASA 的团队可以协助处理与调查和补救工作相关的所有事务。阿耳忒弥斯、月球基地和国家都需要 ULA。我们站在您这边，随时为您提供帮助。”
214 英尺高的火神号于中午 12 点 40 分从卡纳维拉尔角太空部队站的 41 号发射台发射升空。东部时间，在六台诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司捆绑式固体燃料助推器和两架燃烧甲烷的 BE-4 发动机的 380 万磅推力的推动下，沿着东北轨道轰鸣而去。
周五的一次发射尝试因问题而被取消，该工厂为多家发射提供商提供服务。由于火神号和地面系统之间的网络问题，周六又下令推迟一次。
周日，由于火箭出现无法解释的技术问题，发射控制人员要求在 T-20 秒处暂停。重新瞄准发射窗口结束时，ULA 解决了问题，火箭轰鸣着并在发射窗口结束时爬升离开。

body_en: Congress wants to tighten rules on exporting AI chips to China after Nvidia spy scandal | The Verge
Following revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy Congress wants to crack down.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. What happens next?
Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress . Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.

Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act , first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters . Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

body_en: FRIENDS WITH (SNAP) BENEFITS: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled the latest perk of his chummy relationship with President Donald Trump, announcing a deal today that will give stores across the country more time to comply with changes to federal food assistance rules.
New rules from the Department of Agriculture, which took effect last week, required retailers to stock a greater diversity of products in order to continue receiving SNAP benefits.

Just before they kicked in, Mamdani signed onto a bipartisan letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins urging the Trump administration to delay implementing the new requirements. He warned the rules would threaten the viability of the city’s more than 10,000 bodegas and corner stores, as well as the New Yorkers who rely on them, if the stores could not meet the mandates in time and lost the ability to accept SNAP payments.

Now, after negotiations with Rollins and foe-turned-bro Trump, Mamdani secured a 90-day extension for small retailers to comply with the rules — not just in New York City, but nationwide. The extension starts Friday.
Mamdani said he personally escalated the extension request to President Trump after City Hall reached out to the federal government.

“What I told the president was that this is a rule that, if allowed to be implemented on the timeline as it was scheduled, would be one that would throw the lives of so many working New Yorkers into a real place of anxiety and chaos,” he said. “And the president took that concern seriously.”
Mamdani declined to share how often he chats with Trump — “I’ll keep the cadence of that between the two of us,” he said — but he emphasized their conversations are ongoing.
As the two executives approach the one-year anniversary of their unexpected bromance, today’s announcement serves as a reminder that Mamdani’s Trump strategy has largely paid off.

After a seemingly love-struck Trump emerged from the duo’s first Oval Office meeting on Nov. 21, the threat of an immigration enforcement surge on par with Minneapolis largely evaporated, eliminating a potentially explosive situation that at the time loomed over the mayor’s early days in office.

In February, Mamdani successfully petitioned Trump to release a Columbia University student who had been taken into the custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and, as POLITICO reported this week , Mamdani has continued to make those requests privately to the president. The two have also discussed the federal government’s involvement in a massive development project that would span the Sunnyside Yard rail depot in Queens.
The price for these spoils has so far been one Mamdani’s base is willing to accept.

The mayor rarely, if ever, criticizes Trump directly. He demurs when asked by reporters about their private phone calls. And during a joint appearance outside Gracie Mansion in late September, when asked about Trump’s short-lived White House media ban, Mamdani only said that he himself supported having a variety of news outlets covering City Hall. — Molly Reinmann and Joe Anuta
NVIDIA AND BEYOND: Gov. Kathy Hochul isn’t worried that the scandal engulfing former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will impact the broader semiconductor sector.

“It’s a resilient industry,” she said today. “We’ve already planted the flag in places from Malta and all the way to Syracuse. New York’s economy will continue to be sound and continue to grow. This will not have an effect on meeting our obligations to continue the investments and create more jobs.”

New York has placed a massive, long-term bet on the industry, which has toeholds in the Syracuse area and the Saratoga County town of Malta, where Hochul appeared today to tout the groundbreaking of a new chip manufacturing facility.
Huang resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including a relationship with a woman who may be a potential Chinese spy .
The tech boom has helped lift Wall Street and swell New York’s coffers. A slowdown may spell trouble for the economy. — Nick Reisman
LEADERSHIP MOVES: State Sen. Liz Krueger told Playbook today she isn’t angling to chair the body’s housing committee.
“I’m not going to be the housing chair and I’m not lobbying to be the housing chair,” the Manhattan lawmaker said. “Several other people have voiced active interest and I think that’s great.”

“I actually think that whoever is willing to be the housing chair should recognize they need to probably make a six-year commitment to this assignment,” she added. “And I’m not actually planning necessarily to make an additional six-year commitment to the Senate.”
body_zh: 享有（临时）福利的朋友：纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼（Zohran Mamdani）公布了他与唐纳德·特朗普总统的亲密关系的最新福利，并于今天宣布了一项协议，该协议将给全国各地的商店更多时间来遵守联邦食品援助规则的变化。
农业部上周生效的新规定要求零售商储存更多种类的产品，以便继续获得 SNAP 福利。
就在他们开始实施之前，马姆达尼签署了一封两党致美国农业部部长布鲁克·罗林斯的信，敦促特朗普政府推迟实施新​​要求。他警告说，如果这些商店不能及时满足要求并失去接受 SNAP 付款的能力，这些规定将威胁到该市 10,000 多家酒窖和街角商店以及依赖它们的纽约人的生存能力。
现在，在与罗林斯和曾是敌人的兄弟特朗普谈判后，马姆达尼为小型零售商争取了 90 天的延期，以遵守这些规定——不仅是在纽约市，而且是在全国范围内。延期从周五开始。
马姆达尼表示，在市政厅与联邦政府联系后，他亲自向特朗普总统提出了延期请求。
他说：“我告诉总统的是，这项规定如果允许按计划的时间表实施，将会使众多纽约工薪阶层的生活陷入真正的焦虑和混乱。” “总统认真对待了这一担忧。”
马姆达尼拒绝透露他与特朗普聊天的频率——“我会保持我们两人之间的聊天节奏，”他说——但他强调他们的对话正在进行中。
在两位高管即将迎来他们意外的兄弟情谊一周年之际，今天的声明提醒人们，马姆达尼的特朗普战略已基本获得回报。
11 月 21 日，在两人首次椭圆形办公室会面后，看似陷入爱情的特朗普出现后，与明尼阿波利斯市相当的移民执法激增的威胁基本上消失了，消除了当时笼罩在市长上任初期的潜在爆炸性局势。
今年二月，马姆达尼成功请求特朗普释放一名被美国移民和海关执法局拘留的哥伦比亚大学学生，正如《政治》杂志本周报道的那样，马姆达尼继续私下向总统提出这些请求。两人还讨论了联邦政府参与一项横跨皇后区 Sunnyside Yard 火车站的大型开发项目。
到目前为止，这些战利品的价格是马姆达尼的基地愿意接受的价格。
市长很少（如果有的话）直接批评特朗普。当记者询问他们的私人电话时，他表示反对。 9月底，在格雷西大厦外联合露面时，当被问及特朗普短暂的白宫媒体禁令时，马姆达尼仅表示，他本人支持各种新闻媒体报道市政厅。 — 莫莉·莱因曼和乔·阿努塔
NVIDIA 及其他领域：州长 Kathy Hochul 并不担心 Nvidia 前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的丑闻会影响更广泛的半导体行业。
“这是一个有弹性的行业，”她今天表示。 “我们已经在从马耳他一直到锡拉丘兹的地方插上了旗帜。纽约的经济将继续健康并继续增长。这不会影响我们履行继续投资和创造更多就业机会的义务。”
纽约对该行业下了巨大的长期赌注，该行业在锡拉丘兹地区和马耳他萨拉托加县小镇立足，霍赫尔今天在当地宣传了新芯片制造工厂的破土动工。
黄因多项婚外情指控而辞职，其中包括与一名可能是潜在中国间谍的女性的关系。
科技繁荣帮助提振了华尔街并增加了纽约的金库。经济放缓可能会给经济带来麻烦。 — 尼克·赖斯曼

title_en: Flaming Hydra’s new Kickstarter campaign rethinks e-book ownership and digital lending
title_zh: Flaming Hydra 的新 Kickstarter 活动重新思考电子书所有权和数字借贷
summary: A new Kickstarter campaign aims to usher in the “return of the human internet.”
summary_zh: 一项新的 Kickstarter 活动旨在引领“人类互联网的回归”。
body_en: Flaming Hydra’s new Kickstarter campaign rethinks e-book ownership and digital lending | TechCrunch
Here’s a big promise: A new Kickstarter campaign aims to usher in the “return of the human internet.”

That’s the tagline of a crowdfunding campaign for The Phoenix Project , an initiative from the online culture and commentary magazine Flaming Hydra . If you back The Phoenix Project, you’re supporting three things — a one-off print magazine designed to celebrate “the values and fun of the early internet,” a new e-book service for libraries, and a newsletter subscription/archiving program that’s also designed for libraries.

To Flaming Hydra’s lead editor Maria Bustillos, these disparate projects are “basically all one thing,” tied together by the goal of “protecting freedom of information” and fulfilling the “promise of the early internet, where you’re making information available to as many people as possible, while still protecting the right of artists and authors to make a living.”

Bustillos told me that these issues have been highlighted on Flaming Hydra itself, for example when Tal Levin wrote about finding countless AI-generated clones of his book on Amazon. By “creating an ecosystem that is based in people working together, who are offering their stuff in a context that is controlled and doesn’t allow” others to create and sell AI-generated clones, Bustillos said Flaming Hydra is “part of the human project.”

“AI is not this unstoppable force,” she added. “If people just set up publishing pipelines and networks and organizations that are dedicated to the human internet, people who want to read stuff can go to them, and it’s actually completely isolated from mechanistic interference.”
The Phoenix Project fits into this vision by making the work of human writers more accessible to libraries.

Back in 2020, Bustillos wrote about the e-book systems dominating libraries and schools. In one example, instead of just buying a book, a school had to pay $27 per student per year for continued access to copies of “The Diary of Anne Frank.”

This is symptomatic of a broader system that treats true ownership of e-books and other digital media as a thing of the past. Instead, we “license” these e-books from their publishers, and they can be altered or removed at any time.

“E-books are books,” Bustillos said. “They’re not some other thing. They are books, and people should be able to own them, and libraries should be able to own them, and media should be able to be owned. All digital media should be able to be owned.”
In her view, ownership boils down to a simple question: “If you are at the mercy of somebody who can shut the book off, you do not own it.”

So even beyond the question of ongoing payments, there have also been examples of e-books being altered or removed from readers’ devices long after their purchase. Bustillos acknowledged that for individual pieces of media, this distinction may not seem like a big deal, “but if it’s all the textbooks for everybody, if it’s all the books,” then it’s a real problem.

Flaming Hydra and The Phoenix Project seek to solve this by letting libraries truly purchase and own e-books. They can then lend those e-books to their patrons through a new, open source “library in a box” system called Lenny for Libraries .

The Phoenix Project is starting by offering five new e-books from Flaming Hydra writers, including collections of writing from The Awl, and of essays by Tom Scocca and Bustillos herself. That might sound like a relatively small start, but Bustillos said she’s talking to library consortiums and author groups, and the goal here is to “change the conversation” around e-books and digital archiving and lending. So The Phoenix Project could be paving the way for other initiatives that follow a similar model.

Flaming Hydra has been working on all this even before launching the Kickstarter, and Bustillos said she was grateful for the financial support from backers like Anand Raganathan, Brewster Kahle, and Paul Ford. But by turning to crowdfunding, Bustillos said Flaming Hydra can better protect the work, ensuring that it remains sustainable and independent.
“We don’t have to be at the mercy of anybody, and it also protects editorial independence,” she said. “Those things go hand in hand.”
Flaming Hydra seeks to raise $30,000 for The Phoenix Project , with the campaign ending on November 27.

body_zh: Flaming Hydra 的新 Kickstarter 活动重新思考电子书所有权和数字借贷 | TechCrunch
这是一个巨大的承诺：一项新的 Kickstarter 活动旨在迎来“人类互联网的回归”。
这是凤凰计划众筹活动的口号，该活动由在线文化和评论杂志 Flaming Hydra 发起。如果您支持凤凰计划，那么您就支持三件事：一本旨在庆祝“早期互联网的价值和乐趣”的一次性印刷杂志、一项为图书馆提供的新电子书服务，以及一个同样为图书馆设计的时事通讯订阅/存档计划。
在《Flaming Hydra》的主编 Maria Bustilos 看来，这些不同的项目“基本上都是一件事”，它们的目标是“保护信息自由”，并实现“早期互联网的承诺，即向尽可能多的人提供信息，同时仍然保护艺术家和作家谋生的权利。”
Bustilos 告诉我，这些问题在《Flaming Hydra》本身上就得到了强调，例如，当塔尔·莱文 (Tal Levin) 写到在亚马逊上发现了无数人工智能生成的他的书的克隆时。布斯蒂洛斯表示，通过“创建一个基于人们共同工作的生态系统，他们在受控的环境中提供自己的东西，并且不允许”其他人创建和销售人工智能生成的克隆，Flaming Hydra 是“人类项目的一部分”。
“人工智能并不是一种不可阻挡的力量，”她补充道。 “如果人们只是建立了专门用于人类互联网的发布管道、网络和组织，那么想要阅读内容的人就可以去找它们，而且实际上完全不受机械干扰。”
凤凰计划通过让图书馆更容易获取人类作家的作品来实现这一愿景。
早在 2020 年，Bustillos 就撰写了有关电子书系统主导图书馆和学校的文章。举个例子，学校不仅要购买一本书，还必须为每个学生每年支付 27 美元才能继续获得《安妮·弗兰克日记》的副本。
这是一个更广泛的系统的症状，该系统将电子书和其他数字媒体的真正所有权视为过去。相反，我们从出版商处“许可”这些电子书，并且可以随时更改或删除它们。
“电子书就是书，”布斯蒂洛斯说。 “它们不是其他东西。它们是书籍，人们应该能够拥有它们，图书馆应该能够拥有它们，媒体应该能够拥有。所有数字媒体都应该能够拥有。”
在她看来，所有权归结为一个简单的问题：“如果你受到可以关闭这本书的人的摆布，那么你就不拥有它。”
因此，除了持续付款的问题之外，还存在电子书在购买后很久就被更改或从读者的设备中删除的例子。布斯蒂洛斯承认，对于个别媒体来说，这种区别可能看起来没什么大不了的，“但如果它是所有人的教科书，如果它是所有书籍，”那么这是一个真正的问题。
Flaming Hydra 和 Phoenix Project 试图通过让图书馆真正购买和拥有电子书来解决这个问题。然后，他们可以通过一个名为 Lenny for Libraries 的新开源“盒子里的图书馆”系统将这些电子书借给他们的顾客。
凤凰计划首先提供由《火焰九头蛇》作家创作的五本新电子书，其中包括《锥子》的文集，以及汤姆·斯科卡和布斯蒂洛斯本人的散文集。这听起来可能是一个相对较小的开始，但布斯蒂洛斯表示，她正在与图书馆联盟和作者团体交谈，目标是“改变围绕电子书、数字存档和借阅的对话”。因此，凤凰计划可能为遵循类似模式的其他举措铺平道路。
Flaming Hydra 甚至在启动 Kickstarter 之前就一直在致力于这一切，Bustillos 表示，她感谢 Anand Raganathan、Brewster Kahle 和 Paul Ford 等支持者的财政支持。但布斯蒂洛斯表示，通过众筹，Flaming Hydra 可以更好地保护这项工作，确保其保持可持续性和独立性。
“我们不必受到任何人的摆布，这也保护了编辑的独立性，”她说。 “这些事情是齐头并进的。”
Flaming Hydra 寻求为凤凰计划筹集 30,000 美元，该活动将于 11 月 27 日结束。
当您通过我们文章中的链接购买时，我们可能会赚取少量佣金。这并不影响我们的编辑独立性。
Anthony Ha 是 TechCrunch 的周末编辑。此前，他曾担任 Adweek 的科技记者、VentureBeat 的高级编辑、Hollister Free Lance 的地方政府记者以及一家风险投资公司的内容副总裁。他住在纽约市。

title_en: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
title_zh: 新奥尔良港起诉参与密西西比事故的油轮船东
summary: Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.
summary_zh: 官员们正在向上周撞上游轮的油轮船东寻求至少 100 万美元的损失。该事件被称为“米拉事件”
body_en: New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash Officials are seeking at least $1 million in damages from the owners of the tanker that hit a cruise ship last week. The incident was dubbed "the miracle on the Mississippi" after no one was killed.

The American Heritage river cruise paddleboat is seen on its side after being struck by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker ship in the Mississippi River, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, in New Orleans. Gerald Herbert/AP hide caption
New Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit against the owner and operator of the tanker that crashed into a docked cruise ship in the Mississippi River on Friday.

The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans is seeking at least $1 million in damages from people connected to the tanker, which is called Atlantic Asphalt. The lawsuit also names the tanker's owner, Nave Shipping SA and its management company Thome Ship Management as defendants.

The lawsuit states that at 12:30 p.m. Friday, the Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashed into the American Heritage river cruise paddleboat which was docked at the Thalia Street terminal for disembarkment of passengers.
Over 30 injured, no fatalities after tanker strikes cruise ship in New Orleans

There were almost 200 people on board the American Heritage at the time of the crash, which left the ship on its side and partially submerged. All passengers and crew survived, including more than 100 who were rescued from the river, leading New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno to dub the incident "the miracle on the Mississippi."
There were 32 people brought to the hospital, none with critical injuries.
The port commissioners said as a result of the collision, the Thalia Street terminal had significant damage.

"The extent of said damage remains under investigation, but physical damage is currently estimated to exceed [$1 million], with additional substantial direct, indirect and consequential damages anticipated," the lawsuit reads.
The lawsuit also states that the port expects to incur additional costs, including clean-up, surveys, repair, replacement and salvage costs.
On Friday, port officials requested the tanker be seized and sold to cover costs of the damage. A federal judge approved the seizure request.
Officials claimed that the collision occurred "as a result of the negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness" by Atlantic Asphalt, Nave Shipping SA and Thome Ship Management.
As of Saturday, eight people remained in the hospital, two in serious condition.
Mayor Moreno said Saturday that the Atlantic Asphalt had been towed away from the site, but noted it could take weeks to fully remove the American Heritage.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said that operations were now focused on fully reopening the river and safe removal of hazardous material on board the American Heritage. Burnham said it is estimated there are 160,000 gallons of fuel on board the ship.

"We're going to have divers in the water so they can do a full assessment on what's the right path to be able to remove it," Burnham said. "We also have teams that have been deployed throughout the entire area, the river system to monitor the area for any pollution."
body_zh: 新奥尔良港起诉密西西比州撞船事故中的油轮船东 官员正在向上周撞上游轮的油轮船东寻求至少 100 万美元的赔偿。由于没有造成人员伤亡，这一事件被称为“密西西比河奇迹”。
2026 年 11 月 13 日星期五，新奥尔良，美国传统河游明轮船在密西西比河上被大西洋沥青油轮撞倒。杰拉尔德·赫伯特/美联社隐藏标题栏
新奥尔良港口官员对周五在密西西比河撞上一艘停靠的游轮的油轮的所有者和经营者提起诉讼。
新奥尔良港委员会正在向这艘名为“大西洋沥青”的油轮相关人员寻求至少 100 万美元的损失赔偿。该诉讼还将油轮船东 Nave Shipping SA 及其管理公司 Thome Ship Management 列为被告。
诉讼称，中午 12:30周五，大西洋沥青油轮撞上了美国传统河游轮明轮船，该船停靠在塔利亚街码头供乘客下船。
新奥尔良油轮撞上游轮 造成30多人受伤，无人死亡
事故发生时，American Heritage 号上有近 200 人，导致船侧翻并部分淹没。所有乘客和船员均生还，其中包括从河中获救的 100 多人，新奥尔良市长海伦娜·莫雷诺 (Helena Moreno) 将此事件称为“密西西比河上的奇迹”。
共有 32 人被送往医院，没有人伤势严重。
港口专员表示，碰撞事件导致塔利亚街码头遭受严重损坏。
诉讼称：“上述损害的程度仍在调查中，但目前估计有形损害超过[100万美元]，预计还会造成额外的大量直接、间接和后果性损害。”
该诉讼还指出，港口预计将产生额外费用，包括清理、调查、维修、更换和打捞费用。
周五，港口官员要求扣押并出售这艘油轮，以弥补损失费用。联邦法官批准了扣押请求。
官员们声称，此次碰撞是由于大西洋沥青公司、Nave Shipping SA 和 Thome 船舶管理公司“疏忽、重大过失、过失或粗心造成的”。
截至周六，仍有八人留在医院，其中两人伤势严重。
莫雷诺市长周六表示，大西洋沥青已被拖离现场，但他指出，完全清除美国遗产可能需要数周时间。
海岸警卫队上尉梅兰妮·伯纳姆 (Melanie Burnham) 表示，目前行动的重点是完全重新开放河流以及安全清除“美国遗产”号上的危险物质。伯纳姆表示，估计船上有 160,000 加仑的燃料。
伯纳姆说：“我们将让潜水员进入水中，这样他们就可以对清除它的正确路径进行全面评估。” “我们还在整个地区和河流系统部署了团队，以监测该地区是否有任何污染。”

title_en: Trump blasts judge's 2-week halt to his Washington golf project and says administration will appeal
title_zh: 特朗普谴责法官暂停其华盛顿高尔夫项目两周，并表示政府将上诉
summary: "It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court," said Trump, who spent much of the weekend posting photos on his social media site of the golf course.
summary_zh: “它处于年久失修的可怕状态，任何人只要看看现在在全国各地流传的照片就可以看出这一点。
body_en: Seung Min Kim, Associated Press Seung Min Kim, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-blasts-judges-2-week-halt-to-his-washington-golf-project-and-says-administration-will-appeal

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump on Sunday decried a "highly destructive and political decision" from a federal judge after she ordered a two-week delay on renovations at a historic Washington public golf course that he has been trying to redevelop into a championship-level venue.

In a social media post, Trump said his administration will "immediately appeal, on an expedited basis" the temporary restraining order from U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes, which she issued just before East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months.

"It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court," said Trump, who spent much of the weekend posting photos on his social media site of the golf course. "They don't call it Trash Island for no reason!"

Trump had announced work on the site along the Potomac River would begin that day despite the legal challenge initiated against the project in February by the DC Preservation League and two local golfers.

The plaintiffs argue that the president's plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something Trump has denied. They had sought the stop-work order, saying that closing the course and launching work on the project would "irreparably injure plaintiffs and the public interest."

The president's public announcements on social media last month outlining the date of the closure of East Potomac Park and linking it to the renovation of the golf course weighed heavily in the judge's decision.

Reyes, in her ruling Saturday, noted that those posts presented a problem for the government, indicating that Trump's redevelopment plan was final and that the National Park Service "will close the Park to implement it."
Both points, she wrote, "favor granting Plaintiffs' motion for another temporary restraining order."

The order is in effect through Nov. 28. The park's redevelopment is one of multiple projects in the nation's capital that Trump has championed to remake the city. They include a large memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, among others.

Reyes' order was the latest in a series of rulings in lawsuits challenging Trump's projects that were issued just hours before construction was expected to begin. A different judge recently ordered a 14-day delay on work for the arch, a decision that came shortly after a key planning commission stacked with Trump appointees approved plans for the project.

body_zh: 金承敏 (Seung Min Kim)，美联社 金承敏 (Seung Min Kim)，美联社
华盛顿（美联社）——周日，唐纳德·特朗普总统谴责一名联邦法官做出的“极具破坏性和政治性的决定”，此前她下令推迟两周对华盛顿一座历史悠久的公共高尔夫球场进行翻修，而特朗普一直试图将这座高尔夫球场改造成冠军级场馆。
特朗普在社交媒体帖子中表示，他的政府将“立即快速上诉”美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯的临时限制令，她是在东波托马克高尔夫球场周日关闭 15 个月之前发布的。
特朗普说：“它处于年久失修的可怕状态，任何人只要看看现在在全国各地和法庭上流传的照片就可以看出这一点。”周末的大部分时间他都在自己的社交媒体网站上发布高尔夫球场的照片。 “他们不会无缘无故地称它为垃圾岛！”
尽管华盛顿特区保护联盟和两名当地高尔夫球手在二月份对该项目提出了法律挑战，但特朗普仍宣布波托马克河沿岸工地的施工将于当天开始。
原告辩称，总统的计划将改变无障碍高尔夫球场的特征，使其变得难以负担，但特朗普否认了这一点。他们曾寻求停工令，称关闭路线并启动该项目将“对原告和公共利益造成不可挽回的损害”。
总统上个月在社交媒体上发布的公告概述了东波托马克公园的关闭日期，并将其与高尔夫球场的翻修联系起来，这对法官的决定产生了重大影响。
雷耶斯在周六的裁决中指出，这些帖子给政府带来了问题，表明特朗普的重建计划已经最终确定，国家公园管理局“将关闭公园以实施该计划”。
她写道，这两点“都赞成批准原告提出的另一项临时限制令动议”。
该命令的有效期至 11 月 28 日。该公园的重建是特朗普倡导的重建城市的多个项目之一。其中包括大型纪念拱门、白宫宴会厅和约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心等。
雷耶斯的命令是针对特朗普项目的一系列诉讼裁决中的最新一项，这些裁决是在预计施工开始前几个小时发布的。另一位法官最近下令拱门施工推迟 14 天，这一决定是在由特朗普任命的重要规划委员会批准该项目计划后不久做出的。

title_en: Trump's Justice Department faces a new era of scrutiny under a Democratic-led Congress
title_zh: 特朗普的司法部在民主党领导的国会下面临新时代的审查
summary: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress
summary_zh: 司法部作为白宫的延伸部分运行了近两年，不受共和党控制的国会的限制
body_en: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress
By ERIC TUCKER Associated Press and ALANNA DURKIN RICHER Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress as it pursued investigations into President Donald Trump's enemies, fired waves of career employees and defended administration stances that judges across the country repeatedly deemed legally dubious .

Now, sweeping Democratic gains in Congress have shifted the balance of power in Washington, teeing up an onslaught of expected investigations into those actions and others as well as scrutiny from the majority party that the current Justice Department had until now managed to skirt.
The department has, at least publicly, appeared unbowed by the altered landscape.

Attorney General Todd Blanche says the department will cooperate with Congress but has also insisted that “we will not back down” from the Republican president's agenda. Meanwhile, a top aide told prosecutors on a call to prepare to be on “wartime” footing and a U.S. attorney publicly warned a top Democrat about planned congressional investigations.

It sets the stage for a pugilistic dynamic as Democrats promise to join already-skeptical courts in reining in the Trump administration while a Justice Department depleted by the losses of thousands of career employees and the postelection departures of senior leaders pledges to push ahead with its agenda.

Even though Democrats hold the gavel, they’re short on foolproof ways to guarantee Republican cooperation. Lawsuits can take years, subpoenas can be arduous to enforce and criminal contempt referrals for noncompliance would be sent to the Trump administration Justice Department, where they will almost certainly not be acted on.
“It’s a standoff and I don’t know what the answer to that is yet,” said Stan Brand, a former general counsel for the House of Representatives. “I don’t know if the Congress knows.”

Nonetheless, Democrats are eager to highlight what they view as abuses of power, including a succession of investigations the department has launched into the president’s perceived adversaries, many of which have been rejected by grand juries, dismissed by judges or have otherwise stalled without apparent progress.

In just the eventful weeks leading up to the election, the department unsuccessfully sought an indictment against former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, accelerated an investigation into Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar, employed an unusual maneuver to file a fresh criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey and charged two ex-FBI officials in a complaint that was swiftly dismissed by a judge.
Political pressure from the White House is unlikely to wane given the promotion of Stephen Miller, a devoted Trump loyalist, to chief of staff.

And Justice Department leadership has suggested it won’t let Democrats’ threats of investigations deter its pursuit of the White House’s priorities, and may become even more aggressive in pressing the president’s causes.

“We will not back down. This will not slow us down. This will not stop us,” Blanche said in a Fox News interview Monday. “President Trump has two years remaining in this administration and you better believe that we’re going to use it effectively.”

In a call with U.S. attorneys across the country this week, a top Blanche aide, Aakash Singh, told prosecutors to prepare to be on “wartime” footing, and suggested more U.S. attorneys may be pushed out after a spate of postelection departures, according to people familiar with the call who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal department discussions.

The Justice Department said the “‘wartime’ reference had everything to do with public safety,” noting that some “newly elected state and local leaders are no longer interested in partnering with federal law enforcement.”

Any additional U.S. attorney departures would be on top of a string of significant departures in the days after the election, when the Senate-confirmed leaders of the department’s National Security, Civil and Civil Rights divisions all announced their resignations. The divisions will have temporary leaders but are unlikely to get Senate-confirmed ones in light of the Democratic majority.

“What that means for DOJ, potentially, is just a lot of inaction, with tough decisions not being made because typically those tough decisions are made by confirmed people at the top of the components,” said Greg Brower, a former U.S. attorney in Nevada during President George W. Bush’s administration who was later the FBI’s chief congressional affairs official.
body_zh: 司法部作为白宫的延伸部分运行了近两年，不受共和党控制的国会的限制
埃里克·塔克 (ERIC TUCKER) 美联社和阿兰娜·德金·里彻 (ALANNA DURKIN RICHER) 美联社报道
华盛顿——近两年来，司法部一直充当白宫的延伸，不受共和党控制的国会的限制，对唐纳德·特朗普总统的敌人进行调查，解雇了一批职业雇员，并为全国各地法官一再认为法律上可疑的政府立场辩护。
现在，民主党在国会的全面胜利已经改变了华盛顿的权力平衡，引发了对这些行动和其他行动的一系列预期调查，以及现任司法部迄今为止一直设法避开的多数党的审查。
至少在公开场合，该部门似乎并没有因环境的改变而屈服。
司法部长托德·布兰奇表示，该部门将与国会合作，但也坚称“我们不会在共和党总统的议程上退缩”。与此同时，一名高级助手在电话中告诉检察官准备进入“战时”状态，一名美国检察官公开警告一名民主党高级官员有关计划中的国会调查。
这为一场拳击运动奠定了基础，因为民主党人承诺加入本已持怀疑态度的法院来遏制特朗普政府，而司法部因数千名职业雇员的流失和高级领导人的离职而精疲力尽，承诺推进其议程。
尽管民主党握有木槌，但他们缺乏保证共和党合作的万无一失的方法。诉讼可能需要数年时间，传票可能很难执行，因不遵守规定而提出的藐视法庭刑事案件将被送往特朗普政府司法部，而司法部几乎肯定不会采取行动。
“这是一场僵局，我还不知道答案是什么，”众议院前总法律顾问斯坦·布兰德说。 “我不知道国会是否知道。”
尽管如此，民主党人仍急于强调他们认为的滥用权力行为，包括该部门对总统的所谓对手发起的一系列调查，其中许多调查被大陪审团拒绝，被法官驳回，或者因其他原因而停滞不前，没有明显进展。
在大选前的动荡几周内，该部门未能成功起诉前白宫助手卡西迪·哈钦森，加快了对民主党众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔的调查，采取了不寻常的策略对前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米提起新的刑事案件，并在一项指控中指控了两名前联邦调查局官员，但该指控很快被法官驳回。
鉴于特朗普的忠实拥护者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)晋升为幕僚长，来自白宫的政治压力不太可能减弱。
司法部领导层表示，不会让民主党的调查威胁阻止其对白宫优先事项的追求，并且可能会更加积极地推动总统的事业。
“我们不会退缩。这不会让我们放慢脚步。这不会阻止我们，”布兰奇周一在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示。 “特朗普总统在本届政府的任期还剩两年，你最好相信我们会有效地利用它。”
据知情人士透露，在本周与全国各地美国检察官的电话会议中，布兰奇的高级助手阿卡什·辛格告诉检察官，要做好“战时”准备，并建议更多的美国检察官在选举后一连串离职后可能会被解雇。
司法部表示，“‘战时’的提法与公共安全密切相关”，并指出一些“新当选的州和地方领导人不再有兴趣与联邦执法部门合作”。
任何额外的美国检察官离职都将是选举后几天内一系列重大离职事件的基础上，参议院确认的该部门国家安全、民权和民权部门的领导人均宣布辞职。这些部门将有临时领导人，但鉴于民主党占多数，不太可能获得参议院确认的领导人。
“这对司法部来说可能意味着大量无所作为，无法做出艰难的决定，因为这些艰难的决定通常是由已确认的高层人士做出的，”乔治·W·布什总统执政期间内华达州前联邦检察官、后来担任联邦调查局首席国会事务官员的格雷格·布劳尔说。

WASHINGTON (AP) — The government wants to be certain it determines the "root cause" of the problems that led to the grounding of planes across the United States before making broad fixes to air traffic control, the nation's transportation chief said Sunday. President Donald Trump broke his silence about the extraordinary disruption that snarled airline travel and raised troubling questions about how a system so integral to the country could be so vulnerable.

Officials are analyzing two routers installed in recent weeks at Federal Aviation Administration facilities in Arkansas and Texas, according to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who during appearances on five television news shows stepped up his push for Congress to provide billions more to upgrade a system he said had been neglected for decades.
He was the administration's public face in seeking to assure travelers that it was safe to fly as airports and airlines worked to restore normal operations after Friday's nationwide ground stop.
"We're going to figure out what was the root cause and then move forward from there," he said.

Trump had not commented publicly or on social media after the ground stop was ordered Friday afternoon. He had issued statements on social media about unrelated matters while frustrated passengers were left stranded and his team and airlines scrambled for a return to normal travel operations.

Trump weighed in Sunday morning in a post on Truth Social, saying that his administration has begun upgrading the air traffic control system, but that task should not be done in "drips and drabs." The Republican-controlled Congress approved $12.5 billion for the FAA as part of the party's sweeping tax cut package last year, but Duffy has characterized that money as a down payment on a broader overhaul of the aging system.

"If Congress approves the desperately needed money for Air Traffic Control, we can get it built quickly and efficiently," Trump wrote. "It will be the BEST SYSTEM anywhere in the World. Much of our current air control system is 50 years old - RIDICULOUS!"
In another post, he accused Democratic President Joe Biden's administration of making an "old and broken system worse than when they began."

Biden signed a massive infrastructure bill into law in the first year of his presidency, setting aside $25 billion for the FAA to improve airports and its traffic control towers, redevelop airport terminals and "upgrade the foundation" of the air traffic control system, according to the agency.
Duffy says upgrades ready to roll out 'tomorrow' if he gets the money

"I can't apologize for what was passed on to us. And I can't blame Republicans or Democrats, because it's all of them. It goes back, 20, 25, 30 years of a lack of investment," Duffy said in one of his interviews.

In a post on X, Duffy said contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. had secured routers from the two FAA sites and was conducting "deep diagnostics" on the equipment; other engineers were involved, too. He has said the problem began when the federal contractor was replacing a section of old copper wire with new fiber wire, somehow causing the system to overload.

After the wire was replaced at the site in El Dorado, Arkansas, and the router was turned on, a problem then cropped up at a facility in Amarillo, Texas, cascading into the ground stop. "We didn't think that should or would happen," he said.
Billions are needed, he said, to build a "brand new architecture" for the network, and he said companies including AT&T, Verizon and Lumen are ready to deploy it "tomorrow" if the money is there.

他是政府的公众形象，试图向旅客保证飞行是安全的，因为周五全国地面停留后，机场和航空公司正在努力恢复正常运营。

在阿肯色州埃尔多拉多的现场更换电线并打开路由器后，德克萨斯州阿马里洛的一家设施突然出现问题，并最终蔓延到地面站。 “我们认为这种情况不应该或不会发生，”他说。
他说，需要数十亿美元来为网络建立一个“全新的架构”，如果有钱的话，包括 AT&T、Verizon 和 Lumen 在内的公司已经准备好“明天”部署它。

summary: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued the temporary restraining order before the East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months.

WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House, blocking for now President Donald Trump's push to redevelop the site along the Potomac River into a championship-level venue.

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued the temporary restraining order before the East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months. Trump had announced work would begin that day despite the legal challenge initiated against the project in February by the DC Preservation League and two local golfers.

The plaintiffs argue that Trump's plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something the Republican president denies. They had sought the stop-work order, saying that closing the course and launching work on the project would "irreparably injure plaintiffs and the public interest."

The president's public announcements on social media last month outlining the date of the closure of East Potomac Park and linking it to the renovation of the golf course weighed heavily in the decision. Trump said on Oct. 26 that "We are closing the East Potomac Golf Course Site as scheduled on November 15th in order to renovate and rebuild for Competitive (with other such projects!), Safety, Modernization, and Aesthetic reasons." He added that the goal was to renovate and rebuild "a World Championship Public Facility."

Reyes in her ruling Saturday noted that Trump's posts presented a problem for the government. "They indicate that the Washington National Plan is final and that NPS will close the Park to implement it," she wrote. "Both points favor granting Plaintiffs' motion for another temporary restraining order."

Reyes said her order "ENJOINS the government from closing East Potomac Park and the East Potomac Golf Course during the daily hours in which they were open as of November 14, 2026. It does not order the Government to undertake any active management of either. Further, for the avoidance of any doubt, the Government remains free, as it has since the onset of this litigation, to conduct repairs on any part of the Park and Course with any notice required by the existing Preliminary Injunction."
The judge said the order is in effect "through November 28, 2026, or further order from the Court, whichever comes first."

The Justice Department said in a statement Saturday that the judge acknowledged that the National Park Service can limit access to its facilities where the public is at risk of harm. "Nothing in the Court's order precludes planning for the development of a world class golf course to continue," it said. "The Department of Justice will always vociferously defend the Trump Administration's agenda in court."

Catherine Carroll, a senior legal adviser at Democracy Forward, which is representing the plaintiffs, praised the ruling. "We are grateful that once again, a court has intervened to prevent irreparable harm caused by the Trump-Vance administration's pursuit of another one of the president's vanity projects," she said. "The administration's inexplicable drive to destroy East Potomac Park would have taken away a treasured park that could never be replaced."
WATCH: Judge orders ethics inquiry in D.C. golf course case

The park's redevelopment is one of multiple projects in the nation's capital that Trump has championed to remake the city. They include a large memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, among others.

Reyes had signaled throughout a five-hour court hearing Friday that she was likely to issue some stoppage for the park closure. The only issue was how expansive it might be. Justice Department lawyer Adam Gustafson argued that the entire East Potomac Park, which includes three golf courses, a miniature course, bike riding lanes and other recreational areas, was being closed because of safety factors. He also noted that the lease between the government and the current operator, National Links Trust, was ending Sunday.

Reyes pointed out that safety had not been part of the discussion over the closure for months and that ending the lease felt more like an action that provided a premise for the closure rather than an action that led to the closure of the course about 2 miles from the White House.

Even before the order, Trump lashed out in a social media post Saturday, contending that Reyes "doesn't want us to quickly and inexpensively fix up the Course which is, also, very dangerous." He said people who live in the Washington area would get a 50% discount on "any and all Rates charged" and that the redevelopment would "evolve into something very special, something which the Judge will be able to take great pride in seeing!"

Reyes' order was the latest in a series of rulings in lawsuits challenging Trump's projects that were issued just hours before construction was expected to begin. A different judge recently ordered a 14-day delay on work for the arch, a decision that came shortly after a key planning commission stacked with Trump appointees approved plans for the project.

Reyes, who was nominated to the court by Democratic President Joe Biden, had for months been reticent about approving the plaintiffs' requests for work stoppages. The plaintiffs had argued the administration was moving ahead with work related to the project despite the pending lawsuit.

华盛顿（美联社）——周六，一名联邦法官下令将距离白宫不远的一座历史悠久的华盛顿公共高尔夫球场的任何工程推迟两周，暂时阻止了唐纳德·特朗普总统推动波托马克河沿岸的场地重新开发为锦标赛级场馆的努力。
美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 在东波托马克高尔夫球场 (East Potomac Golf Links) 于周日关闭 15 个月之前发布了临时限制令。尽管华盛顿特区保护联盟和两名当地高尔夫球手在二月份对该项目提出了法律挑战，但特朗普仍宣布工作将于当天开始。
原告辩称，特朗普的计划将改变无障碍高尔夫球场的特征，使其变得难以负担，但共和党总统否认了这一点。他们曾寻求停工令，称关闭路线并启动该项目将“对原告和公共利益造成不可挽回的损害”。
总统上个月在社交媒体上发布的公告概述了东波托马克公园的关闭日期，并将其与高尔夫球场的翻修联系起来，这对这一决定产生了重大影响。特朗普10月26日表示，“我们将按计划于11月15日关闭东波托马克高尔夫球场，以便出于竞争（以及其他此类项目！）、安全、现代化和美观的原因进行翻新和重建。”他补充说，目标是翻新和重建“世界锦标赛公共设施”。
雷耶斯在周六的裁决中指出，特朗普的帖子给政府带来了问题。她写道：“他们表示华盛顿国家计划已经最终确定，国家公园管理局将关闭公园以实施该计划。” “这两点都赞成批准原告提出的另一项临时限制令动议。”
雷耶斯表示，她的命令“命令政府在 2026 年 11 月 14 日起的每日开放时间内关闭东波托马克公园和东波托马克高尔夫球场。它并不命令政府对其中任何一个进行任何积极管理。此外，为了避免任何疑问，自本次诉讼开始以来，政府仍然可以自由地对公园和球场的任何部分进行维修，但须按照现有初步命令的要求发出通知。禁令。”
法官表示，该命令的有效期“截至 2026 年 11 月 28 日，或法院的进一步命令，以先到者为准”。
司法部在周六的一份声明中表示，法官承认国家公园管理局可以限制公众进入可能受到伤害的设施。声明称：“法院命令中的任何内容均不妨碍世界级高尔夫球场开发计划的继续进行。” “司法部将始终在法庭上大力捍卫特朗普政府的议程。”
原告的代表“民主前进”高级法律顾问凯瑟琳·卡罗尔对这一裁决表示赞赏。她说：“我们很感激法院再次介入，以防止特朗普-万斯政府追求总统的另一项虚荣项目而造成不可挽回的伤害。” “政府莫名其妙地摧毁了东波托马克公园，这将夺走一座永远无法替代的珍贵公园。”

该公园的重建是特朗普倡导的重塑这座城市的多个项目之一。其中包括大型纪念拱门、白宫宴会厅和约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心等。
雷耶斯在周五长达五个小时的法庭听证会上表示，她可能会下令停止公园关闭。唯一的问题是它的范围有多大。司法部律师亚当·古斯塔夫森辩称，整个东波托马克公园，包括三个高尔夫球场、一个微型球场、自行车道和其他休闲区，由于安全因素而被关闭。他还指出，政府与当前运营商国家链接信托公司之间的租约将于周日结束。
雷耶斯指出，几个月来，安全问题一直没有成为关于关闭球场的讨论的一部分，结束租约感觉更像是为关闭提供前提的行动，而不是导致距离白宫约 2 英里的球场关闭的行动。
甚至在该命令发布之前，特朗普就在周六的社交媒体帖子中猛烈抨击，称雷耶斯“不希望我们快速且廉价地修复球场，这也非常危险”。他表示，居住在华盛顿地区的人们将获得“任何及所有收费”50% 的折扣，并且重建将“演变成非常特别的东西，法官将能够看到这一点感到非常自豪！”
雷耶斯的命令是针对特朗普项目的一系列诉讼裁决中的最新一项，这些裁决是在预计施工开始前几个小时发布的。另一位法官最近下令拱门施工推迟 14 天，这一决定是在由特朗普任命的重要规划委员会批准该项目计划后不久做出的。
由民主党总统乔·拜登提名进入法院的雷耶斯几个月来一直不愿批准原告的停工请求。原告辩称，尽管诉讼悬而未决，但政府仍在继续推进与该项目相关的工作。
